maps.summary: MarkdownEditor.svelte owns one CodeMirror EditorView for the active note or code tab. EditorView.svelte:64-86 mounts it only while a tab is active and the tab is not a collection, canvas, kanban, tasks, tags, graph or calendar view, so each mount/unmount is a tab-kind change. The EditorState is created in onMount from store content (MarkdownEditor.svelte:99-145) and then lives for as long as the component stays mounted. Markdown-to-markdown tab switches reuse the same EditorView and replace its document in the tab-switch $effect (170-275). Keystrokes leave through EditorView.updateListener in setup/editor-extensions.ts:170-190 into editor.service.ts onContentChange (224-227), which writes tabs[activeIndex].content and arms the 2 s or 500 ms auto-save. External writers reach the view through syncExternalContentToEditor, which updates the store and bumps externalContentSignal; the content-sync $effect (311-337) then replaces the whole document from the store. editor-host.ts defines the EditorHost interface (resolveLink, listLinkCandidates, readNote, assetUrl, openLink, openExternal, createNote), NOOP_HOST, and the static editorHost facet that createExtensions installs once. tab-view-state.ts is a module-level Map of path to {scrollTop, scrollLeft, cursorPos}, saved on tab switch and on destroy and restored on mount, cleared by deleteTabViewState and clearAllTabViewStates. Left to decide: nothing in the component itself flushes pending saves on destroy or tab switch, which is safe only because the store is written synchronously on every keystroke. Not verified in a running app: every claim below is from reading code, plus one Node run (no file writes) of the same CodeMirror undo/replace sequence against the installed @codemirror/commands 6.11.1 and @codemirror/state 6.7.6. Noted but not reported (no data consequence or unverified reachability): (a) lastSeenSignal is per-instance but externalContentSignal is module-level, so on each remount with a non-zero counter the content-sync effect does one redundant full-document replace with the same text (MarkdownEditor.svelte:310-337), contrary to the comment at 307-309; (b) isTabSwitching and isExternalEdit are not reset in a finally, so an exception thrown synchronously out of dispatch would leave them true and suppress store updates; CodeMirror catches update-listener and plugin exceptions (view dist index.js:8101-8110, 1508-1540), so only a StateField throw could reach this, and I did not find one; (c) onDestroy writes view state under lastTabPath even when that tab was closed (147-165), leaving stale entries that are clamped on reuse.
maps.data_flow: Load: openFileInEditor (editor.service.ts:98-148) puts file text into the store tab.content and savedContent. Mount: onMount (MarkdownEditor.svelte:107-131) builds EditorState.create({doc: tab.content}) with createExtensions(...) (editor-extensions.ts:124-192), which installs history(), the EditorHost facet and the update listener. Keystroke out: transaction -> updateListener (editor-extensions.ts:170-190, skipped when isTabSwitching or isExternalEdit) -> onContentChange (editor.service.ts:224-227) -> editorStore.updateContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88, writes tabs[activeIndex]) -> debouncedSave 2000 ms / debouncedSaveFrontmatter 500 ms (editor.service.ts:196-221) -> saveDirtyTabs -> saveFileByPath -> writeTextFile (161-194). Tab switch in: effect sets isTabSwitching, dispatches a full-document replace from tab.content with addToHistory(false) (MarkdownEditor.svelte:227-237), then clears the flag. External in: syncExternalContentToEditor (editor.service.ts:70-91) -> store (updateTabContentByPath sets content and savedContent, or updateTabContentOnly) -> bump signal only if the path is active -> content-sync effect (311-337) replaces the doc from activeTab.content with addToHistory(false) and isExternalEdit set. Unmount: onDestroy (147-165) saves scroll and cursor to tab-view-state and calls view.destroy(); the store is already current, so no content is flushed. Right-click and Cmd/Ctrl-click: handleContextMenu and handleEditorClick (65-89, 144) only move the selection or call followWikilinkClick; they do not change the document.
invariants: The store is the only save source. saveFileByPath writes tab.content (editor.service.ts:161-178), so any writer that sets markSaved=true for a dirty tab discards the unsaved keystrokes that are in the store and in CodeMirror.

tabs[activeIndex] must be the tab whose document CodeMirror shows when onDocChanged fires. updateContent writes by index (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88). This holds only because the tab-switch effect runs before any input event (Svelte flushes effects as microtasks).
Store and CodeMirror agree on the active tab's text at every keystroke. The only two suppressed paths (isTabSwitching, isExternalEdit) replace the document from the store, so they do not diverge it.
Background tabs change only in the store (editor.service.ts:87-89 bumps the signal only for the active path). They reach CodeMirror on the next tab switch.

Undo history is per note. The code assumes it, but createExtensions installs one history() on a single EditorState that survives markdown-to-markdown tab switches (editor-extensions.ts:130; MarkdownEditor.svelte:227-237). This assumption is violated (finding 1).

Replace transactions must not create undo entries (addToHistory false), but they still map existing undo entries through the replacement (commands dist index.js:240-241 addMapping). Any replace-based sync therefore changes what undo does afterwards.
The rename branch (MarkdownEditor.svelte:179-194) skips the document replace only when CodeMirror's text already equals the new tab's stored content, so it cannot drop text.
isTabSwitching and isExternalEdit are true only inside their own dispatch calls.

maps.summary: EditorTabs.svelte is a presentational tab bar (no writes): it renders editorStore.tabs and calls switchTab / closeTab / togglePinTab from editor.service.ts. editor.store.svelte.ts holds module-level $state (tabs, activeIndex, pendingScrollPosition, isLivePreview, editorView, externalContentSignal) behind getters, plus mutators: addTab, setActiveIndex, removeTab, updateContent (writes the ACTIVE tab only), markSavedByPath, updateTabContentByPath / updateTabContentOnly (external writers), updateTabPath, togglePin / setPinned (via reorderTabsAfterPinChange), bumpExternalContentSignal, reset. editor.logic.ts holds pure helpers (dirty check, pin boundary and reorder, frontmatter position, lineStartToOffset, virtual-path constants). editor.types.ts is the EditorTab shape. The real write pipeline lives in editor.service.ts and MarkdownEditor.svelte, which I read to trace callers. Main findings: a canvas unmount flush writes into whichever tab is active at that moment, and several external writers replace a dirty tab's unsaved text with disk-derived content.
maps.data_flow: Keystroke: CodeMirror updateListener (setup/editor-extensions.ts:170-189, guarded by isTabSwitching and isExternalEdit) -> MarkdownEditor onDocChanged -> editor.service.ts onContentChange (224-227) -> store.updateContent (store:83-88) writes tabs[activeIndex].content -> scheduleAutoSave (213-221) arms 500 ms (frontmatter) or 2000 ms (body) debounce -> saveDirtyTabs (183-194) -> saveFileByPath (161-178): captures content, writeTextFile, markSavedByPath(path, content), notifyAfterSave. Tab switch: switchTab (250) sets activeIndex synchronously -> MarkdownEditor tab-switch $effect (MarkdownEditor.svelte:170-275) replaces the CM doc from tab.content under isTabSwitching. External writers (tasks toggle, link rename, deep-link append, frontmatter/properties, type rename, watcher reload): syncExternalContentToEditor (editor.service.ts:70-91) with markSaved=true (content and savedContent both set) or false (content only); it bumps externalContentSignal only when the path is the active tab; MarkdownEditor's content-sync effect (311-337) then dispatches a full doc replace under isExternalEdit. Canvas, Kanban and Collection views write back via onContentChange directly (EditorView.svelte:81 and the Kanban/Collection props), so their writes also land on activeIndex.
invariants: updateContent() writes to whichever tab is active at call time, so any writer that can fire after a tab switch or close (for example a component destroyed during the switch) corrupts the newly active tab. Only the CM keystroke path is safe, because the view is torn down with its tab.

isTabDirty = content !== savedContent. markSavedByPath stores the content that was written, not the current content, so edits typed during a write stay dirty. Writers that pass markSaved=true (updateTabContentByPath) assume disk equals the in-memory content; several callers (tasks toggle, deep-link append/prepend, daily-note append) break this by building the new text from disk instead of the tab.

Tab object identity is not stable: togglePin/setPinned replace the toggled tab with a spread copy ({...tab, pinned}). Callers that await must re-find the tab by path (saveFileByPath, closeTab, reloadExternallyChangedTabs do; renameType's for-of loop over the live array does not).
Pinned tabs are a contiguous prefix; reorderTabsAfterPinChange relies on getPinnedBoundary over that prefix.
addTab does not de-duplicate paths; callers must check findTabIndex first (openFileInEditor re-checks after its async read).
activeIndex is -1 exactly when tabs is empty after removeTab/reset; activeIndex is clamped on removeTab.
externalContentSignal bumps only for the active path; background tabs get their content through the tab-switch effect, which reads tab.content at switch time.
fileType is set only at open (editor.service.ts:135-140); updateTabPath does not recompute it, so a rename across kinds keeps the old view.
MarkdownEditor's rename detection assumes that when the old path is gone and the CM doc equals the active tab's content, the path changed rather than the tab switched.

Unverified assumptions: Svelte 5 unmounts the old {#if} branch (and runs its onDestroy) before the new branch mounts; and @tauri-apps/plugin-fs writeTextFile truncates and writes in place. I did not check either in node_modules.

maps.summary: editor.service.ts is the tab and save owner for the markdown editor. It holds the tab-close listener registry, openFileInEditor (disk read, then addTab), saveFileByPath (snapshot content, writeTextFile, markSavedByPath, notifyAfterSave), saveDirtyTabs with a 5 s retry, two debounced auto-save timers (500 ms frontmatter, 2000 ms body) armed by scheduleAutoSave, onContentChange (keystroke entry, writes the ACTIVE tab), saveAllDirtyTabs (close, vault switch, initializeVault), closeTab (dirty prompt), closeTabsForDeletedPath, reloadExternallyChangedTabs (watcher batch), and resetEditor. syncExternalContentToEditor is the single writer for external content into a tab, and bumps externalContentSignal only for the active tab. editor.hooks.ts is the after-save owner: markRecentSave for the watcher self-save skip, notifyAfterSave (applyNoteChange with source 'save', then notifyContentInvalidated, then observers), and resetHooks. open-note-at.service.ts opens a note via openFileInEditor and hands a caret offset to editorStore.pendingScrollPosition; it never writes content. Read-only audit: no tests, builds or git state changes were run. Descriptions of Svelte destroy ordering and Tauri window destroy are from reading code, not from running it.
maps.data_flow: Keystroke: CodeMirror updateListener (src/lib/core/markdown-editor/setup/editor-extensions.ts:171-188) -> onDocChanged -> onContentChange (editor.service.ts:224) -> editorStore.updateContent writes tabs[activeIndex].content (editor.store.svelte.ts:84) -> scheduleAutoSave arms a 2 s or 500 ms timer -> saveDirtyTabs (editor.service.ts:183) -> saveFileByPath (161): captures content, awaits writeTextFile (plugin-fs), markSavedByPath(path, snapshot) sets savedContent only, then notifyAfterSave (editor.hooks.ts:67): markRecentSave, applyNoteChange(save) (synchronous fan-out, no yield for the save row, note-change.service.ts:87 and 259), notifyContentInvalidated, observers. Canvas and collection and kanban views also call onContentChange (EditorView.svelte:79-83), so their emissions also land in tabs[activeIndex]. External writers (tasks.service.ts:114, deep-link.service.ts:262/281/298, deep-link-actions.ts:63, link-updater.service.ts:47, type-definitions.service.ts:220, properties.service.ts:95, frontmatter-write.service.ts:128/156) call syncExternalContentToEditor (editor.service.ts:70): updateTabContentByPath (content and savedContent, when markSaved) or updateTabContentOnly, plus scheduleAutoSave and a signal bump for the active tab only. Watcher batch (app-lifecycle.service.ts:486) calls reloadExternallyChangedTabs (editor.service.ts:375). Close handler, switchVault and initializeVault call saveAllDirtyTabs (editor.service.ts:234), which cancels both timers and then saves a snapshot of dirty tabs. resetEditor (editor.service.ts:412) cancels timers and resets the store. Deletes call closeTabsForDeletedPath (editor.service.ts:356) before the disk op.
invariants: savedContent is the last disk-synced snapshot; a tab is dirty iff content !== savedContent (editor.logic.ts isTabDirty). Only markSavedByPath, updateTabContentByPath, and syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true) change savedContent.

editorStore.updateContent and therefore onContentChange write only the ACTIVE tab (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88). onContentChange has no path parameter, so every producer must be the active tab at the moment it calls.

Every typed change reaches disk only through a timer armed in scheduleAutoSave (editor.service.ts:213-221) or through saveAllDirtyTabs. 'none' arms nothing. Anything that cancels timers (resetEditor at editor.service.ts:412, saveAllDirtyTabs at 235-236) must be followed by a save or a teardown that does not discard edits.

syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true) overwrites in-memory edits and does not check dirtiness. Callers must derive the content from the tab when the tab is dirty. link-updater.service.ts:30-38 and frontmatter-write.service.ts:95-116 do this. tasks.service.ts:102-114 and deep-link paths do not.
Tab-switch and external doc replaces are suppressed from the keystroke pipeline by isTabSwitching and isExternalEdit (MarkdownEditor.svelte:225-237 and 323-334; editor-extensions.ts:171).

closeTabsForDeletedPath must run before diskOp so the debounce cannot recreate the deleted file during the async gap (path-change.service.ts:124-127). It drops dirty tabs without a check, which is the intended behaviour only when the delete succeeds.

The 'save' row of SOURCE_POLICY has no yield before consumers (note-change.service.ts:87, 259-260), so the per-file index fan-out finishes before notifyContentInvalidated runs (editor.hooks.ts:81-83). Verified by reading.

markRecentSave runs after writeTextFile resolves (editor.service.ts:169-170 via notifyAfterSave). This relies on the Rust watcher debounce (500 ms, per CLAUDE.md) being longer than the time between the write and the mark. I did not verify the watcher constant in src-tauri.

Tab-close listeners and after-save observers are called synchronously in registration order; a listener that unregisters itself during iteration would skip the next listener (editor.hooks.ts:85, editor.service.ts:38). Not observed in the code I read.

maps.summary: Shell and editor wiring. src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte registers global keybindings, Tauri listeners, a close handler and the vault init/teardown effect (initializeVault or teardownVault on vaultStore.isOpen/path). It also runs three debounced effects on the active tab: a 150 ms backlinks/outgoing refresh, a 1 s per-file index update (updateIndexesForFile, source 'edit'), and a 200 ms search. AppShell.svelte renders the rail, note list, EditorView, right sidebar and status bar, and the dock badge. EditorView.svelte picks the view by tab fileType (tasks, tags, graph, calendar, kanban, canvas, collection, or MarkdownEditor) and passes onContentChange as the write-back callback for kanban, canvas and collection. editor-host.ts is the single EditorHost (link resolution, openLink, createNote with traversal guard, readNote, fenced renderers). MarkdownEditor.svelte owns the CodeMirror view: doc changes flow through the updateListener into onContentChange, and tab switches, external syncs and source-mode mounts are guarded by isTabSwitching / isExternalEdit. The main defect class is that onContentChange has no path argument and always writes to the active tab (editor.store updateContent uses activeIndex), so any view that emits after it stops being active corrupts a different note.
maps.data_flow: Keystroke: CodeMirror updateListener (setup/editor-extensions.ts:170-190) -> onDocChanged(full doc string) -> onContentChange (editor.service.ts:224) -> editorStore.updateContent writes tabs[activeIndex].content (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-87) and arms the 500 ms (frontmatter) or 2000 ms (body) autosave. Save: saveDirtyTabs -> saveFileByPath writes tab.content, then markSavedByPath and notifyAfterSave (editor.service.ts:161-180). Index: layout content effect (+layout.svelte:137-157) -> updateIndexesForFile -> applyNoteChange('edit') after 1 s idle. Board views (kanban, canvas, collection) emit whole-file strings through EditorView.svelte:79-83 into the same onContentChange; canvas emits from a 300 ms debounce and from onDestroy (CanvasInner.svelte:211-234). External writes: syncExternalContentToEditor bumps externalContentSignal, which MarkdownEditor's content-sync effect turns into a full doc replace with isExternalEdit set (MarkdownEditor.svelte:311-337). Watcher reload: reloadExternallyChangedTabs (editor.service.ts:375-405). Vault switch: switchVault saves dirty tabs, drains writes, then vaultStore.open (vault.service.ts:19-21); the layout effect calls initializeVault, which saves again, drains calendar writes, then teardownVault -> resetEditor empties tabs (app-lifecycle.service.ts:180-188, 622). Window close: registerCloseHandler saves, prompts on failures, drains, then destroys the window (tauri-listeners.service.ts:53-71).
invariants: onContentChange(content) has no path and writes to the ACTIVE tab (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-87). Every caller must run while its own tab is active. CanvasInner onDestroy breaks this, see finding 1.

Every user keystroke reaches the store synchronously through the updateListener, because only programmatic replaces are suppressed (isTabSwitching at MarkdownEditor.svelte:227-237, isExternalEdit at 328-334). Any path that changes the CM doc without going through onDocChanged leaves tab.content stale.

resetEditor() empties tabs and cancels both autosave timers without saving (editor.service.ts:412-416). Every vault teardown therefore needs saveAllDirtyTabs() to have succeeded first. Nothing enforces that: switchVault and initializeVault ignore saveAllDirtyTabs' failed-path result.
A tab with content === savedContent is not dirty, so closeTab removes it without a prompt. Any pending widget write that has not reached the store yet (canvas debounce) is silently dropped on close.
Active-tab identity is by index. markSavedByPath, updateTabContentByPath and the save loop use path, but onContentChange and updateContent do not.

MarkdownEditor keeps its CM doc in sync with the store only through the tab-switch effect (path change), the signal-driven content-sync effect, and the rename shortcut (MarkdownEditor.svelte:179-194). A rename shortcut that fires when two tabs have identical content skips the doc replace; this is harmless because the docs are equal.

Note bytes on disk are written from tab.content with absolute paths (saveFileByPath). The window-close handler and vault switch are the only exits that call saveAllDirtyTabs; closeTab only prompts for dirty tabs.

resolveFilePath rejects traversal (utils/path.ts:33-44) and createNote calls it inside its try, so a wikilink such as [[../x]] cannot write outside the vault (editor-host.ts:85-105). openExternal is gated by isSafeUrl in click-handler.ts:31-36.

maps.summary: Vault lifecycle orchestration. initializeVault (src/lib/app/lifecycle/app-lifecycle.service.ts:133-527) runs from the layout effect on every vaultStore path change (src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte:65-79). Its teardown branch (172-189) saves dirty tabs, drains calendar writes, then calls teardownVault (533-648), which stops the watcher, closes the DB, saves the Rust index cache and resets every store including the editor tabs. Steps 1-9 load settings, open the vault DB, register per-file consumers, build indexes, then start the watcher. boot.ts registers app-lifetime ports once from the layout script (+layout.svelte:27). index-updater.service.ts is the 1 s debounced 'edit' entry point for the active tab (+layout.svelte:137-157) and delegates to applyNoteChange. global-keybindings.ts registers app shortcuts (their handlers call editor/tab/layout services). commands.ts builds the palette list and reads shortcut labels from the binding table. Note-byte flush points: switchVault (src/lib/core/vault/vault.service.ts:18-22), the initializeVault safety-net save (app-lifecycle:180), registerCloseHandler on window close (src/lib/app/tauri-listeners.service.ts:50-82), and teardownVault's resetEditor, which drops every tab (editor.service.ts:412-417).
maps.data_flow: Keystrokes call editorStore.updateContent (editor.service.ts:224-227) and arm the 2 s body or 500 ms frontmatter autosave. saveFileByPath (161-178) writes tab.content with writeTextFile, then markSavedByPath, then notifyAfterSave. On failure it toasts and leaves the tab dirty. The layout content effect calls updateIndexesForFile (index-updater.service.ts:24-44), which calls applyNoteChange 'edit' (Rust update_note_in_index, consumer fan-out). Vault switch: switchVault saves dirty tabs and ignores the failure list (vault.service.ts:19), drainPendingWrites, then vaultStore.open. The layout effect then runs initializeVault, whose teardown branch (only if unsubscribeFileChange is set) saves again with the result ignored (app-lifecycle:180), drains calendar writes, and calls teardownVault, which calls resetEditor (tabs = []). Watcher: onFileChange feeds runWatcherBatch (app-lifecycle:481-498), which runs reloadExternallyChangedTabs (editor.service.ts:375-404; clean tabs only, but the eligibility check is not repeated after the reads) and rebuildAllIndexes. Quit: onCloseRequested calls saveAllDirtyTabs, prompts on failure (tauri-listeners:55-63), drains calendar writes, flushes settings, then destroy().
invariants: Dirty tab content is the only copy of unsaved text (no crash or session copy exists in src/lib/core/editor). Every path that resets the editor must have saved it or obtained discard consent. Today the vault-switch path does not check.
switchVault must not open the next vault while saveAllDirtyTabs reports failed paths unless the user chose to discard (the close handler does this; the switch path does not).

teardownVault / resetEditor run only from the layout effect's closed-vault branch or initializeVault's teardown branch. The latter is gated on unsubscribeFileChange (app-lifecycle:172), which is set only at step 7 (494) and cleared by teardown, so an init that exits before step 7 leaves that gate closed.

initVersion must be re-checked after every await that can outlive a vault switch. Current guards at 240, 296, 322, 373 are not enough: awaits at 202 (configureSentry), 220 (initLogSession) and 384 (ensureTemplatesFolder) have no guard before the next vault-scoped side effect.

Paths captured at start must be used during teardown, because vaultStore.path already points to the new vault then: indexedVaultPath (app-lifecycle:100-108) and the settings persistence path (settings-persistence.svelte.ts:46-66, flush reads session.path synchronously at :82).

Vault-lifetime registrations (note-change consumers, after-save observers, file-history, search) are unregistered at initializeVault entry, before the safety-net save. The safety-net save therefore writes without history snapshots or FTS updates (app-lifecycle:161-168), which the comment at :174-177 accepts. Auto-move's observer is not unregistered there (auto-move.service.ts:95-125).
A pending watcher reload must not overwrite a tab that became dirty during its reads. This is not currently enforced (editor.service.ts:397-401).
The per-file index dedupe map (index-dedupe.ts) is cleared by resetHooks on teardown (editor.hooks.ts:100). registerAppPorts ports are not in the vault-lifetime unregister list (boot.ts:25-27).

maps.summary: Native vault watcher and its TS consumers. src-tauri/src/vault/watcher.rs wraps notify 8.2.1 (FSEvents on macOS): raw events go through a channel to a bridge thread that drops hidden-dir paths (any dot segment), buffers the rest in a HashSet, drops ancestor paths, and emits one vault-files-changed batch after 500 ms of quiet (no max wait). commands/watcher.rs exposes start/stop as sync commands. src/lib/core/filesystem/fs.watcher.ts receives batches, serialises nothing, patches the sidebar tree (resolveRescanParents + scan_vault per parent, or full loadDirectoryTree when more than 5 parents) and notifies onFileChange listeners. app-lifecycle.service.ts (not in this area's file list, read for the call chain) debounces 300 ms, serialises runWatcherBatch, calls reloadExternallyChangedTabs (clean open tabs only, re-read from disk into the editor store) and then watcher-handler.service.ts::rebuildAllIndexes (skip if dir-only or all self-saves; up to 10 .md files go through read_files_batch then applyNoteChange(source 'watcher'); larger sets run rebuildIndex, buildPropertyIndex, buildFrontmatterIconIndex). tauri-listeners.service.ts consumes vault-index-updated (throttled 2 s / 10 s, incremental get_index_delta patch, or fullRefresh) and also registers close, focus and menu listeners. The watcher itself never writes note bytes; its only content effects are the editor reload and the index updates.
maps.data_flow: FSEvents/inotify -> notify thread (fsevent.rs callback) -> mpsc channel (watcher.rs:250-262) -> bridge thread run_debounce_loop (hidden filter, HashSet buffer, 500 ms quiet debounce, filter_ancestor_paths) -> Tauri event vault-files-changed -> fs.watcher.ts handleChangedPaths (tree: scan_vault per parent or refreshTree; then onFileChange listeners) -> app-lifecycle pendingWatcherPaths -> 300 ms debounce -> serializeWithRerun runWatcherBatch -> reloadExternallyChangedTabs (readTextFile for clean open tabs -> editor store updateTabContentByPath + CodeMirror doc replace) -> rebuildAllIndexes (read_files_batch -> applyNoteChange 'watcher' per file: update_note_in_index, update_search_index_file, update_semantic_file, consumers; or delete path: remove_note_from_index, remove_from_search_index, remove_semantic_file) -> Rust VaultIndex emits vault-index-updated -> tauri-listeners throttled refresh (get_index_delta, patchVaultEntries / fullRefresh, typeDefinitions, content order, property index). Start/stop: startWatching -> stopWatching (watchVersion++, unlisten, stop_vault_watcher) -> on(vault-files-changed) -> start_vault_watcher (replace_watcher joins the old bridge thread).
invariants: Watcher code paths only read note bytes (read_files_batch, scan_vault, readTextFile); nothing in this area writes note content. Dirty state exists only in the editor store (editor.logic.ts:44-46 isTabDirty = content !== savedContent).
An open tab may be overwritten from disk only if it was clean. This must hold at apply time, not only at eligibility time (currently violated, finding 1).
The batch carries paths only, never event kinds. The TS side therefore treats a directory-only batch as 'nothing to index'. A rescan request from notify is lost in the bridge (finding 2).

The Rust hidden-dir filter compares event paths against vault_prefix built from the un-canonicalised vault path (watcher.rs:245-249, 71-79). It holds only if the vault path has no symlink component and FSEvents reports the same spelling (finding 7).
Editor tabs, recentSaves (editor.hooks.ts), index-dedupe and the Rust index all key on the exact absolute path string that the watcher reports. Any spelling difference splits keys.
Self-save skip (areAllRecentSaves) assumes the Rust index already holds the saved bytes and that no older watcher read lands afterwards (finding 6). Nothing compares content.

watchVersion invalidates in-flight handleChangedPaths work only across stop/start. Overlapping batches on the same vault are not serialised, so the tree patch is last-writer-wins on a snapshot (finding 4).
rebuildAllIndexes reads vaultStore.path after awaits in the serialised run. Vault-switch safety depends on initVersion guards that runWatcherBatch does not check (finding 8).
Index deltas are last-operation-wins per path (tauri-listeners.service.ts pendingPaths Map, lines ~270-274), and a path missing from get_index_delta counts as removed.
stopWatching must run before the next startWatching's on() listener is stored; two concurrent startWatching calls can leak a listener (finding 9).

maps.data_flow: Test only.
invariants: test invariant

maps.summary: fs.service.ts is the TS facade for disk mutations in the file explorer: create file/folder, delete (to Trash), rename, move, duplicate, reveal, and it builds the file tree (scan_vault, folder-order.json, applyFolderOrder). fs.logic.ts holds the pure helpers (name validation and uniqueness, tree search and removal, folder-order and _order sorting, rescan-parent resolution, drag-drop validation). fs.store.svelte.ts holds fileTree, folderOrder, contentOrder, loadingCount and renamingPath. link-updater.service.ts rewrites wikilinks in backlinking notes after a note rename, using link-updater.logic.ts (replaceWikilinks). folder-notes.logic.ts maps X/X.md folder notes and _order frontmatter into a path-to-order map. Rename, move and delete all go through path-change.service.ts applyPathChange (ordering: close tabs, diskOp, re-point tabs, consumers, link rewrite, refreshTree, rename_note, forget old paths). Create goes through Rust create_note, which writes and indexes. Duplicate copies bytes with plugin-fs copyFile and bypasses the note-change owner. Scope of checks: read all six files fully; traced callers in path-change.service.ts, editor.service.ts, editor.store.svelte.ts, note-change.service.ts, the Rust vault.rs and index.rs, and the plugin-fs 2.7.1 Rust source in the cargo registry. Not done: no tests or builds run (read-only audit); APFS case-insensitive behaviour is taken as the macOS default, not reproduced; the trash move body (trash.service.ts past line 60) was not read; whether vault switching waits for in-flight scans was not verified; FSEvents per-child event behaviour for folder moves was not verified.
maps.data_flow: Create: createFile(parent, name, content) reads sibling names (readDir), picks a case-insensitive unique name (fs.logic.ts:218-249), calls Rust create_note (writes atomically, refuses existing path, indexes content: vault.rs:888-896), markRecentSave, applyNoteChange(upsert, source fs, vaultPath for .md) (fs.service.ts:119-145), then refreshTree. Rename/move: renameItem/moveItem check exists(newPath) (fs.service.ts:205, 233) then applyPathChange with diskOp = plugin-fs rename (fs.service.ts:206-214, 234-240). applyPathChange (path-change.service.ts:117-171) snapshots child paths, awaits diskOp, re-points open tabs synchronously (line 132), runs consumers, awaits updateLinksAfterRename for .md name changes (lines 143-151: get_backlinks_v2(from), read or use dirty tab snapshot, replaceWikilinks, writeTextFile, syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved, 'none'), applyNoteChange(save)), refreshTree, rename_note (re-keys Rust VaultIndex), then forgetNote on old paths (removes dedupe signature, per-file indexes, Rust entry, FTS5 and semantic rows for the old key). Delete: deleteItem -> applyPathChange(to=null): closeTabsForDeletedPath (before disk op), moveToTrash(vaultPath, path, isDirectory) (fallback permanent remove when no vault), removeNodeByPath on the tree, forgetNote. Duplicate: generateCopyName over raw sibling names, copyFile (or recursive mkdir+copyFile), refreshTree; no create_note, no applyNoteChange (Rust index and FTS catch up through the watcher). Tree load: loadDirectoryTree -> scan_vault + loadFolderOrder (reads or creates .kokobrain/folder-order.json; parse failure returns {} without writing) -> applyFolderOrder (uses folder-order.json, then contentOrder from _order via folder-notes.logic.ts) -> attachFileCounts -> setFileTree. Note bytes change only in two ways: rename/move preserves bytes (rename), and updateLinksAfterRename rewrites wikilink target text in backlinking notes. Delete moves bytes to Trash. Duplicate copies bytes.
invariants: An existing destination is never overwritten by a rename, move, create or duplicate. renameItem and moveItem check exists() first (fs.service.ts:205, 233); createFile and createFolder use generateUniqueName, which lowercases for case-insensitive volumes (fs.logic.ts:225-226, 247); Rust create_note refuses an existing path (vault.rs:888-896). duplicateItem is the exception (finding 1). plugin-fs copy_file and rename call std::fs::copy and std::fs::rename, which overwrite the destination (tauri-plugin-fs-2.7.1 commands.rs ~393 and ~864), so the TS guards are the only protection, and exists-then-rename is not atomic.
Name uniqueness is case-insensitive on macOS volumes (APFS default). Any uniqueness helper must lowercase both sides (fs.logic.ts:218-226 documents this).
get_backlinks_v2(from) must run before rename_note re-keys the Rust index, otherwise the affected set is empty (path-change.service.ts:143-151 orders it so).
Open tabs are re-pointed to the new path before any await after the disk op (path-change.service.ts:132), so the autosave debounce writes to the new path.

closeTabsForDeletedPath runs before diskOp so the 2 s autosave cannot recreate a deleted file (path-change.service.ts:125; editor.service.ts:197-200). Side effect: dirty content of a deleted tab is dropped, not saved (finding 2).

The link rewrite assumes no keystrokes land between its content snapshot and syncExternalContentToEditor (link-updater.service.ts:33-47); syncExternalContentToEditor overwrites unconditionally (editor.service.ts:76-80, editor.store.svelte.ts:130-135).
loadFolderOrder never overwrites an existing folder-order.json: it writes only the template when the file is missing, and falls back to {} on read or parse failure (fs.service.ts:42-70).
The only folder-note key is the X/X.md convention (folder-notes.logic.ts:59-63). Renaming a folder does not rename its folder note.
Delete outside an open vault is a permanent remove, bypassing Trash (fs.service.ts:179-182). Not reached by the UI paths read (all delete callers are vault-scoped).
resetFileSystem runs during vault teardown (app-lifecycle.service.ts:623). loadDirectoryTree has no generation token, so a load started for a previous vault can publish after the reset (finding 10).
rename(2) preserves file bytes. Wikilink matching in replaceWikilinks is exact on the bare target (after trim and lowercase), so path-qualified and aliased forms are handled only partly (finding 5).

maps.summary: frontmatter-write.service.ts exports updateNoteFrontmatter(path, mutate), the one writer that rewrites a note's YAML frontmatter for favorite toggles (NoteRowMenu.svelte:215 via lifecycle.service.ts:46-53), icon picks (frontmatter-icon.service.ts:27-41), event-calendar edits (event-calendar.service.ts:753) and bookmark migration. It has two branches. Open tab: base = tab.content (kept in sync per keystroke), rebuilt, pushed to the editor with syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=false), then saved with saveFileByPath. Closed note: base = readTextFile, detectLossyFrontmatter refuses lossy blocks, rebuildContent writes the block plus the untouched body, then exists() and writeTextFile({create:false}) and notifyAfterSave. properties.logic.ts does the parse (yaml 2.9.1 Document, alias/wikilink fold, canonical keys, LRU parse cache), the lossy detector, serializeProperties (yaml Document.set, flow lists, key dedupe), and rebuildContent/extractBody (shared FRONTMATTER_REGEX). yaml-quoting.logic.ts is a pure predicate that documents yaml's quoting rules; production code never imports it (only yaml-quoting.logic.test.ts does), so it cannot change written bytes. The main defect is that scalars which are not strings are rewritten from their parsed JS value: numbers like 0042, 1.0, 0x1F and booleans like True lose their source text on every write, and nothing refuses or warns. Other findings are low: silent rethrow of closed-note write errors, non-atomic truncate-then-write, no per-path serialization of closed-note writers, an unquoted [[X]] falsely refused as nested, and byte-level changes (closing delimiter prefix, CRLF to LF in the frontmatter, BOM dropped by TextDecoder).
maps.data_flow: Open note: the active CodeMirror doc change listener (editor-extensions.ts:170-190) calls onContentChange -> editorStore.updateContent (editor.service.ts:224-227, editor.store.svelte.ts:83-88), so tab.content tracks the doc on every keystroke except during tab switches and external replaces. updateNoteFrontmatter -> attempt reads tab.content, runs detectLossyFrontmatter, parseFrontmatterProperties, mutate, rebuildContent. If next !== base it calls syncExternalContentToEditor(path, next, false, 'none') (sets tab.content only, bumps the CM signal), then saveFileByPath (writes tab.content with writeTextFile, markSavedByPath, notifyAfterSave). On failure it restores base only if tab.content is still next. Closed note: readTextFile(path) -> assertVault -> detectLossyFrontmatter -> parse -> mutate -> rebuildContent; then exists() -> assertVault -> findTab re-check (restarts once into the tab branch) -> writeTextFile(path, next, {create:false}) (plugin-fs truncates then write_all) -> assertVault -> syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true) (no-op unless a tab opened during the write) -> notifyAfterSave(path, next) (applyNoteChange 'save', queryjs invalidation, after-save observers). Failures are FrontmatterWriteError with a reason, except read errors and write errors on an existing file, which are rethrown raw (frontmatter-write.service.ts:117, 150-153). No IPC or store is written except through these calls.
invariants: For an open note, tab.content must equal the live CodeMirror doc at the moment updateNoteFrontmatter reads it: the doc update listener sets it synchronously (editor-extensions.ts:170-190; MarkdownEditor.svelte:124), and it is suppressed only during tab switches and external replaces.

For a closed note, the base is the disk read at entry. Between the findTab re-check (frontmatter-write.service.ts:144) and the writeTextFile call (:149) there is no await, so a tab opened during the read takes the tab branch.

A tab opened during the closed-note write is reconciled by syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true) at :156. A tab whose read was issued before the write but resolved after it is not reconciled here. The watcher's reloadExternallyChangedTabs (app-lifecycle.service.ts:486) heals clean tabs only.

detectLossyFrontmatter must return non-null for every block whose parse-then-serialize changes data. It does not cover numeric or boolean text (0042, 1.0, 0x1F, True), which the round trip rewrites, and it reports a folded unquoted [[X]] as nested although the fold keeps the value.

extractBody and detectLossyFrontmatter share FRONTMATTER_REGEX (properties.logic.ts:37), which has no end-of-line anchor on the closing ---. A line such as ---Hello or ---- closes the block and the rest of that line becomes body text.

Closed-note writers must be serialized per path (contract at frontmatter-write.service.ts:91-93). Nothing enforces it. event-calendar does (holdPath, event-calendar.service.ts:440); the favorite and icon writers do not (lifecycle.service.ts:50, frontmatter-icon.service.ts:36).

mutate must be pure and use canonical keys. serializeProperties' dedupeCanonicalKeys keeps the first populated value of an alias pair and only logs a discarded populated twin (properties.logic.ts:497-506), so an alias written by a mutate would be silently dropped. The three write callers use canonical keys (_favorite, _icon, _color, _title_color, event_*), so no current caller hits this.

saveFileByPath returns early for a clean tab (editor.service.ts:163). A tab-branch write therefore relies on savedContent equalling the bytes on disk; the early return is still correct when next equals savedContent.
After each await, assertVault throws vault-changed. A vault-changed error thrown after the write means the bytes are already on disk (documented at frontmatter-write.service.ts:22-23).
The parse cache hands out clones (properties.logic.ts:224-237, 315), so mutate cannot corrupt cached entries.

The write uses writeTextFile's default open (truncate then write_all, tauri-plugin-fs 2.7.1 commands.rs:1156-1181, 1202). There is no temp file or rename, so a write that fails after truncation leaves a partial note.

maps.summary: The trash moves a deleted note or folder by rename() into <vault>/.kokobrain/trash/items/<uuid>/<fileName> and records metadata (id, originalPath, fileName, isDirectory, trashedAt) in trash-manifest.json. No note bytes are copied or rewritten by the trash itself; the file is the only copy. trash.service.ts exports loadTrash (called at vault init, app-lifecycle.service.ts:288), moveToTrash (called from fs.service.ts:177 via deleteItem and applyPathChange's diskOp), restoreItem (rename back, suffixes "(restored N)" on collision, then re-indexes restored Markdown through applyNoteChange with source 'restore'), deletePermanently, emptyTrash and resetTrash (teardown, app-lifecycle.service.ts:643). Every manifest write is saveManifest(vaultPath, <whole in-memory store>), so the on-disk manifest is only as correct as the in-memory store it is derived from. trash.logic.ts holds path helpers, createTrashItem (crypto.randomUUID), a silent parseTrashManifest, and formatTrashedDate. trash.store.svelte.ts is a plain $state list with getters and setters. Read: trash.service.ts (306 lines, full), trash.logic.ts (105, full), trash.store.svelte.ts (34, full). Plugin-fs behavior checked in node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-fs/dist-js/index.js and the locked tauri-plugin-fs 2.7.1 Rust source (commands.rs).
maps.data_flow: Delete: UI (NoteRowMenu.svelte:124-129, note-action-bar.service.ts:21-27, FilesNavigator.svelte:174) -> deleteItem (fs.service.ts:167-181) -> applyPathChange (path-change.service.ts:125 closeTabsForDeletedPath before diskOp at :127) -> moveToTrash: mkdir items/<id>, rename(abs, items/<id>/<name>) (trash.service.ts:68-72), saveManifest([item, ...store]) (:79, failures logged and swallowed), trashStore.addItem (:83). Note bytes never leave the file. Restore: exists check + suffix (:116-118), mkdir parent (:121-123), rename back (:126), remove empty container (:130), saveManifest(store minus item) (:137-141, failure swallowed), removeItem (:143), then readTextFile of restored .md (:248) -> markRecentSave (:253) -> applyNoteChange upsert source 'restore' (:254) -> notifyContentInvalidated (:258). Load: readTextFile(manifest) -> parseTrashManifest -> setItems (:24-43); any error sets []. Permanent delete: remove(items/<id>) (:188) then saveManifest(filtered) (:191). Empty: remove(items dir) (:207-210) then saveManifest([]) (:213) then clear. Manifest holds metadata only, no content.
invariants: The in-memory trashStore must mirror the on-disk manifest before any save. Nothing enforces this: loadTrash sets [] on failure (trash.service.ts:37-39) and every save writes the whole store (:79, :139, :191, :213). Violating it overwrites the manifest and orphans trashed files (finding 1).

A trashed file lives only at .kokobrain/trash/items/<id>/<fileName>. moveToTrash removes the container only when rename never ran (trash.service.ts:91), and restoreItem removes it only after the rename succeeded (:126-131). Both are safe.

Restore never overwrites an existing path: it probes exists() and picks a suffixed name (:116-118). This is a check-then-act race because the Rust rename (commands.rs:864) replaces an existing destination, as the plugin JS doc says (node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-fs/dist-js/index.js:601-602).

deleteItem closes tabs before the disk op (path-change.service.ts:125) so the 2 s autosave timer cannot recreate the deleted file (editor.service.ts:203-211 iterates current tabs only). The same ordering means unsaved buffer text for that tab is discarded, not written to the trash (finding 2).
The watcher ignores dot-directories such as .kokobrain (CLAUDE.md, Rust side; not re-read here), so trash writes do not trigger a rebuild.

Restored Markdown is marked (markRecentSave) before applyNoteChange so the watcher's self-save skip applies (trash.service.ts:253-254). The 'restore' source fires the Rust IPC on every call (note-change.service.ts:94).
The trash item id is crypto.randomUUID (trash.logic.ts:46). The comments in trash.logic.ts:37 and trash.types.ts:4 say 'timestamp-based' / Date.now(), which is stale.
emptyTrash removes the whole items directory, including any directory with no manifest entry, so orphans are destroyed by Empty Trash (trash.service.ts:207-210).

maps.summary: Per-file snapshot history. Every successful save of a note (editor.service.ts saveFileByPath -> notifyAfterSave -> registerFileHistoryHook) calls the Rust save_snapshot command, which stores the full content in the vault SQLite table `snapshots` (keyed by vault-relative path, deduped against the latest row's SHA-256). Optionally a plain .md copy is written to `.kokobrain/snapshots-backup/<rel>/<ms>.md` (settings snapshotBackupEnabled, default off). The FileHistoryDialog (opened from the command palette, Cmd+Shift+H, or the active tab) lists snapshots grouped by day, computes a line diff (Rust compute_diff via `similar`) between the selected snapshot and the on-disk file, and offers Restore: the snapshot text is dispatched into the single global CodeMirror view and saved through the normal save flow. Rust side (history.rs, history_repo.rs, db/mod.rs) looks sound: per-vault DB at {vault}/.kokobrain/kokobrain.db, mutex-serialized find-latest + insert, retention SQL keeps 1 row per file per day in the medium window. The main problems are on the TS restore path: it never checks that the editor shows the file the dialog was opened for, it discards the unsaved buffer without snapshotting it, and it reports success in cases where nothing was written.
maps.data_flow: Reads: openFileHistory reads the on-disk file (service.ts:28, kept as fileHistoryStore.currentContent, the diff's "new" side) and calls get_file_history (service.ts:31). selectSnapshot calls get_snapshot_content and compute_diff (service.ts:62-68). Backup icons come from a readDir of the backup dir (service.ts:154-178). Writes: save_snapshot inserts a row (history.rs:57-78) and, when it returns true and backups are enabled, a backup .md file (service.ts:117-122, 130-148). Restore: get_snapshot_content (service.ts:85) -> CodeMirror dispatch into editorStore.editorView (service.ts:89-95) -> updateListener (editor-extensions.ts:170-188) -> onContentChange -> editorStore.updateContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88) -> saveCurrentFile (service.ts:99) -> saveFileByPath(activeTab.path) (editor.service.ts:151-177) -> writeTextFile -> notifyAfterSave -> save_snapshot. Note that the write target is the ACTIVE tab, not fileHistoryStore.filePath.
invariants: Restore must write only to the file the dialog was opened for (fileHistoryStore.filePath). NOT enforced: restoreSnapshot (service.ts:82-105) only uses filePath for a null check and a log line; the dispatch goes to editorStore.editorView and the save goes to editorStore.activeTab.path.

The snapshot content equals the bytes written: saveFileByPath captures `const content = tab.content` before writeTextFile (editor.service.ts:162-168) and passes that same string to notifyAfterSave. Holds.

History is keyed by vault-relative path only (service.ts:115, history.rs:57-84). Renames, moves and deletes do not migrate or remove rows (no reference in path-change.service.ts), so a path's history can belong to a different file over time.

The DB is per vault (db/mod.rs:36-46) and save_snapshot runs before the vault switch completes (vault.service.ts:14-19 comment: saves and drains happen while vaultStore.path is still the old vault). Holds.

Backup names use JS Date.now() taken after the save_snapshot IPC returns (service.ts:121), not the Rust created_at (history.rs:63-64), so backup-to-snapshot matching depends on a 10 s tolerance (file-history.logic.ts:151-173).

Auto-save is a 2 s debounce that resets on every keystroke (editor.service.ts:197, debounce.ts:9-17), so unsaved text can stay in memory only for the length of a typing burst. openFileHistory does not flush it.
The after-save hook is registered per vault init and unsubscribed on teardown (app-lifecycle.service.ts:161-163, 557-560); closeFileHistory runs at teardown (app-lifecycle.service.ts:604).

The Rust side never deletes backup .md files (grep: no reference to snapshots-backup in src-tauri), and cleanup_history (history.rs:142-158) touches only SQL rows. Backups therefore grow without bound when enabled. This is a storage risk, not a content-loss bug.

maps.summary: Rust-side note writes: fs.rs write_atomic (temp file in the same dir, then rename over the target) plus its vault-tree and directory walkers, and vault.rs commands that write note bytes (toggle_task_status_inner, propagate_type_rename_inner, create_note, create_folder). rename_note/rename_note_inner touch only the VaultIndex (the disk rename is TS-side). files.rs read_files_batch is read-only and confines reads to the vault via canonicalize + Path::starts_with. Every Rust write goes through write_atomic, and the index is updated only after the disk write succeeds. The main typing save does NOT use this path: editor.service.ts:161-170 calls plugin-fs writeTextFile. The worst finding is in the TS handoff of toggle_task_status: Rust computes the new content from the disk copy, and the frontend then overwrites the open tab's unsaved buffer with it.
maps.data_flow: toggle_task_status: TS tasks.service.ts:102 invoke -> vault.rs:707 takes VaultIndexState write lock -> toggle_task_status_inner reads disk (vault.rs:669) -> toggle_task_in_content (parsing.rs:1873) -> write_atomic (vault.rs:683, fs.rs:16) -> update_note_in_index_inner (vault.rs:685) -> emit if changed. TS then calls syncExternalContentToEditor(path, updatedContent, markSaved=true) (tasks.service.ts:113, editor.service.ts:70-92), which replaces tab.content and savedContent with the disk-derived text and dispatches a CodeMirror doc replace (MarkdownEditor.svelte:328-333, addToHistory false). propagate_type_rename: TS renameType rewrites open tabs first via writeTextFile (type-definitions.service.ts:215-220), then Rust walks index members, reads disk, rewrite_type_in_frontmatter (parsing.rs:101), write_atomic, reindex (vault.rs:342-386). create_note: ensure_safe_write_path (vault.rs:862) -> exists() check (vault.rs:896) -> write_atomic (vault.rs:899) -> index -> emit. rename_note: index re-key only (vault.rs:1001-1033). read_files_batch: canonicalize -> starts_with vault root -> read_to_string (files.rs:24-84).
invariants: Index is mutated only after the disk write succeeds (vault.rs:683-685, 370-378, 899-905); a failed write leaves the index untouched and returns Err.
The indexed content equals the bytes written (updated / new_content), and mtime is re-read after the write (vault.rs:684, 900).

write_atomic keeps the old file on any failure before the rename; the temp file is in the same directory so rename is same-filesystem (fs.rs:16-32). Rename failure removes the temp file (fs.rs:28-31).
Task line numbers are 1-based and split on '\n' in both extract_tasks (parsing.rs:1680-1694) and toggle_task_in_content (parsing.rs:1878), so CRLF and counting agree.
create_note and create_folder reject non-absolute paths and any '..' component (vault.rs:862-874). toggle_task_status and propagate_type_rename do not call this check.
toggle_task_status and propagate_type_rename read disk, never the editor buffer. Nothing in Rust enforces that the TS caller flushes or merges a dirty tab first.
propagate_type_rename rewrites only when the disk frontmatter still matches the old type (parsing.rs:101-125), so a stale index entry cannot rewrite an unrelated note.
read_files_batch confines reads with canonicalize + Path::starts_with, which is component-wise, so /vault-other is not treated as inside /vault (files.rs:37-60). It has no write path.
The create_note exists() check (vault.rs:896) is not atomic with the rename in write_atomic (fs.rs:28); the window is small and TS createFile generates unique names first (fs.service.ts:121-124).

maps.summary: setup/editor-extensions.ts builds the CodeMirror 6 extension array for the markdown editor (createExtensions, editorModeEffects, sourceModeExtensions). setup/editor-theme.ts builds the theme. extensions/composition-aware-bracket-matching.ts is a ViewPlugin replacing bracketMatching() that freezes bracket decorations during IME composition (WebKit workaround). highlight-styles.ts holds the markdown language factory (GFM + math + highlight lezer extensions), the markdown and code HighlightStyles, and getLanguageEffects/getLanguageEffectsSync, which pick the language per file. extensions/lezer/math-extension.ts adds InlineMath and BlockMath nodes; highlight-extension.ts adds ==highlight== nodes. One EditorView is created per MarkdownEditor mount (MarkdownEditor.svelte:131) and reused across markdown and code tab switches, which replace the whole document with a dispatch marked addToHistory=false. The history() extension (editor-extensions.ts:130) and historyKeymap (line 160) are therefore shared across all notes shown by that view.
maps.data_flow: User keystroke: CM doc change -> EditorView.updateListener (editor-extensions.ts:170-190, skipped only when isTabSwitching or isExternalEdit is set) -> opts.onDocChanged(doc.toString(), fmChanged) -> onContentChange (MarkdownEditor.svelte:124, editor.service.ts:224) -> editorStore.updateContent writes tabs[activeIndex].content (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88) -> scheduleAutoSave (2000 ms body, 500 ms frontmatter). Tab switch: MarkdownEditor.svelte:170-275 sets isTabSwitching, dispatches a full-doc replace with addToHistory=false, then clears the flag (lines 227-237); the code-file language load is fired without a tab check (239-243). External sync (watcher reload editor.service.ts:401, frontmatter-write.service.ts:128, link-updater.service.ts:47) uses the same full replace with isExternalEdit set (328-334). Language: markdown and kanban take the sync path (fs.logic.ts:104-110 returns null for markdown); code files await langDesc.load() (highlight-styles.ts:120-133). Parse tree: the lezer extensions feed syntaxTree, which live-preview decorations read, including block-math-field.ts.
invariants: isTabSwitching and isExternalEdit wrap only a synchronous dispatch; CodeMirror calls update listeners synchronously (node_modules/@codemirror/view/dist/index.js ~8101-8104), so no real keystroke is suppressed.
The store copy is written from the CM doc on every user edit (onContentChange), so the external-sync source activeTab.content equals the CM doc just before the replace.

Non-history document replaces must not leave the undo stack pointing at text that is no longer in the document. This is VIOLATED: CM maps old undo entries through addToHistory=false replaces (node_modules/@codemirror/commands/dist/index.js:240-241, 479-486), and inverse insertions of deleted text land at a document boundary. Nothing clears or isolates history on tab switch or external sync.
getLanguageForFile returns null for markdown and kanban files (fs.logic.ts:104-109), so markdown never takes the async code-language path.
A destroyed EditorView ignores dispatch (node_modules/@codemirror/view/dist/index.js:8026-8029), so the late applyLanguageForTab after unmount is harmless.

Bracket decorations are rebuilt on the first non-composing docChanged or selectionSet: compositionend sets composing to -1 before the commit transaction (view dist ~5330), so the commit after an IME edit is not frozen.
A lezer BlockMath node must not span content that belongs to other block structure. This is VIOLATED by the unclosed or stray $$ parser (math-extension.ts:76-91).

maps.summary: live-preview.ts assembles the live-preview extension array (block decorators, inline pipeline, inline plugins, scroll debounce, click and paste handlers) behind a compartment that is replaced by [] in source mode. core/ holds the shared machinery: blockDecorator (the single ViewPlugin factory for full-document block decorators), checkUpdateAction and isPureScroll (the update gate), revealPredicate and touchedLines (which lines show source), hideLines (line collapse via Decoration.replace and a line class), frontmatterSlice, isInsideBlockContext, the fencedBlockRenderers facet, the mouse-drag StateField and handlers, the calloutFoldState StateField, scrollDebouncePlugin (150 ms after scroll stops, dispatches forceDecorationRebuild), expandedVisibleRanges, and profiling/error ports. This layer never changes the document: its only dispatches are effects (forceDecorationRebuild, setMouseSelecting, toggleCalloutFold). I found no path in this area that loses or rewrites note bytes. The findings are display or interaction defects only. I did not run tests or builds (read-only audit).
maps.data_flow: Note text enters only as the EditorState document owned by MarkdownEditor (createExtensions and external content sync). Core reads state.doc, the Lezer syntax tree and its own StateFields, and writes only DecorationSets (replace, line, widget) to ViewPlugins plus fold and drag state. Dispatch sites in core: scroll-debounce-plugin.ts:37 (forceDecorationRebuild after 150 ms without viewport change), mouse-selecting.ts:21 and :42 (setMouseSelecting), and callout-field.ts:33 (toggleCalloutFold, plugin side). MarkdownEditor.svelte dispatches forceDecorationRebuild at lines 268, 354, 370 and 135 (tab switch, tag colors, renderer rebuildOn). Mode changes go through editorModeEffects (setup/editor-extensions.ts:112-121), which reconfigures livePreviewCompartment. Block decorators run compute(state) on construction and on rebuild triggers only (block-decorator.ts:66-87). Inline plugins gate on checkUpdateAction too (inline-formatting-plugin.ts:192-196).
invariants: Core never mutates the document. Grep of core/ and the plugins shows dispatches carry only effects. Note bytes change only through the editor's own input path and MarkdownEditor's external sync.
Every docChanged transaction rebuilds full-document block decorators (check-update-action.ts:20), so decoration positions never outlive the document they were computed from.

Hidden lines (hide-lines.ts:14-19) show whenever the touched-line set intersects them (reveal.ts:66-76). An edit that moves the cursor into a hidden block reveals it in the same update, so hidden-text edits are visible afterwards.

A selection-only 'none' answer is valid only while the touched-line set equals the set the last rebuild used (check-update-action.ts:34-36). Drag end always rebuilds (check-update-action.ts:28). A release transaction that also carries a viewport-only change is skipped by isPureScroll (block-decorator.ts:72) and recovers when scrollDebouncePlugin fires about 150 ms later (scroll-debounce-plugin.ts:32-40).
A replace decoration never spans a line break. hideLines replaces only line text (hide-lines.ts:17-18), and @codemirror/view rejects block-level replaces from plugins (view dist index.js:2804).

frontmatterSlice (frontmatter-slice.ts:12-18) returns a prefix that FRONTMATTER_REGEX (properties.logic.ts:37) matches the same way as the full text. The parity holds except when a lone CR, which CodeMirror treats as a line break (@codemirror/state DefaultSplit /\r\n?|\n/), precedes the closing fence.

A throw in a ViewPlugin update or constructor deactivates that plugin and logs 'CodeMirror plugin crashed' (view dist index.js:1507-1509). A throw in a StateField update propagates out of dispatch. The only core StateField with logic is calloutFoldState; its remap (effects.ts:19-28) calls tr.startState.doc.line(n) and needs every stored number to be within the document. This holds because toggle values come from CalloutFoldWidget.startLine and the widget's eq() compares startLine (callout-field.ts, CalloutFoldWidget.eq), so a retained DOM never carries a stale line.
The drag flag is cleared only by a document-level mouseup listener armed on each mousedown (mouse-selecting.ts:43-45), or by a content mouseup or dragstart. Nothing else clears it.
revealPredicate returns () => false while dragging (reveal.ts:67) by design, so nothing is revealed mid-drag and the release rebuild restores reveal.

maps.summary: The inline pipeline is one ViewPlugin (inline-formatting-plugin.ts:176-208) built from a registry of Lezer node handlers (NodeHandler, dispatched by node name) and regex line handlers (LineHandler, run per non-block line), plus a HighlightStyle for bold/italic/strikethrough/monospace (markdown-highlight-style.ts:15-20). inline-extensions.ts assembles the production lists (lines 27-49) and maps Troubleshooting kill-switch names to handler groups (lines 60-86). Each rebuild walks the syntax tree over expandedVisibleRanges (visible range plus 2000 chars, core/expanded-ranges.ts) and emits hiddenSyntaxDeco replaces, mark/line decorations and widgets. Reveal is per line: a construct is shown as source when any line it touches is in the selection (core/reveal.ts:66-77), and nothing is revealed during a mouse drag. Rebuilds happen on doc change, reconfigure, drag release, forceDecorationRebuild, or a selection change that alters the touched-line set (core/check-update-action.ts:19-42). A throwing handler loses only its own output for that node or line (runIsolated, inline-formatting-plugin.ts:76-91). All 10 handler files and the three top-level files were read in full, plus the core, parser and widget modules they call.
maps.data_flow: Reads: state.doc slices and syntaxTree nodes only. Writes to the document: none, except TaskCheckboxWidget's mousedown handler (widgets.ts:36-42), which dispatches a change replacing the character at pos+1 of a TaskMarker (called from simple-widget-handlers.ts:28). Output: a DecorationSet returned to the editor view. No store, IPC or file access happens in this area. Wikilink clicks are resolved later from the rendered DOM classes (wikilink-click-target.ts, outside this area).
invariants: Decorations never remove text from the document. Hidden syntax stays in the doc, and copy/cut read doc text, so hidden content is not lost by this layer.

Every Decoration.replace range must stay within one line. CodeMirror validates this when it emits DOM for ViewPlugin decorations (@codemirror/view index.js:2800-2804), not inside decorate(), so runIsolated (inline-formatting-plugin.ts:76-91) cannot catch a violation and a future multi-line replace would break the draw path. Today every replace producer is single-line; linkHandler guards its one multi-line case (markdown-link-handlers.ts:49).

TaskCheckboxWidget.pos must be the TaskMarker's from, so that '[' is at pos, the state char is at pos+1 and ']' at pos+2. This holds because any docChanged rebuilds first (check-update-action.ts:20) and eq() compares pos (widgets.ts:46-48), so a reused DOM never carries a stale pos.

Node handlers test block context by walking all ancestors (is-inside-block-context.ts:13-20). Line handlers test only resolveInner(line.from) (inline-formatting-plugin.ts:153-154). Probed with @lezer/markdown: interior lines of a list-nested or quote-nested fence resolve inside FencedCode, so code bodies are skipped. Only the opening fence line of such a block is not skipped, and it holds no wikilink or comment.

Node dedupe is by name:from across visible ranges (inline-formatting-plugin.ts:133-135); line dedupe is by line number (lines 150-151). The blockquote handler dedupes per line through the per-build scratch Map (blockquote-handler.ts:29-37).

The plugin never rebuilds on a transaction that changes only the parse tree (Language.setState). Decoration correctness therefore depends on the tree being complete when the plugin builds, which is not guaranteed in production (see the stale-parse finding).
CodeMirror ViewPlugin decorations are typed as dynamic functions, so the line-crossing check at @codemirror/view index.js:3450-3458 applies to this plugin.

maps.summary: Widget classes for the live-preview editor. widgets.ts holds the task checkbox, list markers, image/media/embed widgets, the table widget with +col/+row buttons, the meta-bind select/text/toggle widgets, and the shared dispatchMetaBindUpdate frontmatter writer. widgets/ holds the code-block language switcher and copy button, math, mermaid, and the meta-bind button. Block widgets are built by plugins (table-field.ts, code-block-field.ts, meta-bind-input-plugin.ts, inline simple-widget-handlers.ts, image-plugin.ts). Only four widgets write to the document: TaskCheckboxWidget (rewrites the 1-char state at a captured pos), TableWidget (+col/+row rewrites the whole table range from a parsed-then-re-rendered model), CodeBlockWidget (rewrites the fence info string at a captured languageRange), and the meta-bind writers (dispatchMetaBindUpdate re-reads the live doc and rewrites the whole frontmatter via yaml). Each write dispatches into the single EditorView, and editor autosave persists it. Read-only audit: no tests or builds were run, and browser and library behaviour was checked against node_modules source only.
maps.data_flow: Note bytes enter widgets only through the CodeMirror doc. Plugins parse the doc (Lezer tree plus parsers/*.ts) and attach widgets that hold captured copies of positions and parsed cell text. A click or change event calls view.dispatch with changes computed from those captures. TaskCheckbox writes pos+1..pos+2. CodeBlock writes languageFrom..languageTo (or openFenceTo). TableWidget writes table.from..table.to with renderTableSource(headers, alignments, rows). Its cells are raw source slices (parsers/table.ts:92) passed through cellEscape (widgets.ts:490), and its rows are normalized to header width (parsers/table.ts:143). dispatchMetaBindUpdate reads view.state.doc, parses the frontmatter with the yaml-based properties.logic, drops nested maps and comments, re-serializes with serializeProperties, and replaces [0, frontmatterEnd). Editor autosave then writes the doc to disk (CLAUDE.md: 500 ms debounce for frontmatter edits). The properties-panel writer (frontmatter-write.service.ts:95-159) is the only path that calls detectLossyFrontmatter before rewriting. The widget path does not.
invariants: Widget dispatches use positions captured at toDOM time. This is safe only because every block decorator rebuilds on docChanged (core/block-decorator.ts:82 via core/check-update-action.ts:20) and because eq() compares each captured position (TaskCheckboxWidget.eq widgets.ts:46; TableWidget.eq widgets.ts:382-387; CodeBlockWidget.eq code-block-widget.ts:126-139). Dropping any of these lets a stale pos or range write into the wrong text.

dispatchMetaBindUpdate assumes the frontmatter is exactly the slice [0, doc.length - body.length) and that rebuildContent round-trips every key. Both fail for nested maps, comments, duplicate keys and unsafe integers (findings 2 and 5).

TableWidget assumes parse-then-render of cell text is the identity. It is not: raw cell text is re-escaped (finding 1), cells beyond the header are dropped (finding 2), and container prefixes outside the Table node range are deleted (finding 3).

A single EditorView is reused across tabs (MarkdownEditor.svelte:131 and the tab-switch effect). Any async callback that keeps a reference to `view` can write into a different note than the one it was created for (finding 7).

Interactive controls stop mousedown propagation so CodeMirror does not reveal the line under the pointer (table buttons widgets.ts:419-438, meta-bind inputs widgets.ts:696-698 and 940, code-block select code-block-widget.ts:162). TaskCheckbox calls preventDefault, and CM's eventBelongsToEditor (node_modules/@codemirror/view/dist/index.js:4921-4930) then ignores the event, so that path is fine.

Meta-bind text inputs write only on blur or Enter (widgets.ts:931-944). MetaBindTextInputWidget has no destroy() hook, so a reveal that removes the focused input discards the pending value (finding 4).

maps.summary: src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/parsers/ holds 18 pure finder modules that turn the CodeMirror doc (Lezer GFM/math tree for fences, tables, blockquotes, callouts, math, links; line regex for comments, frontmatter, media, footnotes, meta-bind INPUT, wikilink embeds) into ranges and models. Plugins (plugins/*-field.ts, via blockDecorator) turn those ranges into replace/hide decorations and widgets. Four widget paths write back to the note using parser output: CodeBlockWidget language select (languageFrom/languageTo), TableWidget +col/+row (whole-table model rewrite over sourceRange), CalloutTypeSwitcher (typeFrom/typeTo), and meta-bind (frontmatter rewrite, not parser-driven). embed-resolver.logic.ts is read-only extraction for embed widgets (widgets.ts:561-578). code-highlight.logic.ts is lowlight to escaped HTML for the code-block widget display only. Cursor-reveal (revealPredicate) decides whether a block shows as source.
maps.data_flow: Read path: note text lives in the CodeMirror doc; the Lezer tree (syntaxTree) or per-line regex produces ranges (parsers/*.ts); plugins build decorations (plugins/code-block-field.ts:19-89, table-field.ts:14-50, video-plugin.ts:12-45, frontmatter-field.ts:12-25); widgets render DOM (widgets/code-block-widget.ts:67-124, widgets.ts:322-372). Embed path: host.readNote(disk) -> embed-resolver extractors -> text in a read-only widget (widgets.ts:561-578). Write path 1: CodeBlockWidget.dispatchLanguageChange replaces [languageFrom, languageTo) (code-block-widget.ts:170-181) with the value from findAllFencedCodeBlocks (fenced-code-block.ts:59-62). Write path 2: TableWidget +col/+row rebuilds the model with renderTableSource and replaces [sourceRange.from, sourceRange.to) (widgets.ts:448-482), where the model is parsers/table.ts raw cell text (table.ts:84-113) run through normalizeRow (table.ts:54-58). Write path 3: callout type switch replaces [typeFrom, typeTo) computed from the header line (plugins/callout-field.ts:200-214, 85-87). Non-parser write: meta-bind frontmatter rewrite (widgets.ts:754-769).
invariants: A range used as a write target covers exactly the bytes being replaced. languageFrom..languageTo must span only the language token, but Lezer CodeInfo is the whole info string (node_modules/@lezer/markdown/dist/index.js:463-465), so attributes after the language are inside the replaced range.

The table model holds raw source cell text (escapes kept), so a rewrite must not re-escape it. renderTableSource expects unescaped cells (widgets.ts:486-503; test table-widget.test.ts:35-38 'escapes | in cell content'). These two contracts conflict.

sourceRange covers only the table's own lines. Lezer Table.from/to spans container prefixes (a '> ' or list indent on rows 2+), so a rewrite removes them (verified: Table 2-51 for a blockquoted table, rows 2+ include '> ').
Models are lossy (normalizeRow truncates excess cells; extractCells merges across an unclosed [[). Rewrites built from the model are therefore lossy; nothing checks the rewrite against the source.

TableWidget.eq must cover every field the click handlers read. It omits alignments (widgets.ts:374-392), and CodeMirror reuses the old DOM and its handlers when eq is true (node_modules/@codemirror/view/dist/index.js:2617-2619).

Line-regex finders assume column-0 fences (mermaid/queryjs/collection/meta-bind-button regexes anchor ^), LF line endings (embed-resolver heading regex), and that closing '---' lines are exact (frontmatter.ts:10) while frontmatter-slice.ts:16 uses startsWith.
Callout type text length equals the lower-cased type length (callout.logic.ts:31), so typeTo = typeFrom + type.length is exact.
Code-block highlight escapes text (code-highlight.logic.ts:9,14); DOMPurify then restricts output to span/class (code-block-widget.ts:114-118). Checked, no bug.

maps.area: doc-mutating-handlers (live-preview paste handlers, click/wikilink navigation, meta-bind input/button writers)
maps.summary: Read-only audit of the live-preview paste handlers (paste-html-link, paste-tsv), the link click handlers (click-handler.ts, wikilink-navigation.ts, MarkdownEditor capture hook), and the meta-bind writers (meta-bind-input-plugin, meta-bind-button-field, meta-bind-button widget and logic, meta-bind-input parser). Paste handlers insert converted text into the single CodeMirror doc. Meta-bind select, toggle, number/date and button updateMetadata writes go through dispatchMetaBindUpdate (widgets.ts:754-768), which re-serializes the whole frontmatter from parseFrontmatterProperties. The button runs its actions in sequence against one shared EditorView, and open/createNote actions switch that view to another note. Link clicks navigate through the EditorHost (app/editor-host.ts) to openFileInEditor / openOrCreateNote, which never overwrite an existing file. Pure paste logic was replayed with node and jsdom (read-only, no files written). The app was not run.
maps.data_flow: Paste: clipboard text/html and text/plain -> pasteHtmlLinkHandler (paste-html-link-handler.ts:21-45) returns converted text or null; if null, pasteTsvHandler (paste-tsv-handler.ts:18-41) runs; a hit is one transaction replacing only state.selection.main (userEvent input.paste) -> updateListener (editor-extensions.ts:184-190) -> onDocChanged -> editorStore.updateContent -> autosave 2000 ms body / 500 ms frontmatter (editor.service.ts:197-219; saveDirtyTabs writes every dirty tab). Link click: Cmd/Ctrl mousedown on .cm-lp-link -> isSafeUrl -> host.openExternal (click-handler.ts:16-40). Wikilink click: MarkdownEditor capture mousedown (MarkdownEditor.svelte:65-82) -> followWikilinkClick (wikilink-navigation.ts:29-53) -> same-note heading via view.dispatch, else followWikilink -> host.resolveLink / openLink (openFileInEditor) / createNote (openOrCreateNote, which checks exists() and never overwrites). Meta-bind writer: widget event -> dispatchMetaBindUpdate(view, key, value): refuse only if isFrontmatterUnparseable; parseFrontmatterProperties; setPropertyByBindTarget; rebuildContent; view.dispatch replacing [0, frontmatterEnd) -> fmChanged -> 500 ms save. Button click: meta-bind-button-widget.ts:30-37 runs getButtonActions in order with one shared view; updateMetadata calls dispatchMetaBindUpdate(view); open/createNote go through host and can switch the active tab.
invariants: MarkdownEditor creates one EditorView for its lifetime (MarkdownEditor.svelte:131) and swaps tabs by replacing its document in an $effect (MarkdownEditor.svelte:170-230). Any closure that captured `view` and later reads view.state.doc sees whichever note is open at that moment. The button action loop assumes the note does not change between actions, which does not hold for open/createNote.

dispatchMetaBindUpdate is the only frontmatter writer for these widgets. It rebuilds the whole block from Property[], so every construct parseFrontmatterProperties drops is lost on write. Its only guard is isFrontmatterUnparseable (widgets.ts:756). The Properties panel also refuses detectLossyFrontmatter cases (frontmatter-write.service.ts:121-122).
FRONTMATTER_REGEX (properties.logic.ts:37) needs at least one line between the two `---` delimiters, so `---\n---` is not a frontmatter block.
Paste handlers and widget dispatches bypass CodeMirror's read-only check. No readOnly or editable configuration exists under src/lib (grep found none), so this is latent today.

openOrCreateNote checks exists() before create (note-creator.service.ts:86-103); Rust create_note refuses an existing path (vault.rs:896-898); path traversal is rejected by resolveFilePath (utils/path.ts:33-45) and ensure_safe_write_path (vault.rs:862-874). Button and wikilink createNote therefore cannot overwrite a note.
Autosave saves every dirty tab (editor.service.ts:197-200), so switching tabs from a link click does not discard unsaved text in the previous tab.
Number and toggle meta-bind writes are intentionally serialized as quoted strings (meta-bind-writers.test.ts:113-117, 'meta-bind writes every value as a string'). Not reported as a bug.
handleLivePreviewLinkMousedown only opens URLs that pass isSafeUrl (click-handler.ts:33).
