maps.summary: Read-only audit of the non-test note writers outside the core note-change owner: auto-move (debounced rule evaluation after save, then moveItem and an icon write), type-definitions (type create/rename, .view YAML writes), file-icons (frontmatter icon writes through updateNoteFrontmatter, folder-note placeholder, recent-icons JSON), tasks (toggleTask via Rust toggle_task_status, Todoist sent-task JSON), deep-link and app/deep-link-actions (kokobrain:// new/append/prepend/overwrite/silent, daily, capture), and templates (template scaffolding and create-from-template via openOrCreateNote). Most paths route through applyNoteChange/notifyAfterSave and the frontmatter owner correctly. The main defects are in the URL-driven and task-toggle writers: a silent new overwrites an existing note, several read-from-disk writers overwrite a dirty open tab with the disk version (markSaved=true), prepend places text above the frontmatter, and path resolution lets the vault root map to a sibling "<Vault>.md". Not verified by execution (read-only, no tests run): processTemplate YAML output for the capture finding, the stale-line timing in the task toggle finding, and the link-updater side effects of auto-move moves.
maps.data_flow: Editor save calls notifyAfterSave (editor.hooks.ts:67-92), which runs the after-save observers, including auto-move (debounce 3 s from settings.store.svelte.ts:104). That leads to evaluateAndMove (auto-move.service.ts:150-213), then moveItem and applyPathChange (path-change.service.ts:117-171), which renames on disk and updates tabs; then setIconForPath calls updateNoteFrontmatter (frontmatter-write.service.ts:95-159). For an open tab that patches and saves the tab; for a closed note it reads, rebuilds, writes with create:false, then calls notifyAfterSave. Deep links: onOpenUrl/getCurrent feed enqueueDeepLinkUrl, a serial queue (deep-link.service.ts:23-33), then resolveAndDispatch, then executeAction, which dispatches to executeNewAction, executeDailyAction or executeCaptureAction. Those read disk, write disk, then call syncExternalContentToEditor(path, content, markSaved=true) and notifyAfterSave. Task checkbox: TasksView calls toggleTask, which calls Rust toggle_task_status (reads disk, flips the marker, write_atomic), then syncs the disk content into the tab with markSaved=true. Type rename: renameItem on the definition, then a raw writeTextFile of each dirty tab's rewritten content plus applyNoteChange, then Rust propagate_type_rename for the rest of the vault. Templates: create-from-template goes through openOrCreateNote, which opens existing files and never overwrites; ensureTemplatesFolder writes empty placeholders only when missing.
invariants: A read-modify-write that reads note bytes from disk (not from the tab) must not be synced into a dirty tab with markSaved=true. reloadExternallyChangedTabs skips dirty tabs ("the editor always wins", editor.service.ts:370-373). toggleTask and deep-link/daily append/prepend break this.
Frontmatter is only recognized at byte 0 (properties.logic.ts:37 anchored regex, :44-47). A writer that inserts text before it detaches the properties.
Open-or-create writers must not overwrite an existing note (note-creator.service.ts:86-89 returns early when the file exists). The deep-link silent branch does not follow this.
Resolved note paths must stay strictly inside the vault. resolveFilePath (utils/path.ts:33-53) accepts the vault root itself and then appends '.md'.

Writers that parse and rebuild frontmatter should check detectLossyFrontmatter first. auto-move and frontmatter-write do; deep-link capture injection (injectTitleIntoContent / injectTagsIntoContent) does not.
updateNoteFrontmatter callers must serialize writes per path (frontmatter-write.service.ts:91-93). Concurrency between auto-move icon writes and the icon picker on the same note was not verified.
Byte-changing writes route through applyNoteChange / notifyAfterSave (raw-write-ratchet.test.ts). The ratchet reasons do not cover overwrite semantics.
The deep-link pending action is a single slot (deep-link.store.svelte.ts:18-20), consumed once per vault init.
Type names are written unquoted into _type: lines (type-definitions.service.ts:73, type-definitions.logic.ts:206).

maps.area: other-writers-creators: note-creator, periodic-notes, quick-capture, kanban, one-on-one, plus the deep-link writers that dispatch into open tabs (app/deep-link-actions.ts, features/deep-link/deep-link.service.ts) and the tasks toggle that syncs into tabs
maps.summary: Read-only audit. Note creation goes through core/note-creator/note-creator.service.ts openOrCreateNote (exists check, then Rust create_note, then template via processTemplate and optional buildContent, then markRecentSave, applyNoteChange 'create', open tab). Periodic notes, quick-capture composer and one-on-one all call openOrCreateNote with different paths/templates; no data-loss path found in them. Kanban writes only through the active editor tab (KanbanView applyChange -> onContentChange -> 2 s autosave). The real risks are the disk-based writers that push results into an open tab with markSaved=true: deep-link append/prepend/daily (deep-link.service.ts:254-289, app/deep-link-actions.ts:54-63) and tasks.toggleTask (tasks.service.ts:100-116). They read disk, not the tab, and syncExternalContentToEditor(..., true, 'none') overwrites unsaved typed text in both the store and the CodeMirror doc. The same file has a silent-create branch that overwrites an existing note (deep-link.service.ts:308-315). Kanban's parser discards every line it does not model, so the first board mutation rewrites the file without the user's other text. Not checked: Rust create_note/toggle_task internals beyond the disk read/write lines; TasksView UI wiring beyond the call site; Tauri capability scopes; no tests were run (read-only).
maps.data_flow: Editor keystrokes: editor.service.onContentChange -> editorStore.updateContent (active tab content only) -> debouncedSave 2000 ms (editor.service.ts:197) -> saveFileByPath (writeTextFile of tab.content, markSavedByPath, notifyAfterSave). New notes: loadNoteTemplate (note-creator.service.ts:49-64, processTemplate on template file or inline text) -> optional buildContent (one-on-one ensureFrontmatterLink) -> Rust call('create_note') -> markRecentSave -> applyNoteChange 'create' -> openFileInEditor. Deep-link writes (deep-link.service.ts:243-323, deep-link-actions.ts:31-178): read disk, compute new text, writeTextFile, then syncExternalContentToEditor(path, text, markSaved=true), which calls editorStore.updateTabContentByPath (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136, sets content and savedContent to the same text) and bumps externalContentSignal, which makes MarkdownEditor replace the whole doc. Capture: renderCaptureBody + per-kind template (processTemplate on the template file only) + injectTitle/injectTags (deep-link.logic.ts:385-455, which rebuild frontmatter via parseFrontmatterProperties/rebuildContent) -> writeTextFile to a unique new path -> notifyAfterSave. Tasks: Rust toggle_task_status reads disk (src-tauri vault.rs:669-670), writes disk (:683), returns full text; tasks.service.toggleTask syncs it into the tab with markSaved=true. Kanban: KanbanView.applyChange (KanbanView.svelte:70-91) serializes the in-memory board and calls onContentChange (EditorView.svelte:79), so writes go through the tab and the normal autosave.
invariants: A dirty open tab (content !== savedContent) holds the user's newest text. Any writer that touches disk for that path must build its new content from tab.content, as link-updater.service.ts:33-35 does, or must not overwrite. reloadExternallyChangedTabs (editor.service.ts:368-374, 380) states the same rule for watcher events ('editor always wins'). Deep-link append/prepend/daily and tasks.toggleTask break it.
syncExternalContentToEditor(..., markSaved=true) assumes the written text is the whole truth of the file. It is only safe when the tab is clean or the text was built from the tab.

writeTextFile overwrites by default (node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-fs/dist-js/index.js:763: 'creating a new file if needed, else overwriting'), so every writer must check exists itself. openOrCreateNote relies on create_note refusing existing paths (fs.logic.ts:218 comment) for its non-atomic exists-then-create.
buildContent runs before create_note, so a throw leaves no file (note-creator.service.ts:100-103).
The kanban round trip assumes the .kanban file holds only lanes, '- [ ]/[x]' items, the '---' archive, and a settings block. Anything else is dropped on the first mutation (kanban.logic.ts:54-106).
processTemplate is safe only for trusted template files; applying it to note content rewrites every <% %> (template.ts:22, 188-215).

Quick-capture and deep-link capture run on two different queues (quick-capture.service.ts:53 vs deep-link.service.ts:23). resolveUniqueCapturePath's exists-then-write is only race-free within one queue. Default filenameFormat has milliseconds (settings.store.svelte.ts:35), so this was judged practically unreachable and not reported.

findings.title: Undo after a tab switch re-inserts text deleted in the previous note, and autosaves it
findings.scenario: 1) Open note A (markdown) and press Backspace once: the character is deleted and the undo history stores an inverse insert of that character. 2) Click the tab of note B (also markdown). The tab-switch effect dispatches a full-document replace with addToHistory(false) (MarkdownEditor.svelte:230-235). The EditorView and its history() stay mounted, so the history is not cleared; CodeMirror maps the pending undo entry through the replacement (commands index.js:240-241, state index.js:1084-1150, which keeps inserted text of the mapped change). 3) Without typing in B, press Cmd+Z. Undo replays A's entry on B's document, inserting the deleted character into B. 4) The undo is an ordinary user transaction, so the update listener calls onDocChanged (editor-extensions.ts:171-188) -> onContentChange -> updateContent on B -> the 2 s auto-save writes B to disk (editor.service.ts:224-227, 196-200). Result: foreign text in note B, saved silently. The same mapping applies to the external-content replace at MarkdownEditor.svelte:329-334, so an undo in the same note after a deletion followed by a Properties/task/link write can reinsert the deleted text at a boundary of the document; I read this path but did not run it. Typed-character undo entries are dropped by addMappingToBranch (commands index.js:460-478) when mapped, so the trigger is deletion-type edits (Backspace, Delete, cut, a word delete).
findings.evidence:
Run with the repo's installed packages (Node, ESM, no file writes): state with 'Alpha bxeta note A text' -> user delete of 'x' (userEvent delete.backward) -> A = 'Alpha beta note A text' -> full-doc replace to '# Note B

Unrelated body of note B.' with Transaction.addToHistory.of(false) (the same annotation as MarkdownEditor.svelte:233) -> undo({state, dispatch}) returned true and produced '# Note B

Unrelated body of note B.x'. Mapping code: commands index.js:240-241 (addToHistory false -> state.addMapping(tr.changes.desc)), 460-478 (addMappingToBranch), 479-487 (mapEvent uses event.changes.map(mapping)); state index.js:1084-1150 (mapSet keeps the inserted text of a change that falls inside the replaced range). No override of Mod-z exists in src/lib (grep for undo/historyField/isolateHistory found only the canvas history and a calendar command). CodeMirror versions: @codemirror/commands 6.11.1, @codemirror/state 6.7.6.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F84: one shared history() survives the full-doc replace that uses addToHistory(false) (MarkdownEditor.svelte:230-235, :329-334; commands dist/index.js:240-241, 460-486). The undo is then persisted through editor-extensions.ts:171-188 and editor.service.ts:224-227. I confirmed it with an in-memory repro using the repo's CodeMirror packages.

findings.title: Toggling a task from the Tasks tab overwrites the unsaved text of that note
findings.scenario: 1) Type in note A, then within the 2 s auto-save window (debounce restarts on every keystroke, editor.service.ts:197, debounce.ts:9-17) switch to the Tasks tab. switchTab only sets the index and does not flush (editor.service.ts:250-255). 2) Click a checkbox in the Tasks view for a task in note A. toggleTask calls toggle_task_status, and Rust reads the file from disk (vault.rs:669 std::fs::read_to_string), toggles the line, writes it, and returns the disk-based text (vault.rs:683-688). 3) tasks.service.ts:114 calls syncExternalContentToEditor(A, updatedContent, true, 'none'). With markSaved=true, updateTabContentByPath sets both content and savedContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136), so the unsaved characters are removed from the store and the tab is clean. If A is active the content-sync effect replaces the CodeMirror document too (MarkdownEditor.svelte:311-337). 4) The pending debounced save finds no dirty tab (editor.service.ts:183-187) and writes nothing. When the user returns to A, the typed text is gone from the screen, the store and the disk. Same pattern: deep-link.service.ts:255-262 (append and prepend read from disk), :275-281 and :298 (overwrite replaces content), and deep-link-actions.ts:53-63 (daily note: read from disk, write, markSaved=true) lose the unsaved text of an open dirty tab the same way. The window is narrow for the task toggle (about 2 s after the last keystroke, or as long as a save keeps failing with the 5 s retry at editor.service.ts:180-194), but the loss is permanent and silent. Callers that compute from tab.content (link-updater.service.ts:30-47, type-definitions.service.ts:206-220, frontmatter-write.service.ts:115-156) avoid it.
findings.evidence: tasks.service.ts:102-114: call('toggle_task_status') -> updatedContent from the Rust result -> syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, updatedContent, true, 'none') (comment says 'Rust already wrote the toggled line to disk'). vault.rs:669-671 reads the disk file, and vault.rs:683 writes the toggled disk text. editor.service.ts:78-82: markSaved -> updateTabContentByPath. editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136: sets tab.content and tab.savedContent. editor.service.ts:250-255: switchTab does not flush. editor.service.ts:183-187: saveDirtyTabs filters by isTabDirty, which is content !== savedContent (editor.logic.ts:44-46). EditorView.svelte:70-71: the Tasks tab replaces the markdown editor, so the document is not mounted when the toggle runs.

It never checks isTabDirty, never reads tab.content and never flushes a save first. Rust toggle_task_status_inner (src-tauri/src/commands/vault.rs:669) builds its result from std::fs::read_to_string(path), writes it with write_atomic (:683) and returns it (:686-688). syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true) (src/lib/core/editor/editor.service.ts:78-79) calls updateTabContentByPath, which sets both tab.content and tab.savedContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136). The tab then reads clean. saveDirtyTabs filters on isTabDirty (editor.service.ts:183-187), so the armed 2 s debounce writes nothing, and 'none' arms no timer (:213-221). No flush path covers this. switchTab only calls setActiveIndex (:250-255). MarkdownEditor onDestroy only saves scroll and cursor state (MarkdownEditor.svelte:147-165). The only saveFileByPath / saveAllDirtyTabs callers are frontmatter-write, event-calendar, vault switch, app close and lifecycle. The Tasks tab replaces the editor (EditorView.svelte:70-71), and TasksView.svelte:67 is the only caller of toggleTask. If the note is the active tab when you return, the tab-switch effect loads the replaced tab.content, and the external sync uses addToHistory(false) (MarkdownEditor.svelte:328-333), so undo cannot bring the text back. Refutation attempt: the global debounce still fires 2 s after the last keystroke even after the switch to Tasks, because nothing cancels it. So the loss needs the checkbox click within about 2 s of the last keystroke, or a save that is failing and retrying every 5 s (:189-193). That limits the window, but the path is still reachable from real UI actions. The existing test (src/tests/lib/features/tasks/tasks.service.test.ts:192-201) only covers a clean tab.
verification.repro: Vitest with the real editorStore: mock call('toggle_task_status') to return {updatedContent: '- [x] task', updateResult: {changed: true}}. Then editorStore.addTab({path: '/v/a.md', name: 'a.md', content: '- [ ] task\nunsaved para', savedContent: '- [ ] task'}). await toggleTask('/v/a.md', 1). Expect editorStore.tabs[0].content to contain 'unsaved para'. Today it fails: content === savedContent === '- [x] task'. Manual: type a line in a note that has a task, switch to the Tasks tab and tick that note's task within 2 s, then go back. The line is gone.

findings.title: Watcher reload overwrites keystrokes typed while the disk read is in flight
findings.scenario: A clean note A is open and is changed on disk by something outside the app (the watcher then calls reloadExternallyChangedTabs). The tab is clean when the function selects it (editor.service.ts:378-381), then it awaits Promise.allSettled of readTextFile (385-387). If the user types into A during that IPC read, the tab becomes dirty, but the re-check after the read (395-399) only tests that the tab exists and that diskContent !== savedContent, not that it is still clean. syncExternalContentToEditor(A, diskContent, true, 'none') then replaces the store text and savedContent and, for the active tab, the CodeMirror document (MarkdownEditor.svelte:311-337), so the keystrokes typed in the window are lost. The window is the duration of one readTextFile IPC per changed file, so this is rare; the fix is one isTabDirty check in the re-check.
findings.evidence: editor.service.ts:378-381 checks isTabDirty only before the awaits; 395-399 re-checks only tab existence and diskContent === tab.savedContent, then calls syncExternalContentToEditor with markSaved=true at 401. updateTabContentByPath (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136) overwrites content. The content-sync effect (MarkdownEditor.svelte:311-337) replaces the document from activeTab.content.

verification.reasoning: I tried to refute this and could not. reloadExternallyChangedTabs checks isTabDirty only before the await (editor.service.ts:380). It then awaits Promise.allSettled of readTextFile IPCs (385-387), and that await yields to the event loop. A keystroke in that window goes MarkdownEditor onDocChanged (MarkdownEditor.svelte:124) -> onContentChange (editor.service.ts:224-226) -> editorStore.updateContent, so tab.content changes synchronously. After the await, the comment at :396 promises a re-check, but :398 only tests `!tab || diskContent === tab.savedContent`. It never tests isTabDirty. :401 calls syncExternalContentToEditor(path, disk, true, 'none'), which goes to updateTabContentByPath (sets content and savedContent, so the tab reads clean) and bumps the signal for the active tab (editor.service.ts:76-88). The MarkdownEditor effect (MarkdownEditor.svelte:311-337) then replaces the whole doc with Transaction.addToHistory.of(false), so Cmd+Z cannot bring the text back. The 'none' schedule arms no save, and the 2 s timer armed by the keystroke later finds the tab clean (saveDirtyTabs editor.service.ts:183-186). Nothing upstream prevents this: runWatcherBatch (app-lifecycle.service.ts:481-488) calls it with no guard. No test covers dirtiness during the read. The tests around editor.service.test.ts:1150 cover only dirty-before-call. The window is the read IPC time. It gets longer with several eligible tabs or a slow iCloud-evicted file.
verification.repro: vitest: addTab('/vault/n.md','old',{savedContent:'old'}); let resolveRead; vi.mocked(readTextFile).mockImplementationOnce(()=>new Promise(r=>resolveRead=r)); const p=reloadExternallyChangedTabs(['/vault/n.md']); onContentChange('old typed'); resolveRead('disk v2'); await p; expect(editorStore.tabs[0].content).toBe('old typed') -> fails (content is 'disk v2', savedContent 'disk v2').
verification.fix_hint: At editor.service.ts:398 also skip when isTabDirty(tab) (the tab became dirty during the read). Optionally also skip when tab.savedContent changed since eligibility.

findings.title: Async language load lands on whichever note is open when it resolves
findings.scenario: Open a code file (for example foo.ts, which is rendered by this same MarkdownEditor) whose language parser has not loaded yet. The tab-switch effect takes the async path (langEffects === null, MarkdownEditor.svelte:241-243), which calls applyLanguageForTab, awaits getLanguageEffects (which awaits langDesc.load(), highlight-styles.ts:127-128), and then dispatches to the shared view without checking which tab is now shown (line 62). If the user switches to a markdown note before the load resolves, the TypeScript parser and code highlight are applied to that note. Live-preview decorations derived from the markdown syntax tree then go missing, and stay wrong until the next switch to a markdown tab (the sync branch at 223 re-applies markdown effects). Two code tabs switched quickly can end with the wrong grammar, because the earlier load can resolve last. The document text is not changed. The window is the first load of each language, so it is narrow.
findings.evidence: applyLanguageForTab (59-63) captures tab.name but not the tab identity, and dispatches to the mutable view. getLanguageEffects (highlight-styles.ts:120-133) returns a Promise for non-markdown files. The sync-effects branch (MarkdownEditor.svelte:223) re-applies markdown effects only when the next tab is markdown or kanban.

verification.reasoning: I could not refute it. applyLanguageForTab (MarkdownEditor.svelte:59-63) awaits getLanguageEffects and then calls view.dispatch({ effects }) on the shared view. Nothing checks that editorStore.activeTab is still the tab it was called for. The tab-switch effect calls it without await and without a token (241-243). The only abort controller guards the rAF chain (247-257), not this call. getLanguageEffects awaits langDesc.load() (highlight-styles.ts:127-128). LanguageDescription.load() caches its promise (@codemirror/language dist index.js:738), so after the first load the await settles in a microtask, which a user tab switch cannot beat. The real window is the first dynamic import of each language. A markdown tab installs its language in the same doc-replace dispatch (223-235), so a late TypeScript or Python reconfigure lands after it and overrides it. The note keeps the code grammar until the next tab switch. The text is not touched: these effects only reconfigure compartments. The onMount call (133) has the same shape.
verification.repro: Vitest with jsdom: mount MarkdownEditor with tabs [a.ts, b.md], active a.ts. Make the ts LanguageDescription.load a deferred promise. Switch to b.md, then resolve the deferred. Assert that view.state.facet(language) is the markdown language. Today it is the TypeScript language.
verification.fix_hint: Capture the tab path or a counter before the await. Dispatch only when the view still shows that path (editorStore.activeTabPath === path or lastTabPath === path), or reuse an AbortController the way the rAF chain does.

findings.title: Canvas unmount flush writes canvas JSON into whichever tab is active, corrupting another note
findings.scenario: Open canvas Plan.canvas and note N.md. Drag a node or edit node text in the canvas, then within 300 ms click the N.md tab (or close the canvas tab, or open another file from the sidebar). switchTab sets activeIndex to N.md synchronously. EditorView's {#if} then destroys CanvasView, and CanvasInner.onDestroy sees pendingPersist===true and calls persistChanges -> onJsonChange(canvasJson) -> onContentChange -> store.updateContent, which writes tabs[activeIndex] (now N.md). N.md becomes dirty and the 2 s body autosave writes the canvas JSON over N.md on disk. If the new tab is another canvas, that canvas is overwritten and then shows the wrong nodes. The same path runs for closeTab / closeTabsForDeletedPath (removeTab shifts activeIndex) and openFileInEditor (addTab makes the new tab active). pendingPersist is set by any change to nodes and is only cleared by the 300 ms timer (CanvasInner.svelte:219-223); persistChanges does not clear it, so it stays armed after drag-stop reassignments (lines 127, 143).
findings.evidence: CanvasInner.svelte:219 sets pendingPersist=true on every nodes change; :231-233 onDestroy calls persistChanges when it is true; :105-109 persistWithoutHistory calls onJsonChange(json) with no check of which tab is active. EditorView.svelte:81 wires onJsonChange={onContentChange}. editor.service.ts:224-227 onContentChange -> editorStore.updateContent (no tab identity check) and scheduleAutoSave('body'). editor.store.svelte.ts:83-88 writes tabs[activeIndex].content. switchTab (250-252) changes activeIndex before the view is torn down. Not verified: the exact Svelte 5 ordering of destroy versus the new branch's mount, and whether file-history keeps the pre-corruption bytes.

verification.reasoning:
I tried to refute it and could not. The flush has no tab identity at any step. CanvasInner.svelte:212-226 sets pendingPersist=true on every non-sync change to `nodes`, and only the 300 ms callback clears it (:223). onDestroy at :230-234 calls persistChanges -> persistWithoutHistory (:104-108) -> onJsonChange(json). EditorView.svelte:81 wires onJsonChange={onContentChange}. onContentChange (editor.service.ts:224-227) calls editorStore.updateContent(content) with no path, then scheduleAutoSave('body'). updateContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88) writes tabs[activeIndex].content.

Ordering: CanvasView is torn down only because isCanvasTab, derived from activeTab (EditorView.svelte:36,80), flipped. So activeIndex already points at the new tab whenever onDestroy runs. This holds on both the sync and the transition path of Svelte 5.57.2 BranchManager#commit (branches.js:131-161). setActiveIndex and removeTab (store:64-81) are synchronous. switchTab (service:250-252) and closeTab both reach them: a clean canvas tab skips the dirty prompt at :270-278 and goes straight to removeTab at :285, so the neighbour becomes active. openFileInEditor reaches them through setActiveIndex or addTab (:116, :140).

The new MarkdownEditor's onMount (MarkdownEditor.svelte:99-108) runs as a user effect after the old branch is destroyed, so it loads the JSON as a fresh doc with no undo history. saveDirtyTabs (service:183-194) then writes the JSON to the note 2 s later through saveFileByPath (:161-178). The canvas's own last edit is lost as well.

Triggers, all confirmed: a TextNode keystroke (TextNode.svelte:40 updateNodeData), and node selection on mousedown (xyflow store/index.js addSelectedNodes reassigns store.nodes, which flows back through bind:nodes, SvelteFlow.svelte:72-88). Likely but timing-dependent: measurement right after mount (NodeWrapper.svelte:134-148 rAF -> updateNodeInternals -> store.nodes = ..., store/index.js:46), which would arm the flag with no user edit.

Coverage: no unit test covers this. The only canvas e2e spec (e2e/specs/canvas-view.spec.ts) tests only the source toggle, where activeIndex does not change. The flush came from c3ab02d4, which targeted quit only.
verification.repro: E2E: seed Board.canvas (one text node) and Note.md ('original'). Open both, activate Board. Double-click the text node and type 'x'. Within 100 ms press Cmd+Shift+] (or click the Note.md tab, or Cmd+W on Board). Assert .cm-content does not contain '"nodes"', then wait 2.5 s and assert that the mock fs content of Note.md is still 'original' (it will be canvas JSON). Vitest variant: mount EditorView with a real editorStore holding a canvas tab and a markdown tab, call updateNodeData via the TextNode input, then editorStore.setActiveIndex(1), flushSync(), and assert tabs[1].content is unchanged.
verification.fix_hint: Bind the flush to the canvas tab's path. Capture the path at mount, or pass a path-bound callback from EditorView (e.g. onJsonChange={(json) => updateContentByPath(tab.path, json)}), and use editorStore.updateTabContentByPath-style writes that keep the dirty state. Clear pendingPersist inside persistChanges too. Add a vitest that switches tabs inside the 300 ms window.

findings.title: Tasks toggle replaces a dirty tab's unsaved text with the disk version
findings.scenario: Open note N.md and type a paragraph. Before the 2 s autosave fires, open the Tasks tab (a virtual tab) and tick a task that lives in N.md. toggle_task_status reads N.md from disk (vault.rs:669), toggles the line, and writes it back. The disk copy never had the paragraph. tasks.service then calls syncExternalContentToEditor(path, updatedContent, true, 'none'), which sets content and savedContent to the disk-derived text. The tab is clean, so the autosave timer finds nothing to save, and the paragraph is gone from both the store and the editor and was never written.

There is no isTabDirty check in toggleTask.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause and same path as F2: tasks.service.ts:114 syncs disk-derived text with markSaved=true, and no dirty check exists.
verification.repro: See F2.
verification.fix_hint: See F2.

findings.title: Deep-link and daily-note append/prepend discard unsaved edits in the open tab
findings.scenario: Type in N.md, then within 2 s receive a deep link with append or prepend (or a daily-note append) for N.md. The new content is built from readTextFile(disk), written to disk, and then synced into the tab with markSaved=true. Unsaved keystrokes are dropped from disk and from the tab, and the 2 s autosave has nothing dirty to write. The overwrite action (deep-link.service.ts:298) is an explicit replacement and is out of scope here.
findings.evidence: deep-link.service.ts:257 and :276 read disk; :262 and :281 call syncExternalContentToEditor(fullPath, newContent, true, 'none'). deep-link-actions.ts:54 reads disk, :63 syncs with markSaved=true. Compare renameType (type-definitions.service.ts:216), which builds from tab.content, and updateLinksAfterRename (link-updater.service.ts:33-37), which uses the dirty tab content.

verification.reasoning: executeNewAction prepend (src/lib/features/deep-link/deep-link.service.ts:254-262) and append (:273-281) both readTextFile(fullPath) from disk, write, then call syncExternalContentToEditor(fullPath, newContent, true, 'none'). executeDailyAction (src/lib/app/deep-link-actions.ts:37-63) first opens the daily note (openOrCreateDailyNote only opens it; periodic-notes.service.ts:64-66), then reads disk (:54), writes (:61) and syncs with markSaved=true (:63). None of these read tab.content or check isTabDirty. updateTabContentByPath sets content and savedContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136). If the tab is active, bumpExternalContentSignal makes MarkdownEditor replace the document with addToHistory(false) (MarkdownEditor.svelte:328-333), and the pending autosave then finds the tab clean. The race-audit test (src/tests/lib/features/deep-link/deep-link.service.race-audit.test.ts:131-160) sets up a dirty tab, but it mocks syncExternalContentToEditor and only asserts that it was called with markSaved=true. It passes even though 'dirty editor content' is discarded. The same condition applies: within 2 s of the last keystroke, or while a save keeps failing. It is reachable when a global capture hotkey (Shortcuts/Raycast) fires while the user is writing in the daily note. I leave overwrite out because it is an explicit replace.
verification.repro: Vitest with the real editorStore, without mocking syncExternalContentToEditor. addTab({path: '/vault/note.md', content: 'disk\ntyped', savedContent: 'disk'}), readTextFile returns 'disk', and the pending action is {type: 'new', name: 'note.md', append: true, content: 'x'}. await executePendingAction(). Expect tab.content to contain 'typed'. Today it fails: content is 'disk\nx'.
verification.fix_hint: Before the read-merge-write, flush the dirty tab with saveFileByPath and abort on failure. Alternatively, build from tab.content when the tab is open and dirty, as link-updater.service.ts:33-35 does. Strengthen the race-audit test to assert that the dirty text survives.

findings.title: Watcher reload overwrites a tab that became dirty during the disk read
findings.scenario: A clean note N.md is changed on disk by a sync tool, and the watcher calls reloadExternallyChangedTabs. Eligibility (dirty excluded) is checked before the awaited readTextFile. If the user types into N.md before the read resolves, the apply loop only checks diskContent === savedContent and never re-checks isTabDirty. It then calls updateTabContentByPath(disk), which drops the typed text from the store and the CM doc (via the signal) and clears the dirty flag, so nothing is autosaved. The window is the IPC read duration, so the trigger is narrow.
findings.evidence: editor.service.ts:378-382 is the only dirty check. Line 398 is 'if (!tab || diskContent === tab.savedContent) continue;'. Line 401 calls syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, diskContent, true, 'none').

verification.reasoning: Same root cause: no isTabDirty re-check at editor.service.ts:398 after the readTextFile await at 385-387.
verification.repro: See F3.
verification.fix_hint: See F3.

findings.title: Vault switch opens the new vault after a failed save and silently drops dirty tabs
findings.scenario: Note N.md has unsaved edits and its disk write fails (read-only file, permission error). The user picks another vault from the recent list. switchVault ignores the array returned by saveAllDirtyTabs and calls vaultStore.open. initializeVault retries the save once, then teardownVault calls resetEditor, which empties the tabs. The only signal is a toast from saveFileByPath. The window-close handler in tauri-listeners.service.ts does ask before discarding, so the two exits behave differently.
findings.evidence: vault.service.ts:19 'await saveAllDirtyTabs();' with the result unused, then :21 vaultStore.open(path). The comment at app-lifecycle.service.ts:175-179 documents that the new vault opens anyway. tauri-listeners.service.ts:55-61 prompts 'Close anyway and lose unsaved changes?'. Likelihood depends on a save failure, and the behavior is documented, so this is a consistency and data-safety concern rather than an accident.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F151: vault.service.ts:19 and app-lifecycle.service.ts:180 ignore the result of saveAllDirtyTabs, then teardownVault calls resetEditor and the tabs are wiped. One correction: 'picks another vault from the recent list' cannot happen while a vault is open. The recent list renders only when !vaultStore.isOpen (AppShell.svelte:160-161), so the trigger is a deep link.
verification.repro: See F151.

findings.title: Renaming an open .canvas to .md keeps the canvas view, so later edits overwrite the .md file
findings.scenario: Rename the open Plan.canvas to Plan.md through the explorer rename input (FilesNavigator.svelte:153 -> fs.service.ts:201-220). updateTabPath changes only path and name, so fileType stays 'canvas' and the canvas view stays mounted. Its JSON is markdown text, so parseCanvas returns an empty canvas. Adding a node persists canvas JSON through updateContent, and the 2 s autosave writes it over Plan.md.
findings.evidence: updateTabPath (store:121-127) sets path and name only. fileType is assigned only in openFileInEditor (service:135-140). EditorView.svelte:36 keys the canvas branch on fileType. parseCanvas catches non-JSON and returns an empty canvas (canvas.logic.ts:36-48). Rename accepts any typed name (fs.service.ts:201-211, no extension check).

verification.reasoning: The premise is wrong. A rename does not change file bytes: Plan.md still contains the canvas JSON after renameItem (fs.service.ts:201-220), and tab.content is still that JSON. updateTabPath (editor.store.svelte.ts:121-127) keeps fileType 'canvas', so the canvas view stays mounted and parseCanvas parses valid canvas JSON, not markdown, so the canvas does not come up empty. Later edits write canvas JSON into the same file, which is what it already contained. renameItem refuses an existing target (:205 exists check), so no other note's bytes can be overwritten. What remains is a cosmetic mismatch: a .md file still shown as a canvas until the tab is reopened. There is no data loss or corruption.
verification.repro: Rename open Plan.canvas to Plan.md, then add a node. Plan.md contains valid canvas JSON with the new node, the same data the file held before.
verification.fix_hint: Optional: recompute fileType in updateTabPath from the new extension, or close and reopen the tab on an extension change.

findings.title: renameType loop iterates the live tab array across awaits, so it can skip a tab
findings.scenario: Tabs [A, B, C] all carry the renamed _type. While writeTextFile(A) is awaited, the user closes A. removeTab splices the same array in place, so the for-of index moves to C and B is skipped. Rust propagate_type_rename then rewrites B on disk, but B's in-memory content keeps the old _type. If B is later edited, the autosave writes the old _type back over the rename.
findings.evidence: type-definitions.service.ts:215 'for (const tab of editorStore.tabs)' with await at :218. removeTab (store:72-73) uses tabs.splice in place. addTab and removeTab mutate the same proxied array rather than replacing it.

verification.reasoning: The loop runs for-of over editorStore.tabs with an await inside it (type-definitions.service.ts:215-218), and removeTab splices in place (editor.store.svelte.ts:72-73), so closing an earlier tab during the await skips the next tab. The skipped tab is rewritten on disk by propagate_type_rename while its buffer keeps the old _type. A dirty tab then autosaves the old type back, and a clean tab is reloaded by the watcher. This needs the user to close a tab during one IPC round trip from the rename dialog.
verification.repro: vitest: tabs [A,B,C] all with _type Old. Make writeTextFile(A) deferred and call editorStore.removeTab(0) while it is pending. Assert that B's content has _type New. This currently fails.
verification.fix_hint: Iterate a snapshot ([...editorStore.tabs]) and re-look-up each tab by path after the await.

findings.title: Closing a tab whose neighbour has identical content takes the rename branch in MarkdownEditor
findings.scenario: Close tab A, which becomes lastTabPath and is no longer in tabs. The neighbour B becomes active and its content is byte-identical to the CM doc (for example two empty notes, or a .md and a .ts file with the same text). The rename heuristic matches, so the branch returns before the doc replace and before applyLanguageForTab / getLanguageEffectsSync. B keeps A's language mode and receives A's saved view state (cursor and scroll). Text and saving are not affected, because the doc and tab content already match.
findings.evidence: The check at MarkdownEditor.svelte:181-185 is 'findTabIndex(tabs, lastTabPath) < 0 && view.state.doc.toString() === tab.content'. It returns at :193 before the language effects at :223 and :241.

verification.reasoning: MarkdownEditor.svelte:179-194 treats 'lastTabPath not in tabs AND CM doc === activeTab.content' as a rename and returns before getLanguageEffectsSync (:223), the doc replace and applyLanguageForTab (:239-241). Closing tab A removes it from tabs. If neighbour B has byte-identical content (for example two empty notes), the branch runs: A's view state moves to B's path (:186-190) and the language is not reconfigured. Nothing checks whether B was already an existing tab. That two empty markdown notes exist is very plausible, but there the only effect is a carried-over cursor and scroll position on an empty doc, which is harmless. A wrong language mode needs identical content across different file types, which is rare. The doc equals the tab content by construction, and no save is triggered, so no note bytes are at risk. Side note: history is not cleared on this path either, but that is covered by F84.
verification.repro: Create two empty notes X.md and Y.ts, open both, focus X and close it so Y becomes active. Y keeps markdown highlighting and X's cursor and scroll state, because the rename branch returned at MarkdownEditor.svelte:193.
verification.fix_hint: Tell rename apart from close: for example, take the rename branch only when the new path was not in the previous tabs list, or have the rename service set an explicit rename signal instead of comparing content.

findings.title: Canvas unmount flush writes canvas JSON into whichever tab is active, corrupting a markdown note
findings.scenario: Tabs: board.canvas (index 0, active) and todo.md (index 1). Move or edit a canvas node, then within 300 ms click the todo.md tab, or press Cmd+W on the canvas tab (global-keybindings.ts:84, closeTab removes the canvas and removeTab makes the neighbour active). setActiveIndex or removeTab changes activeIndex synchronously. EditorView's {#if} then destroys CanvasInner during Svelte's flush. onDestroy sees pendingPersist === true (set by the effect at CanvasInner.svelte:219) and calls persistChanges, which calls onJsonChange = onContentChange (EditorView.svelte:81) with the canvas JSON. updateContent writes that JSON into tabs[activeIndex], which is now todo.md. onContentChange arms the 2 s body timer, and saveDirtyTabs saves every dirty tab, so writeTextFile(todo.md, canvasJson) replaces the note on disk. The canvas edit is never stored in the canvas tab. The same happens when the canvas file is deleted while a persist is pending (closeTabsForDeletedPath, editor.service.ts:356-366). Not verified: whether file-history keeps the pre-save bytes of todo.md, which would make recovery possible.
findings.evidence: CanvasInner.svelte:219-224 arms a 300 ms timer and sets pendingPersist; CanvasInner.svelte:230-234 flushes unconditionally when pendingPersist is set, with no check that this canvas is still the active tab; persistWithoutHistory (104-109) calls onJsonChange(json); EditorView.svelte:81 wires onJsonChange={onContentChange}; editor.service.ts:224-226 calls editorStore.updateContent(content) with no path and scheduleAutoSave('body'); editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88 writes tabs[activeIndex].content; editor.service.ts:183-194 saves all dirty tabs; saveFileByPath (161-178) calls writeTextFile(path, content). findings.title: Note saves are non-atomic and not serialized per path
findings.scenario: saveFileByPath writes with plugin-fs writeTextFile. If the older write completes last, markSavedByPath(oldSnapshot) leaves the disk stale while the tab shows dirty, and no timer is armed to save again until the next keystroke or quit.

verification.reasoning:
Both canvas tabs share one branch (EditorView.svelte:80-81), so CanvasView and CanvasInner are reused and only jsonContent changes. The sync effect (CanvasInner.svelte:85-98) sees json !== lastSyncedJson, sets syncing=true and reassigns nodes. That re-runs the debounce effect. Its cleanup (:225) clears Board-1's 300 ms timer, and the new run returns early at :218 because syncing is still true (it resets in a microtask, :96). Board-1's last edit is therefore never written to Board-1's tab or to disk. pendingPersist also stays true (it is only cleared at :223), but it is usually reset by the next measurement-driven persist into Board-2, the active tab, which is correct. The stale-flag consequence (a later flush into a markdown tab) is the F5 root cause.

The loss is bounded to under 300 ms of canvas edits, such as the last characters typed in a card. No other note is corrupted on this path.

The user's layout, editor, sentry, auto-move and tag-colour settings are gone from disk with no backup. Only error() is logged. This affects settings, not note bytes.
