verification.reasoning: Any throw inside the try block (readTextFile, JSON.parse, a TypeError on JSON 'null' at parsed.periodicNotes, normalizeSettings) reaches the catch at settings.service.ts:166-178. The catch sets DEFAULT_SETTINGS and awaits saveSettings, which overwrites settings.json without a backup. writeSettingsFile is a plain writeTextFile, not atomic (:193). Only settings are lost, not note bytes, but the loss cannot be undone.
verification.repro: vitest: mock exists->true and readTextFile->'{"editor":' (truncated). Call loadSettings(v). Assert writeTextFile was not called with the settings path. This currently fails.
verification.fix_hint: On a read or parse failure, rename the bad file to settings.json.corrupt-<ts> (or skip saving) before writing defaults, and use an atomic write.

findings.title: Teardown is skipped after an aborted init, so the previous vault's tabs carry into the next vault
findings.scenario: Vault A's open_vault_db fails, for example a read-only vault where .kokobrain cannot be created, or a corrupt DB. initializeVault toasts and returns at line 237 before step 7, so unsubscribeFileChange stays null. The user keeps A's notes open as tabs and switches to vault B. switchVault saves what it can. initializeVault(B) sees the closed gate (172) and skips both the safety-net save and teardownVault, so A's tabs stay in B's editor. If A's writes still fail, A's dirty buffers keep their failing autosave inside B's session. They are dropped at a later real teardown, through the path in the first finding.
findings.evidence: app-lifecycle.service.ts:172 gate `if (unsubscribeFileChange)`. :232-238 open_vault_db catch returns at :237. unsubscribeFileChange is assigned only at :494. Teardown resets tabs only via resetEditor at :622.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F194: the early return at app-lifecycle.service.ts:237 leaves unsubscribeFileChange null, so the :172 teardown gate skips resetEditor on the next switch. Reaching it is unlikely because the failed session has no file tree and no tab restore.
verification.repro: See F194.
verification.fix_hint: See F194.

findings.title: Init continues past its version guard after three awaits and touches the new vault
findings.scenario: A vault switch lands while the previous init is inside one of these awaits, all of which are ms-scale except configureSentry, which can wait on Sentry.close(2000) (sentry.service.ts:45-47). Guards at lines 240, 296, 322 and 373 run after the calls they should protect. (1) If the stale init is parked at initLogSession (220), its open_vault_db(A) at 233 can be issued after B's open. The global Rust DB then points at A while B is shown. The DB also backs file-history snapshots (db/mod.rs:13), so B's snapshots can land in A's kokobrain.db. (2) If it is parked at ensureTemplatesFolder (384), the stale init runs registerSearchIndexHook and assigns unsubscribeSearchIndex (426), overwriting B's handle and leaking one after-save observer for the session. It also reaches startWatching(A) at 499. In the common ordering, B's later startWatching replaces it.
findings.evidence: app-lifecycle.service.ts:202 `await configureSentry`, :210 startSettingsPersistence(vaultPath), :220 `await initLogSession()`, :233 call('open_vault_db', { vaultPath }), :240 first guard after it. :384 `await ensureTemplatesFolder()`, :426 `unsubscribeSearchIndex = registerSearchIndexHook()`, :499 startWatching(vaultPath). db/mod.rs:36-46 open_database replaces the connection. The window needs a second switch within ms of the first, and debugLogToFile on for the :220 path. I did not reproduce it.

verification.reasoning: The missing guards are real. Nothing checks initVersion between :200 and the open_vault_db call at :233, which follows configureSentry (:202, can wait on Sentry.close(2000) per sentry.service.ts:46) and initLogSession (:220). Nothing checks after `await ensureTemplatesFolder()` at :384 before registerSearchIndexHook at :426, the auto-move hook, onFileChange at :494, startWatching at :499 and executePendingAction at :503. A stale init that resumes there overwrites the new init's handles. Reaching it needs a second vault switch while the previous init is parked at one of those awaits. With a vault open, only back-to-back cross-vault deep links can do that, and the deep-link queue serializes them only up to vaultStore.open. The outcome depends on IPC ordering. Note bytes are not affected, only DB and hook state.
verification.repro: Vitest sketch: make ensureTemplatesFolder return a deferred promise. Start initializeVault(B), then start initializeVault(C) and let it finish. Resolve B's deferred. Assert that startWatching was last called with B and that two search after-save observers are registered.
verification.fix_hint: Add `if (initVersion !== version) return;` after every await in initializeVault, including :202, :220, :233 and :384.

findings.title: Quit path destroys the window after one dirty-tab snapshot
findings.scenario: On Cmd+Q, saveAllDirtyTabs snapshots the dirty tabs (235-245). The handler then awaits drainEventCalendarWrites and flushSettingsPersistence (66-70) before destroy() (71). Keystrokes typed in that gap are not in the snapshot. Their 2 s autosave timer is armed, but destroy() fires first and nothing re-checks dirtiness. The window is tens of ms, so this is rare.
findings.evidence: tauri-listeners.service.ts:55 saveAllDirtyTabs, :66 drainEventCalendarWrites, :70 flushSettingsPersistence, :71 getCurrentWindow().destroy(). editor.service.ts:234-247 takes the snapshot once.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F17. Its premise is also wrong: Cmd+Q never reaches this handler (see F189), so the snapshot gap applies only to closing the window with the red button.
verification.repro: See F17.
verification.fix_hint: See F17.

findings.title: Auto-move for a note saved just before a vault switch is silently dropped
findings.scenario: The user saves note N. The after-save observer schedules evaluateAndMove with the 3000 ms debounce (settings.store.svelte.ts:104). If the user switches vault within 3 s, teardownVault calls resetAutoMove (app-lifecycle:640), which clears every pending timer (auto-move.service.ts:224-226). N's rule is never applied. It is evaluated again on the next save.
findings.evidence: auto-move.service.ts:95-125 schedules a setTimeout of settingsStore.autoMove.debounceMs. :216-227 resetAutoMove clears debounceTimers and unsubscribes the hook. app-lifecycle.service.ts:640 calls it inside teardownVault.

verification.reasoning: auto-move.service.ts:113-122 schedules a per-file setTimeout using settingsStore.autoMove.debounceMs. resetAutoMove (:216-227), called from teardownVault, clears every timer. A save within the debounce window before a vault switch therefore never moves the note. This is arguably the intended behavior, since moving files in a vault that was just closed is riskier. The rule is evaluated again on the next save. No content is lost.
verification.repro: Register the auto-move hook, fire notifyAfterSave for a matching note, call teardownVault(), advance the fake timers by debounceMs, and assert that no move IPC was called.
verification.fix_hint: Optional: flush pending evaluations before teardown, or accept and document the current behavior.

findings.title: Keystrokes typed during the watcher's disk read are wiped when an open tab is reloaded
findings.scenario: Active note N is open and clean. An external process rewrites N on disk, so disk text differs from savedContent. The watcher batch reaches reloadExternallyChangedTabs. N passes the isTabDirty check (line 380) and the function awaits readTextFile through Promise.allSettled (line 385). While that IPC is in flight the user types 'abc' in N; onContentChange sets tab.content (editor.service.ts:224-226). The apply loop re-checks only that the tab exists and that diskContent !== savedContent (lines 397-398). It never re-checks dirtiness. It then calls syncExternalContentToEditor(..., true, 'none') (line 401), which sets content and savedContent to the disk text (store 133-134) and replaces the CodeMirror doc (editor.service.ts:87-89). 'abc' is discarded, the tab reads clean, and no autosave is armed because the schedule is 'none'. The window is the readTextFile round trip, so a few milliseconds for one file and longer when several eligible paths are awaited together.
findings.evidence: The comment at editor.service.ts:396 says 'Re-check tab state - it may have changed during parallel reads' but the re-check does not include isTabDirty. The eligibility dirty check is at line 380. The overwrite sets savedContent too (store lines 133-134), so the lost text is not recoverable from the store.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause. The added trace detail checks out: editor.service.ts:224-226 updates content synchronously, and the store's updateTabContentByPath sets savedContent as well.
verification.repro: See F3.
verification.fix_hint: See F3.

findings.title: Notify's rescan flag is dropped, so a dropped-event burst skips the index rebuild
findings.scenario: A large external burst (git checkout, a sync client writing hundreds of notes) makes FSEvents coalesce and set MustScanSubDirs. notify 8.2.1 turns that into an event with flag Rescan and the directory as its path (fsevent.rs:115-120, path attached at fsevent.rs:573). The bridge iterates only event.paths (watcher.rs:255-256) and never checks need_rescan(), so the flag never reaches TS. The batch contains only the directory (for example /vault/Projects, with no dot in its basename). rebuildAllIndexes drops it from filePaths (watcher-handler.service.ts:33-36) and returns at lines 41-44 as 'directory-only changes'. The notes changed inside the dropped window are never read or re-upserted. VaultIndex (backlinks, tags, tasks, properties) and FTS/semantic rows keep pre-burst content until restart or a later per-file event. The tree is fine: resolveRescanParents rescans the directory's parent (fs.logic.ts:302-312), which covers it.
findings.evidence: notify-8.2.1/src/fsevent.rs:115-120 builds Event::new(EventKind::Other).set_flag(Flag::Rescan) and fsevent.rs:573 attaches the callback path to every translated event. watcher.rs:255-256 reads only event.paths. watcher-handler.service.ts:41 and 33-36 skip any batch whose filtered list is empty. I did not reproduce FSEvents emitting MustScanSubDirs under this app's load.

verification.reasoning: I checked the library code. Cargo.lock pins notify 8.2.1 (Cargo.lock:3159-3160). fsevent.rs:115-123 maps MUST_SCAN_SUBDIRS to Event(Other)+Flag::Rescan, and :571-573 attaches the reported path, which is a directory. The bridge (watcher.rs:254-258) forwards only event.paths and drops the flag. TS rebuildAllIndexes drops paths without a dot in the basename (watcher-handler.service.ts:33-36) and returns early when none remain (:41-44). reloadExternallyChangedTabs gets only the directory path, which matches no tab. So when FSEvents coalesces or drops per-file events, an open clean tab whose file changed is not reloaded, and the next edit plus autosave overwrites the external content. The index also stays stale. The finding rates this as index-only, but the tab-reload miss raises the severity. I could not verify how often FSEvents emits MustScanSubDirs (kernel/user drop) under this app's load.
verification.repro: Rust unit test: feed the bridge closure an Event with Flag::Rescan and paths=[/vault/Projects]. Observe the batch is ['/vault/Projects'] and nothing marks it a rescan. TS: rebuildAllIndexes(['/vault/Projects']) returns without reading files, and reloadExternallyChangedTabs(['/vault/Projects']) reloads nothing.
verification.fix_hint: In the notify callback, check event.need_rescan() and emit a rescan marker. TS should then treat it as a full rebuild and reload every open clean tab whose disk content differs from savedContent.

findings.title: A failed read of an existing note is treated as a deletion and removes it from the index
findings.scenario: A note that was valid UTF-8 at the last scan becomes unreadable. Examples: permissions changed (chmod 000 by a sync tool), or an external editor saved it in Latin-1 or UTF-16 (invalid UTF-8). read_files_batch's fs::read_to_string fails, so the result has content None and error Some (files.rs:69-73). incrementalUpdateFiles maps content === null to kind 'delete' (watcher-handler.service.ts:106-108) and ignores error. applyNoteChange's delete branch calls remove_note_from_index, remove_from_search_index, remove_semantic_file and fanOut('remove') (note-change.service.ts:197-223). The note disappears from backlinks, tags, search and semantic results while it is still on disk and in the sidebar. A later successful event or a save restores it. Contrast: the cached full scan keeps the cached entry on a re-read failure (commands/vault.rs:1312, 'keeping cached').
findings.evidence: files.rs:63-73 returns content None on any read error. watcher-handler.service.ts:106 tests only content !== null. The Rust scan path at vault.rs:1305-1313 keeps the stale entry instead.

verification.reasoning: read_files_batch returns content None for a canonicalize failure, an outside-vault path, or any read_to_string error, including invalid UTF-8 and EACCES (files.rs:36-46, 63-73). incrementalUpdateFiles maps content === null to a delete and ignores error (watcher-handler.service.ts:105-109). The owner's delete branch then removes the note from VaultIndex, FTS, semantic and the TS consumers. The note's bytes on disk are untouched, and a later successful event or save restores the index entries. A full cached scan keeps the stale entry instead. Severity is low: no note content is lost.
verification.repro: Open a vault. `chmod 000 note.md` (or rewrite it as UTF-16). The watcher incremental path removes it, and backlinks and search no longer list it while the file is still in the sidebar.
verification.fix_hint: Treat content === null as a delete only when the error indicates not-found. Otherwise skip the path and keep the existing entries.

findings.title: Overlapping incremental tree patches can overwrite a fresher tree written by a concurrent refresh
findings.scenario: handleChangedPaths is not serialised. Batch 1 is a full refresh: loadDirectoryTree (fs.service.ts:93) writes the whole tree with no sequence check, and on a large vault it takes more than 500 ms. Batch 2 can start only after the 500 ms Rust quiet window (watcher.rs:187-222), so it runs while batch 1 is still awaiting. Batch 2 snapshots the pre-refresh tree at fs.watcher.ts:157, its scan of one parent finishes after batch 1 completes, and line 184 writes the stale snapshot with one parent replaced. Notes created in batch 1 disappear from the sidebar, and notes deleted in batch 1 reappear, until an event touches their folder. Disk and VaultIndex are unaffected. watchVersion (line 166) guards only start and stop, not overlapping refreshes.
findings.evidence: fs.watcher.ts:157 copies fsStore.fileTree before the awaits in the loop and fs.watcher.ts:184 writes that copy with no re-read. loadDirectoryTree at fs.service.ts:93 writes the tree unconditionally.

verification.reasoning: handleChangedPaths is not serialized (fs.watcher.ts:199, `void`). The incremental branch snapshots fsStore.fileTree at :157, awaits scan_vault per parent, and writes the snapshot back at :184 with no re-read. Two overlapping batches can therefore lose one batch's tree patch, and an incremental patch can land after a full refresh and revert it. That needs batch 1 to outlast the 500 ms Rust quiet window, for example a full or vault-root scan on a large vault (resolveRescanParents can return [vaultPath], fs.logic.ts:309). It affects the sidebar only; disk and index are unaffected. Whether it happens depends on timing.
verification.repro: vitest: mock scan_vault so the first call resolves after the second. Call handleChangedPaths twice with different parents and assert that the final fsStore.fileTree lacks batch 1's patch.
verification.fix_hint: Serialize handleChangedPaths (a queue or serializeWithRerun), or re-read fsStore.fileTree after the awaits and before patching.

findings.title: Rust debounce never flushes while real events keep arriving less than 500 ms apart
findings.scenario: Every accepted real event sets last_event = now (line 197) and the flush condition is last_event.elapsed() >= debounce (line 222). There is no maximum wait. A process that writes a file every 300 ms for several minutes (a bulk copy or sync of notes) keeps the buffer unflushed for the whole stream. No vault-files-changed is emitted, so the tree, the index and the open-tab reload stay stale, and the HashSet grows. The Audit 2026-06-01 fix (lines 175-186) addressed starvation caused by hidden events only. This matches the explicit trailing-quiet design in the comments (lines 214-221), so it is a design gap rather than a regression.
findings.evidence: watcher.rs:197 and 222 as cited. No code path emits after a fixed interval while the stream continues.

verification.reasoning: watcher.rs:194-198 resets last_event on every real event, and the flush condition is last_event.elapsed() >= debounce (:222). There is no max-wait path, so a sustained stream of real events less than 500 ms apart defers the emit indefinitely. This matches the documented trailing-quiet design (:214-221), so it is a design gap. Side effect: open-tab reloads are delayed for the whole stream, which widens the F155 overwrite window for clean tabs the user starts editing during the stream.
verification.repro: Rust unit test on the bridge loop: send a real path every 300 ms for 10 s. on_emit is not called until 500 ms after the last send.
verification.fix_hint: Add a max-wait: flush when the buffer is non-empty and first_event.elapsed() >= MAX_WAIT (for example 3 s).

findings.title: Self-save skip hides a later external edit to the same file for up to 15 seconds
findings.scenario: The app saves note N at t0. markRecentSave arms a 15 s TTL (editor.hooks.ts:37-43). An external tool edits N at t0+5 s. The watcher batch is [N]. areAllRecentSaves([N]) is true, so rebuildAllIndexes returns at lines 41-44 without reading the file. The open-tab reload still runs first (runWatcherBatch, app-lifecycle.service.ts:481-487), so the editor shows C2. But the VaultIndex, FTS and semantic rows for N keep the app's C1 bytes, while disk has C2. Closed notes stay stale until the next save or restart. I did not trace whether the layout content effect re-indexes a reloaded active tab. The skip is keyed on path only and never compares content.
findings.evidence: watcher-handler.service.ts:41 is the only use of areAllRecentSaves in the rebuild path. editor.hooks.ts:47-49 checks only recentSaves.has(path).

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F159: path-only areAllRecentSaves skip at watcher-handler.service.ts:41. The claim that VaultIndex keeps C1 is partly wrong for the active tab, because the layout 'edit' effect re-indexes it.
verification.repro: See F159.
verification.fix_hint: See F159.

findings.title: Latent prefix mismatch when the vault path contains a symlink component
findings.scenario: start_watcher_inner builds vault_prefix from the raw vault_path (watcher.rs:245-249) and never canonicalises it. notify canonicalises the watch root (fsevent.rs:376) and delivers only events under that canonical root (fsevent.rs:552). If FSEvents reports resolved paths (assumed, not verified here), a vault opened through a symlinked directory gets event paths that do not start with vault_prefix. Then is_inside_hidden_dir returns false for every event (watcher.rs:72-73), so .git and .kokobrain churn is not filtered. resolveRescanParents' inVault check (fs.logic.ts:299) fails, so every batch falls back to a full refresh. Watcher paths also stop matching the app's tab, recentSaves and dedupe keys, so the index can hold two keys for one note. A vault under a non-symlinked path is not affected.
findings.evidence: watcher.rs:245-249 uses vault_path unchanged. fsevent.rs:376 canonicalises the watch root; fsevent.rs:552 filters events with path.starts_with(canonical root). The FSEvents path spelling itself was not checked against Apple's documentation or a run.

verification.reasoning: vault_prefix comes from the raw vault_path (watcher.rs:245-249). notify canonicalizes the root for filtering (fsevent.rs:376, 552-556), and scan_vault returns canonical tree paths (utils/fs.rs:39-46 validate_vault_path canonicalize). So with a symlinked vault path, tree and tab paths are canonical while vaultStore.path and vault_prefix are raw. That breaks the hidden-dir filter (watcher.rs:72-73) and the inVault check in resolveRescanParents (fs.logic.ts:299), so every batch takes a full refresh. Tabs and watcher paths are likely both canonical, so the tab reload probably still matches. I did not verify which path spelling FSEvents reports.
verification.repro: Open a vault through a symlink (for example ln -s ~/Notes /tmp/v and open /tmp/v), then touch a file in .git. Check whether the debug log shows the hidden path forwarded and full refreshes on every batch.
verification.fix_hint: Canonicalize vault_path in start_watcher_inner (and ideally where vaultStore.path is set) so every prefix uses one spelling.

findings.title: A vault switch during a watcher batch can upsert the old vault's note into the new vault's index
findings.scenario: incrementalUpdateFiles captures vaultPath (watcher-handler.service.ts:50) and awaits read_files_batch (line 90). If vault B is initialised during that round trip, the read still succeeds for old-vault path A. The loop then calls applyNoteChange(upsert, vaultPath A) (lines 105-107), which calls update_note_in_index on the global VaultIndex that now belongs to B. runWatcherBatch does not check initVersion (app-lifecycle.service.ts:481-487), and teardownVault only clears pendingWatcherPaths (line 538). A's note stays in B's index until a rebuild replaces the index. The window is one IPC round trip, and the entry survives only if B's build finished before the upsert landed.
findings.evidence: update_note_in_index (commands/vault.rs:303-308) takes only path and content and writes the single managed VaultIndex, with no vault check.

verification.reasoning: runWatcherBatch has no initVersion check (app-lifecycle.service.ts:481-488). teardownVault clears pendingWatcherPaths and cancels the debounce, but cannot stop a batch already awaiting. incrementalUpdateFiles captured vaultPath A (watcher-handler.service.ts:50) and calls update_note_in_index on the single managed index, plus FTS keyed relative to A, which could land in B's DB. For the entry to survive, B's initialization (DB open plus full scan) must finish inside the remaining per-file IPCs of A's batch. That ordering is very unlikely, though I found no guard that forbids it.
verification.repro: vitest: hold read_files_batch pending, call teardownVault plus a fast initializeVault(B) with mocks, then resolve. Assert that update_note_in_index was invoked with A's path after B's scan.
verification.fix_hint: Capture initVersion in runWatcherBatch and pass an isStale check into incrementalUpdateFiles that is tested before each applyNoteChange.

findings.title: Overlapping startWatching calls can leak a vault-files-changed listener
findings.scenario: startWatching awaits stopWatching (line 191) and then awaits on() (line 198) before storing unlisten. If a second startWatching starts before the first on() resolves (for example, a fast vault switch while the first initialisation's startWatching is still in flight), the later assignment overwrites unlisten and the first listener is never detached. Every vault-files-changed then runs handleChangedPaths twice and notifies listeners twice. rebuildAllIndexes is serialised, so the work doubles rather than corrupts. stopWatching detaches only the stored listener.
findings.evidence: fs.watcher.ts:198 assigns the module-level unlisten after an await, with no check that a listener is already held.

verification.reasoning: fs.watcher.ts:190-200 assigns unlisten after `await on(...)` with no check for an existing listener. A leak needs a second startWatching whose `await stopWatching()` completes before the first on() resolves. The only caller is initializeVault step 7 (app-lifecycle.service.ts:499), which runs after the awaited index builds, so B's call comes long after A's on() IPC resolves. In practice this is close to unreachable, and the impact is doubled work rather than data loss.
verification.repro: vitest: make on() resolve slowly, call startWatching('A') and startWatching('B') back to back, then emit an event. handleChangedPaths runs twice.
verification.fix_hint: Use a version token in startWatching. If watchVersion changed after `await on()`, call the new unlisten immediately.

findings.title: duplicateItem overwrites an existing case-variant sibling on case-insensitive volumes
findings.scenario: On macOS (APFS, case-insensitive by default) a folder holds Note.md and note copy.md. The user chooses Duplicate on Note.md. readDir returns the real names. generateCopyName builds a case-sensitive Set of siblings, so the candidate Note copy.md is not seen as taken and is returned. copyFile(/v/Note.md, /v/Note copy.md) opens the existing note copy.md entry and truncates it, so its content is replaced with Note.md's bytes, with no Trash copy. The numbered loop (Note copy 2.md) has the same flaw. createFile and createFolder are safe: generateUniqueName lowercases (fs.logic.ts:225-226) and Rust create_note refuses existing paths (vault.rs:888-896).
findings.evidence: generateCopyName: const siblings = new Set(existingSiblingNames) (fs.logic.ts:185), membership tested with exact strings (fs.logic.ts:203-208). generateUniqueName lowercases both sides, and its comment says why (fs.logic.ts:218-226, 247). duplicateItem passes raw readDir names (fs.service.ts:269-272) and calls copyFile (fs.service.ts:278). JS wrapper: node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-fs/dist-js/index.js:386-391 invokes plugin:fs|copy_file. Rust: tauri-plugin-fs-2.7.1 src/commands.rs:393 calls std::fs::copy(from, to), which overwrites an existing destination.

verification.reasoning: generateCopyName builds a case-sensitive Set (fs.logic.ts:185) and tests exact strings (:203-208). generateUniqueName next to it lowercases both sides and its comment gives the APFS reason (fs.logic.ts:218-226). duplicateItem passes raw readDir names and then calls copyFile with no exists() check (fs.service.ts:268-278). The lockfile pins tauri-plugin-fs 2.7.1 (Cargo.lock:5557-5558), and its copy_file calls std::fs::copy (commands.rs:393), which is documented to overwrite the destination. With Note.md and 'note copy.md' in the same folder on case-insensitive APFS, the copy truncates 'note copy.md' and fills it with Note.md's bytes, with no Trash copy. Folder duplicates are safe because mkdir fails when the target exists. The existing tests (fs.logic.test.ts:677+) have no case-variant case.
verification.repro: vitest: expect(generateCopyName('Note.md', false, ['Note.md','note copy.md'])).not.toBe('Note copy.md'). It currently returns 'Note copy.md'. Manual repro on APFS: create Note.md and 'note copy.md' with distinct text, Duplicate Note.md, and 'note copy.md' now holds Note.md's text.
verification.fix_hint: Lowercase the sibling set and the candidates in generateCopyName, as generateUniqueName does. Optionally also check exists(newPath) before copyFile.

findings.title: Deleting a note or folder discards its unsaved edits before the Trash move
findings.scenario: The user types in note A. Autosave is a trailing 2 s debounce (editor.service.ts:197, utils/debounce.ts) that every keystroke resets, so during continuous typing nothing is saved yet. Before a 2 s pause, the user confirms Move to Trash (FilesNavigator.svelte:174, NoteRowMenu.svelte:128, or note-action-bar.service.ts:24). applyPathChange calls closeTabsForDeletedPath before diskOp (path-change.service.ts:125), which removes the dirty tab without saving (editor.service.ts:356-366). The pending saveDirtyTabs iterates editorStore.tabs (editor.service.ts:183-186) and no longer finds A. The Trash receives the last saved bytes, so everything typed since the last save is lost. The 500 ms frontmatter timer behaves the same way.
findings.evidence: path-change.service.ts:125 closes tabs before await diskOp() (127). closeTabsForDeletedPath removes tabs with no save call (editor.service.ts:356-366). saveDirtyTabs reads editorStore.tabs at call time (editor.service.ts:183-186). debounce resets its timer on every call (utils/debounce.ts:9-18). deleteItem passes the disk path to moveToTrash (fs.service.ts:169-178); moveToTrash was read only to line 60 (trash.service.ts:49-60).

verification.reasoning: Same root cause and code path as F165, including the folder-delete case through the prefix match at editor.service.ts:360.
verification.repro: See F165.
verification.fix_hint: See F165.

findings.title: Link rewrite on rename overwrites keystrokes typed while it awaits disk I/O
findings.scenario: The active tab is Y, which links to X. The user renames X in the explorer. For Y, updateLinksAfterRename snapshots openTab.content (dirty) or awaits readTextFile (clean), then awaits writeTextFile. While that runs, keystrokes reach editorStore.updateContent through onContentChange (editor.service.ts:224-225). When the write resolves, syncExternalContentToEditor calls updateTabContentByPath, which sets content and savedContent to the snapshot with no check (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-135), and bumps the signal so CodeMirror replaces its whole document. The disk file was written from the snapshot, so the typed characters are gone from both the editor and disk. Each affected file has one read and one write IPC of window, and the files run concurrently under Promise.allSettled (link-updater.service.ts:30).
findings.evidence: link-updater.service.ts:33-35 takes the snapshot, :39 awaits writeTextFile, :47 calls syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, updatedContent, true, 'none'). syncExternalContentToEditor (editor.service.ts:70-85) calls updateTabContentByPath when markSaved is true. onContentChange -> updateContent runs per keystroke (editor.service.ts:224-227, editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88).

verification.reasoning: The path is real. updateLinksAfterRename takes the content snapshot (link-updater.service.ts:33-35), awaits writeTextFile (:39), then syncExternalContentToEditor(..., true) (:47). That sets content and savedContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-135) and replaces the whole CM doc with no history entry (MarkdownEditor.svelte:310-335). No check confirms the tab still equals the snapshot. Keystrokes reach tab.content synchronously (editor.service.ts:224-226). The window is reachable from real UI: FilesNavigator commits the rename on blur (FilesNavigator.svelte:421), so clicking into the editor commits it while the user starts typing. All affected files run in one Promise.allSettled (:30), so on a hub note the active tab's read and write queue behind many IPCs. Whether a keystroke lands inside that window is timing-dependent and was not measured. The renamed note itself is excluded (:28).
verification.repro: vitest: open tab Y (dirty) linking [[X]]. Make writeTextFile return a deferred promise. Start updateLinksAfterRename('/v/X.md','/v/Z.md'). While it is pending, call editorStore.updateContent(Y.content+'typed'), then resolve the write. Assert the tab content contains 'typed'. This currently fails.
verification.fix_hint: After the write, compare the tab's current content to the snapshot. When they differ, re-run replaceWikilinks on the current buffer and leave the tab dirty, or use updateTabContentOnly instead of markSaved.

findings.title: Case-only rename is refused as already existing on case-insensitive volumes
findings.scenario: On macOS the user renames note.md to Note.md in the explorer. commitRename skips only exact equality (FilesNavigator.svelte:147), so renameItem runs. exists('/v/Note.md') is true because it resolves to the same file, so renameItem throws 'Note.md already exists in this folder'. The user has no in-app way to fix the casing. Links are not affected, because updateLinksAfterRename skips case-only changes (link-updater.service.ts:25).
findings.evidence: fs.service.ts:205 returns the error when exists(newPath) is true. plugin-fs exists is Path::exists (tauri-plugin-fs-2.7.1 src/commands.rs:1270), which follows the case-insensitive lookup on APFS. The same path is used by NoteRowMenu.svelte:102.

verification.reasoning: renameItem returns early only when the strings are exactly equal (fs.service.ts:204), and exists(newPath) is true for a case variant on case-insensitive APFS, so the rename throws targetExistsError (:205). No other code path handles case-only renames. No data is lost; the check is what protects against an overwrite.
verification.repro: Manual test on APFS: rename note.md to Note.md in the explorer and see the error toast. vitest: mock exists()->true and check that renameItem rejects for '/v/note.md' -> 'Note.md'.
verification.fix_hint: When oldPath.toLowerCase() === newPath.toLowerCase(), skip the exists check, or rename through a temporary name.

findings.title: Rename rewrite skips path-qualified and self-links, leaving them dangling
findings.scenario: (a) Note B contains [[Projects/Old]]. The index resolves it (resolve_with_cache falls back to the basename, index.rs:118-122), so B is in the affected set. replaceWikilinks compares the full target projects/old with old (link-updater.logic.ts:27) and returns the text unchanged. B is not written, and after the rename to New the link is broken. (b) Note Old.md contains [[Old]]. The index excludes self-references (index.rs:344 resolved != *src; the incremental path filters self at 390 and 398), and link-updater.service.ts:28 also filters the renamed note, so the self-link is never rewritten and points to nothing after the rename.
findings.evidence: link-updater.logic.ts:26-28 matches target.trim().toLowerCase() against the bare old name only. index.rs:110-124 resolves by full target, then by basename.

verification.reasoning: Rust resolves [[Folder/Note]] and [[Note.md]] by basename fallback (index.rs:85-91, 110-124; by_path is keyed by the stem, :305-307), so those sources are returned by get_backlinks_v2. replaceWikilinks compares the full trimmed target with the bare stem (link-updater.logic.ts:27), so these forms stay unchanged and the service writes nothing (link-updater.service.ts:38). After the rename the link is broken, or it silently resolves to another note with the same old basename. Self-links are excluded by the index (index.rs:344) and by the filter at link-updater.service.ts:28. No note bytes are lost, but links break or retarget silently.
verification.repro: vitest: expect(replaceWikilinks('[[Work/Plan]] [[Plan.md]]','Plan','Roadmap')).toBe('[[Work/Roadmap]] [[Roadmap.md]]'). This currently returns the input unchanged.
verification.fix_hint: In replaceWikilinks, match on the target's basename-without-extension and keep the original folder prefix and extension. Rewrite self-links in the renamed file too.

findings.title: Renaming a folder leaves its folder note and _order behind
findings.scenario: Folder Projects/ contains Projects.md with _order: 2. The user renames the folder to Work. renameItem renames only the folder, so the note becomes Work/Projects.md. folderNoteDir maps only X/X.md to X (folder-notes.logic.ts:59-63), so Work/Projects.md yields no directory key, and contentOrder no longer has the .../Work entry. applyFolderOrder then falls back to name order, and the folder moves among its siblings. findFolderNote (folder-notes.logic.ts:9-13) has no callers in src, so nothing maintains the convention.
findings.evidence: renameItem and applyPathChange never touch a folder note (fs.service.ts:201-220, path-change.service.ts:117-171). contentOrder is built only through folderNoteDir (folder-notes.logic.ts:46-56 via addContentOrder; tauri-listeners.service.ts:194, 231-234). applyFolderOrder reads contentOrder.get(folder.path) (fs.logic.ts:416-419, 426-430).

verification.reasoning: renameItem and applyPathChange never rename the folder note (fs.service.ts:201-220, path-change.service.ts:117-171). folderNoteDir only maps X/X.md (folder-notes.logic.ts:59-63), so after a folder rename both the folder-note click (FilesNavigator.svelte:210 uses findFolderNote; the finding's claim that it has no callers is wrong) and the _order lookup stop working. This is missing behavior and nothing is lost.
verification.repro: vitest: buildContentOrderMap([{path:'/v/Work/Projects.md', frontmatter:{_order:2}}]).has('/v/Work') is false after renaming Projects/ to Work/.
verification.fix_hint: When folderNotes is enabled, rename X/X.md to Y/Y.md as part of the folder rename.

findings.title: Names containing #, [ or ] are written verbatim into rewritten wikilinks
findings.scenario: getFileNameError forbids only <>:"/\|?* (fs.logic.ts:121-122), so # [ ] are allowed. Renaming Note.md to C#.md makes replaceWikilinks write [[C#]] into each linker (link-updater.logic.ts:30 uses newName raw). The app's own WIKILINK_RE (link-updater.logic.ts:8) does not match [[C#]], because a # must be followed by at least one non-] character, so the rewrite pass no longer recognises that link and any other parser reads it as target C with no heading. Names with ] (for example a]b) produce [[a]b]], which the regex cannot parse at all. The Rust resolver's reading of these forms was not checked.
findings.evidence: fs.logic.ts:121-122 forbidden set; link-updater.logic.ts:8 regex; link-updater.logic.ts:30-37 concatenates newName without escaping.

verification.reasoning: getFileNameError allows #, [ and ] (fs.logic.ts:121-122). replaceWikilinks concatenates newName raw (link-updater.logic.ts:30). WIKILINK_RE's target class excludes '#' and the heading group needs at least one character (link-updater.logic.ts:8), so '[[C#]]' does not match on later rewrite passes, and '[[a]b]]' cannot be parsed. Links break and existing text is unaffected. The Rust parser's reading of these forms was not checked.
verification.repro: vitest: replaceWikilinks(replaceWikilinks('[[Note]]','Note','C#'),'C#','D') is still '[[C#]]'.
verification.fix_hint: Reject '#', '[', ']' and '|' in note names (getFileNameError), as Obsidian does.

findings.title: A failed backlink lookup aborts the rename after the disk move
findings.scenario: get_backlinks_v2 returns Err when the VaultIndex lock is poisoned (vault.rs:431-441). updateLinksAfterRename awaits it with no try/catch (link-updater.service.ts:27), so the error escapes applyPathChange at path-change.service.ts:149 before refreshTree (153), rename_note (159) and the removal sweep (168-170). renameItem logs and rethrows (fs.service.ts:216-218), so the user sees 'Could not rename' although the file moved on disk. The Rust index stays keyed to the old path and the tree is stale until a watcher event arrives.
findings.evidence: link-updater.service.ts:27 has no try/catch around call('get_backlinks_v2'). path-change.service.ts:149 awaits it unguarded. The early returns skip lines 153-170.

verification.reasoning: updateLinksAfterRename awaits call('get_backlinks_v2') outside the allSettled (link-updater.service.ts:27). applyPathChange awaits it, and refreshTree, without a try/catch (path-change.service.ts:149, 153), which contradicts the docstring's 'Never throws on the index legs'. A rejection skips rename_note and the forgetNote sweep, and renameItem rethrows (fs.service.ts:216-218) after the disk rename succeeded. The trigger is rare: get_backlinks_v2 errors only on a poisoned lock (vault.rs:436-438), and refreshTree fails only on a scan error.
verification.repro: vitest: mock call('get_backlinks_v2') to reject. Call renameItem('/v/A.md','B.md'). Assert that rename_note was invoked and that renameItem resolves. This currently fails.
verification.fix_hint: Wrap updateLinksAfterRename and refreshTree in try/catch inside applyPathChange and log, so the re-key and the sweep always run.

findings.title: Folder rename or move gives moved notes no FTS5 or semantic rows under the new paths
findings.scenario: Folder A/ with notes is renamed to B/. The sweep calls forgetNote for each old child path, which removes the FTS5 and semantic rows under the old keys. Nothing inserts rows under the new keys: rename_note re-keys only the VaultIndex (vault.rs:1045-1072), and no applyNoteChange runs for the new paths. Recovery depends on the watcher reporting the moved .md files. watcher-handler drops directory-only batches (watcher-handler.service.ts:31-43), and path-change.service.ts:74-76 says watcher events are not a reliable substitute. Search may therefore miss the moved notes until a full rebuild.
findings.evidence: path-change.service.ts:168-170 forgets the old child paths with vaultPath. note-change.service.ts:206-223 removes the FTS and semantic rows for the old key. rename_note (vault.rs:1045-1072) touches only the VaultIndex.

verification.reasoning: forgetNote deletes the FTS5 and semantic rows for each old child path (path-change.service.ts:168-170 -> note-change.service.ts:206-223). rename_note re-keys only the VaultIndex, and nothing upserts the new paths. The comment at path-change.service.ts:74-76 says a folder rename arrives as one directory event, which the watcher filter drops (watcher-handler.service.ts:31-43). Whether notify/FSEvents also reports the child .md paths, and whether a startup reconcile restores the rows, was not verified.
verification.repro: Integration test: index a folder A with notes, rename A to B via renameItem, and check that search_fts finds the notes under B/ without a full rebuild.
verification.fix_hint: In applyPathChange, after rename_note, upsert FTS and semantic for each moved child (read the bytes, or add a Rust re-key command for the search tables).

findings.title: Vault switch can publish the previous vault's tree from an in-flight load
findings.scenario: loadDirectoryTree(A) is awaiting scan_vault when the user switches to vault B. Teardown calls resetFileSystem (app-lifecycle.service.ts:623) and B's load starts. If A's scan resolves last, setFileTree(A's tree) overwrites B's tree (fs.service.ts:93), and loadFolderOrder(A) can overwrite the folder order (fs.service.ts:49, 64). There is no generation check. Whether vault switching waits for in-flight scans was not verified.
findings.evidence: loadDirectoryTree has no token check before setFileTree (fs.service.ts:74-95). fsStore.reset clears the tree but not in-flight loads (fs.store.svelte.ts:36-42).

verification.reasoning: loadDirectoryTree (fs.service.ts:74-102) has no generation or vault check before setFileTree, and loadFolderOrder (:41-70) calls setFolderOrder without one either. Besides init step 4 (app-lifecycle.service.ts:315), it is called from refreshTree and from tauri-listeners.service.ts:182. To publish A's tree over B's, a scan of A started before the switch has to resolve after B's step-4 scan, which runs only after B's save, drain, settings, DB and step 3 awaits. That is only possible on a large vault with a slow scan. The effect is a wrong tree, and files opened from it still map to their real paths, so no note bytes are corrupted.
verification.repro: Mock call('scan_vault') for vault A with a deferred promise. Call loadDirectoryTree(A), then resetFileSystem() and loadDirectoryTree(B) resolving immediately. Resolve A and assert that fsStore.fileTree is A's tree.
verification.fix_hint: Capture vaultPath, or a load token, and drop the result if vaultStore.path changed or a newer load started.

findings.title: Numeric and boolean scalars are rewritten from parsed value, losing source text
findings.scenario: A closed note has frontmatter `phone: 0612345678`, `id: 0042`, `version: 1.0`, `done: True`. The user clicks Favorite (NoteRowMenu.svelte:215 -> toggleFavoriteForPath -> updateNoteFrontmatter). parseFrontmatterProperties turns the unquoted scalars into JS numbers and booleans (convertToProperty keeps type number/boolean), and serializeProperties writes them back with Document.set. The file becomes `phone: 612345678`, `id: 42`, `version: 1`, `done: true`. No refusal and no toast. The same happens on the open-tab path (saveFileByPath) and on every other updateNoteFrontmatter caller (icon picker, event edits). detectLossyFrontmatter only flags integers above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (properties.logic.ts:426-434), so none of this is caught.
findings.evidence: Code: convertToProperty number/boolean branches (properties.logic.ts:184-190) and serializeProperties Document.set with the JS value (:575-582). Read-only repro: I replicated parse (parseDocument(...).toJS()) plus new Document + set + toString({lineWidth:0, flowCollectionPadding:false}) with the installed yaml 2.9.1 (node_modules/yaml). Output: id 0042->42, zip 01234->1234, version 1.0->1, rating 4.50->4.5, mask 0x1F->31, sign +5->5, exp 1e3->1000, lead .5->0.5, done True->true, flag FALSE->false. Root cause in yaml: node_modules/yaml/dist/schema/core/int.js resolves decimal ints with parseInt, and float.js sets minFractionDigits, which toJS() drops. Tests do not catch it: properties.logic.test.ts:1232 ('numbers' fixture) and the round-trip check at :1253-1257 compare yaml-parsed values, so 0x1F -> 31 passes. ADR-0029 (docs/adr/0029-frontmatter-yaml-canonical-form.md:36) covers numbers only for string scalars; numeric values read from disk are not in its list of accepted coercions.

verification.reasoning: Tried to refute through the lossy guard and the tests, and both fail. updateNoteFrontmatter calls detectLossyFrontmatter (frontmatter-write.service.ts:121). For numbers that guard only flags non-safe integers (properties.logic.ts:426-434). convertToProperty keeps JS numbers and booleans (properties.logic.ts:184-190), and serializeProperties does doc.set(key, jsValue) on a fresh Document (:572-584), so the source spelling is gone. I ran a read-only node check with the installed yaml 2.9.1: `zip: 01234, version: 1.10, hex: 0x1F, done: True, price: 9.90` came back as `zip: 1234, version: 1.1, hex: 31, done: true, price: 9.9`, with 0 errors and 0 warnings. The 'numbers' fixture (properties.logic.test.ts:1232) and its round-trip check (:1253-1257) compare yaml-parsed values, so 0x1F -> 31 passes. ADR-0029:105 says Rust reads 0x1F as a string, so the index value changes too. Reachable from one Favorite or icon click on any note, open or closed. Silent value change (phone, zip, version numbers).
verification.repro:
vitest: _resetParseFrontmatterCache(); const c='---
zip: 01234
version: 1.10
---
body
'; expect(detectLossyFrontmatter(c)).toBe(null); const out=rebuildContent(toggleFavorite(parseFrontmatterProperties(c),true), extractBody(c)); expect(out).toContain('zip: 01234') // fails: 'zip: 1234'
verification.fix_hint: Make the rewrite edit the parsed Document in place: parseDocument(raw) then doc.set only on changed keys, so untouched scalars keep their source text. Or add a detectLossyFrontmatter reason for numeric/boolean scalars whose source differs from String(value).

findings.title: Closed-note write truncates the file before writing and is not atomic
findings.scenario: The closed-note rewrite calls writeTextFile(path, next, {create:false}). tauri-plugin-fs 2.7.1 opens the file with truncate (commands.rs:1163 truncate = !append, or the default branch with truncate:true at :1177) and then calls write_all (:1202). If write_all fails partway (disk full, I/O error), or the app is force-quit while it runs, the note is left as a prefix of the new bytes or empty. There is no temp file and no rename to recover from. The rejection is rethrown raw (see the silent-error finding), so the user is not told. The test 'passes a write error through when the note is still there' mocks writeTextFile to reject without touching the mocked disk, so it cannot see a truncated file. Likelihood is low (a window of a few ms per write), but the cost is the whole note body. The same writer is used for every tab save (editor.service.ts:169).
findings.evidence: Rust source read from the local crate cache, ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/tauri-plugin-fs-2.7.1/src/commands.rs:1125-1202 (write_file_inner: OpenOptions with truncate, then write_all); version pinned in src-tauri/Cargo.lock:5557-5558. JS side: node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-fs/dist-js/index.js:777-788 (writeTextFile sends bytes straight to plugin:fs|write_text_file). Test at frontmatter-write.service.test.ts:205-212 mocks the rejection and asserts disk is unchanged, which the mock guarantees rather than the real plugin.

verification.reasoning: tauri-plugin-fs 2.7.1 (Cargo.lock:5557-5558) write_file_inner opens with truncate:true (commands.rs:1150-1184) and then calls write_all (:1201). There is no temp file and no rename. Every TS note write uses it: the tab save (editor.service.ts:168), the closed-note frontmatter write (frontmatter-write.service.ts:149), the link updater, deep links and others. The repo already has an atomic writer, vault_fs::write_atomic (src-tauri/src/utils/fs.rs:16), but only Rust-side writers use it (task toggle, vault.rs:683). A failure mid-write (ENOSPC, I/O error, power loss, force quit) leaves the note truncated or partial. On the closed-note path the old bytes exist only in the local `base`, which is then discarded. The test at frontmatter-write.service.test.ts:205-212 mocks the rejection, so it cannot see a truncated file. Likelihood is low, but the cost is the whole note.
verification.repro: Not reproducible in vitest. Manually: fill the disk to nearly full and trigger a save of a large note, or kill -9 the app during a write of a multi-MB note, then inspect the file length.
verification.fix_hint: Route note writes through a Rust command that uses write_atomic (temp file in the same dir, fsync, rename), and keep plugin-fs writeTextFile for non-note files.

findings.title: Concurrent writers to one closed note lose an update without error
findings.scenario: Two writers target the same closed note and their read-to-write windows overlap. Writer A (Favorite, lifecycle.service.ts:50) and writer B (icon picker, frontmatter-icon.service.ts:36) both await readTextFile and both see base0. A writes base0+favorite. B then writes base0+icon. The favorite is silently gone, and nothing reports it. The doc at :91-93 says callers must serialize writes per path, but this file has no queue. event-calendar serializes per path (holdPath, :440), and bookmark migration runs sequentially, but the favorite and icon writers do not. The window is a few IPC round trips, so two UI actions would have to land within milliseconds of each other.
findings.evidence: Read: frontmatter-write.service.ts:117 (await readTextFile), :139 (await exists), :149 (await writeTextFile); no queue in the file. lifecycle.service.ts:50 and frontmatter-icon.service.ts:36 call without serialization. event-calendar.service.ts:440 holdPath chains per-path tails.

verification.reasoning: There is no per-path queue in frontmatter-write.service.ts. The closed branch awaits readTextFile (:117), exists (:139) and writeTextFile (:149), and the JSDoc (:91-93) leaves serialization to callers. lifecycle.service.ts:50 and frontmatter-icon.service.ts:36 do not serialize. Only event-calendar (holdPath) and bookmark migration (sequential) do. The race needs two writes to one closed note within a few IPC round trips, either two human UI actions in milliseconds or startup bookmark migration overlapping a user click on the same note. The path exists. Reachability depends on timing I could not settle by reading.
verification.repro: vitest: mock readTextFile with a deferred promise. Start toggleFavoriteForPath(p,true) and setFrontmatterIcon(p,'star') together, resolve both reads, and assert the final disk content has both _favorite and the icon. It will have only one.
verification.fix_hint: Add a per-path promise chain inside updateNoteFrontmatter, like event-calendar's holdPath.

findings.title: Write errors on a closed note are rethrown raw and not shown to the user
findings.scenario: A closed note is read-only (chmod 444) or otherwise not writable. The user clicks Favorite. writeTextFile rejects with EACCES, and since the file still exists, the catch at :150-153 rethrows the raw Error. toggleFavoriteForPath only toasts FrontmatterWriteError (lifecycle.service.ts:52) and rethrows anything else. NoteRowMenu.svelte:215 does not catch the promise, and src has no unhandledrejection handler (grep). Nothing is written, nothing is shown, and the favorite silently does not change. The doc at frontmatter-write.service.ts:89 says every other failure is a FrontmatterWriteError, which contradicts the code.
findings.evidence: Read the catch at frontmatter-write.service.ts:150-153 and the rethrow at lifecycle.service.ts:52 and frontmatter-icon.service.ts:39. grep for unhandledrejection in src (excluding tests) returns nothing. The test at frontmatter-write.service.test.ts:205-212 pins the raw pass-through.

verification.reasoning: In the closed-note branch, a writeTextFile rejection while the file still exists is rethrown raw (frontmatter-write.service.ts:150-153). toggleFavoriteForPath rethrows anything that is not a FrontmatterWriteError (lifecycle.service.ts:52), and so does writeIconFrontmatter (frontmatter-icon.service.ts:39). NoteRowMenu.svelte:215 calls it from onclick with no catch. grep shows no unhandledrejection handler in src. Sentry may capture it, but the user sees nothing. The JSDoc at :89 says every other failure is a FrontmatterWriteError, which the code contradicts. Nothing is lost: the write failed, so the disk and the UI keep the old state.
verification.repro: vitest: mock writeTextFile to reject with new Error('EACCES') while exists() returns true. Call toggleFavoriteForPath on a closed note and assert toast.error was called. It fails, and the promise rejects instead.
verification.fix_hint: Wrap the raw write error in a new FrontmatterWriteError reason (e.g. 'write-failed') with a toast message, or toast it in the callers.

findings.title: Unquoted [[X]] is read as text but refused as a nested value
findings.scenario: A note has `_related_to: [[Alice]]` (unquoted). The panel and the Rust index read it as the text "[[Alice]]" (folded by foldUnquotedWikilinks). Clicking Favorite calls updateNoteFrontmatter, and detectLossyFrontmatter returns 'nested' because the inner flow sequence sits inside a sequence. The write is refused with the toast 'has nested values; it cannot be rewritten without losing them'. Nothing is lost: the rewrite would emit "[[Alice]]", which reads back identically. The same false refusal reaches ensureFrontmatterLink for a second link (:546, 'Cannot add ...: frontmatter nested') and event-calendar template creation (event-calendar.service.ts:937, template-lossy).
findings.evidence: Read properties.logic.ts:111-165 (fold) and :436-446 (nested rule: a collection whose ancestor is a sequence). Read-only replication of that visit rule with the installed yaml: `related: [[X]]` -> ["nested"]; `related: "[[X]]"` -> []; `related:\n  - [[X]]` -> ["nested"]. The read side is pinned as text at properties.logic.test.ts:230-232 and the ADR-0029 amendment of 2026-11-01 (line 106) says the TS read path matches Rust on this shape, while the write refusal does not follow it.

verification.reasoning: detectLossyFrontmatter parses its own Document without foldUnquotedWikilinks (properties.logic.ts:412-446). For `[[Alice]]`, the inner flow seq has a seq ancestor, so it adds 'nested' (:440-445). The read path folds it to the string "[[Alice]]" (properties.logic.ts:111-165, test :230-232), and a rewrite would emit a quoted string that reads back the same in both TS and Rust (ADR-0029:105). The refusal is a false positive. It loses no data, but Favorite, icon and calendar writes are blocked on such notes.
verification.repro:
vitest: expect(detectLossyFrontmatter('---
rel: [[Alice]]
---
')).toBe(null) // returns 'nested'
verification.fix_hint: Run the same fold (or a shape check for one-item chains ending in a scalar) before the nested rule in detectLossyFrontmatter.

findings.title: Closing delimiter matched as a prefix, so the rest of its line is moved and changed
findings.scenario:
A note reads `---
title: a
---Hello
world
`, or has a closing line `----`. FRONTMATTER_REGEX has no end-of-line anchor, so the closing match is `---` even when text follows it on that line. extractBody returns `Hello
world
`, and rebuildContent writes `---
...
---
Hello
world
`, which inserts a line break after the closing delimiter. For `----`, the body becomes `-
body`. Only notes whose first line is `---` and whose block parses as YAML reach this path, so the likelihood is low.
findings.evidence:
Replicated extractBody and the rebuild template with the file's regex: `---
title: a
---Hello
world
` -> `---
...
---
Hello
world
`; `----` -> `---
-
body`. Code: properties.logic.ts:37, :53-57, :615-622.

verification.reasoning:
FRONTMATTER_REGEX `/^---?
([\s\S]*?)?
---/` (properties.logic.ts:37) has no end-of-line anchor. A read-only node check matched `---
title: a
---Hello
world
` with body 'Hello
world
', and `----` with body '-
body'. rebuildContent then writes `---
...
---
` + body (:621), which splits the delimiter line. No text is lost. It is a byte and structure change on rare inputs.
verification.repro:
vitest: const c='---
title: a
----
body'; expect(rebuildContent(parseFrontmatterProperties(c), extractBody(c))).toBe(c) // gets '---
title: a

findings.title: A UTF-8 BOM is dropped on every read and never written back
findings.scenario: A note starts with a UTF-8 BOM (common for files saved by some Windows editors). readTextFile decodes with new TextDecoder(encoding).decode(bytes), which strips the BOM by default. The closed-note write, and every tab save through saveFileByPath, writes the string back without it, so the first byte of the note is removed the first time any frontmatter write or save happens. This is editor-wide and sits outside this area; it is noted because it affects these writes.
findings.evidence: node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-fs/dist-js/index.js:497-498 (TextDecoder used for readTextFile). Ran a read-only node check: TextDecoder('utf-8').decode([0xEF,0xBB,0xBF,0x61]) returns "a" (length 1), so the BOM is consumed.

verification.reasoning: readTextFile uses new TextDecoder('utf-8') with ignoreBOM false (plugin-fs index.js:498), which strips a leading BOM. A node check confirms the decoded length is 1 for EF BB BF 61. Every write path (frontmatter-write.service.ts:149, editor.service.ts:168) writes the string without it. Only the BOM byte is lost, not note text.
verification.repro: Manual: create a BOM-prefixed .md file, Favorite it while closed, and check the first bytes. The BOM is gone.
verification.fix_hint: Preserve a leading BOM: read bytes, detect EF BB BF, and re-prepend it on write. Or accept it and document the behavior.

findings.title: Failed or unparseable manifest load makes the next trash operation overwrite the manifest; Empty Trash then deletes the orphaned notes
findings.scenario: 1) Trash holds notes A, B, C; their files sit in .kokobrain/trash/items/<id>/ and trash-manifest.json lists them. 2) The manifest is unreadable or truncated at launch: a crash or power loss during writeTextFile (the plugin opens with truncate, tauri-plugin-fs commands.rs:1155-1165), a sync tool rewriting it, or a one-off read error. 3) loadTrash hits JSON.parse failure (parseTrashManifest returns [] silently, trash.logic.ts:58-65) or a read error (caught, setItems([]), trash.service.ts:37-39). The Trash panel shows empty (TrashSection.svelte:82-83). No toast: loadTrash swallows everything, so the Promise.all catch in app-lifecycle (:290-294) never runs. 4) The user moves note D to trash. moveToTrash writes saveManifest(vaultPath, [itemD, ...store]) with store = [] (trash.service.ts:79), so the manifest now lists only D. A, B, C are unreferenced but their files still exist. 5) The panel shows only D. 'Empty trash' calls emptyTrash, which removes the whole items directory (:207-210), destroying A, B, C, which the user never saw. Restore (:137-139) and permanent delete (:191) persist the same overwrite. A corrupt manifest also drops malformed entries on the next save: parseTrashManifest filters them (trash.logic.ts:62) and the next write persists the drop. The existing test 'sets empty items on read error' (trash.service.test.ts:105-113) asserts the emptied store but nothing tests a save after a failed load.
findings.evidence: trash.service.ts:37-39 catch -> trashStore.setItems([]); trash.logic.ts:63-65 parse catch returns [] with no log; trash.service.ts:79 saveManifest(vaultPath, [item, ...trashStore.items]) writes unconditionally; trash.service.ts:207-213 emptyTrash removes getTrashItemsDir recursively then saves []; app-lifecycle.service.ts:288-294 wraps loadTrash in Promise.all, but loadTrash never rejects. Trace confirmed by reading all three trash files and the lifecycle caller.

verification.reasoning: Traced the full path and could not refute it. loadTrash catches every error and calls setItems([]) (trash.service.ts:37-39). parseTrashManifest returns [] on bad JSON or a non-array, and silently filters out invalid entries (trash.logic.ts:58-66). So loadTrash never rejects, and the toast in app-lifecycle.service.ts:290-294 can never fire. Next, moveToTrash writes saveManifest(vaultPath, [item, ...trashStore.items]) unconditionally (trash.service.ts:79), which overwrites the manifest with only the new entry. No code in src/lib/core/trash reconciles the items/ directory against the manifest: grep found no readDir and no orphan scan. emptyTrash then calls remove(itemsDir, {recursive:true}) (:207-210), deleting the unlisted notes the user never saw in the panel. The manifest is itself written with a plain truncating writeTextFile (:275; plugin-fs 2.7.1 commands.rs:1169-1180 opens with truncate:true), so a crash during a manifest write can produce exactly this corrupt state. No test covers a save after a failed load.
verification.repro: Vitest with the real trashStore and mocked plugin-fs: exists->true, readTextFile->'{"trunc', then loadTrash('/v'). Next call moveToTrash('/v','/v/d.md',false) and assert that writeTextFile's manifest arg contains only d. Then emptyTrash('/v') and assert remove was called on '/v/.kokobrain/trash/items' with recursive, which destroys the earlier items that are still on disk.
verification.fix_hint: Track a 'manifest load failed' flag in loadTrash and refuse to write (or toast and back up the corrupt file) while it is set. Better: rebuild missing entries by scanning items/<id>/ when the manifest is unreadable, and have emptyTrash remove only the item dirs listed in the manifest. Write the manifest via temp file + rename.

findings.title: Deleting a note from three UI surfaces drops unsaved text typed in the last ~2 s; the trash keeps the last saved bytes
findings.scenario: 1) User types in note N. The body autosave is a 2000 ms debounce (editor.service.ts:197), so the last keystrokes are only in editorStore.tabs. 2) Within 2 s of the last keystroke the user opens the row menu and confirms 'Move to Trash' (ask() at NoteRowMenu.svelte:125-127, or note-action-bar). 3) deleteItem -> applyPathChange calls closeTabsForDeletedPath(from) before diskOp (path-change.service.ts:125). That splices the tab out (editor.service.ts:356-366) with no saveFileByPath and no dirty check. 4) The pending debounce fires later, but saveDirtyTabs finds no dirty tab for N, so the tail never reaches disk. 5) The trash holds the pre-keystroke bytes. Restoring gives back a note missing the last edits, with no warning. The timer keeps running during the native confirm dialog, so the loss needs a confirm within 2 s of the last keystroke. The event-calendar path avoids this by saving first (event-calendar.service.ts:1034-1037, whose comment says deleteItem 'closes tabs without a dirty check and the Trash keeps only the disk bytes'). The explorer, note list and note action bar do not.
findings.evidence: path-change.service.ts:125 closeTabsForDeletedPath before :127 diskOp; editor.service.ts:356-366 removeTab with no save; editor.service.ts:161-176 saveFileByPath is the only flush and is not called on this path; editor.service.ts:197 debounce 2000 ms; event-calendar.service.ts:1037 calls saveFileByPath before deleteItem. No ghost recreation: saveDirtyTabs iterates current tabs (editor.service.ts:183-192).

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F165. It correctly notes the event-calendar flush at event-calendar.service.ts:1035-1037 and that the timer keeps running during ask(), which limits the common case.
verification.repro: See F165.
verification.fix_hint: See F165.

findings.title: Manifest write failure after a successful move leaves the item visible only until restart, then orphaned until Empty Trash
findings.scenario: 1) moveToTrash renames the note into items/<id>/ (:71). 2) saveManifest fails (disk full, permission, EIO); the error is logged and swallowed (:78-82) and the item is added to the in-memory store only. 3) The comment at :74-77 says the entry 'would just be re-persisted on the next save'. That holds only within this session, because any later trash operation writes the whole store. 4) If the user quits or relaunches without another trash operation, loadTrash reads a manifest without the entry. The file stays in items/<id>/, invisible in the Trash panel. 5) Empty trash later deletes it (see the emptyTrash invariant).
findings.evidence: trash.service.ts:78-83 swallows the save failure and calls trashStore.addItem; loadTrash (:24-43) rebuilds the store only from the manifest on disk; emptyTrash (:207-210) removes the whole items directory.

verification.reasoning: A swallowed manifest save after the rename (trash.service.ts:78-83) keeps the entry only in memory. The comment's 're-persisted on the next save' holds only within the session, because loadTrash rebuilds from disk (:24-43) and nothing scans items/. After a relaunch the note is invisible in the Trash and emptyTrash removes it (:207-210). The user had asked to trash it, so the impact is lost restorability, not loss of a live note. Same orphan mechanism as F61, but a different trigger.
verification.repro: Mock writeTextFile for the manifest to reject during moveToTrash, call trashStore.clear() and loadTrash with the old manifest, and assert the item is absent while rename moved the file into items/<id>.
verification.fix_hint: Same as F61: reconcile items/ against the manifest on load.

findings.title: Manifest is saved after the disk op, so a failed save leaves entries that cannot be cleared; emptyTrash comment contradicts its code
findings.scenario: (a) deletePermanently removes the container (:188), then saveManifest fails (:191). The entry stays in the manifest and the store, but the container is gone. Retrying calls remove() on the missing directory, which fails: the plugin's remove calls symlink_metadata first (tauri-plugin-fs 2.7.1 commands.rs:787-792), so it throws, the entry is never removed, and the user is stuck until Empty Trash. Restore of the same phantom fails at rename. (b) restoreItem renames the note back, then a failed saveManifest (:139-140) is logged and the in-memory entry is removed (:143). On relaunch the entry reappears; restoring it fails at rename (the source is gone), and deleting it hits the same missing-directory error. (c) emptyTrash deletes the files (:207-210) before the manifest (:213), but its comment at :212 says 'Persist manifest to disk first, then update store'. The comment is wrong, and the ordering is what creates the phantoms if the save fails.
findings.evidence: trash.service.ts:188 remove before :191 saveManifest; plugin-fs 2.7.1 commands.rs:787-792 remove errors on missing path; trash.service.ts:139-143 failure swallowed; trash.service.ts:207-213 order vs :212 comment.

verification.reasoning: (a) deletePermanently runs remove (trash.service.ts:188) before saveManifest (:191). If the save fails, it throws and the store keeps the entry. A retry hits plugin-fs remove, which calls symlink_metadata first (commands.rs:787-792) and errors on the missing directory, so the entry is stuck until Empty Trash. (b) restoreItem swallows the manifest failure (:138-143), so the entry reappears after a relaunch, and restoring it fails at rename. (c) The emptyTrash comment at :212 says 'first', but the code removes the files first (:207-210). That is only a wording mismatch. No note content is lost in any of these; they are stuck phantom entries.
verification.repro: Mock writeTextFile to reject once, then deletePermanently(v, item) rejects. Call deletePermanently again with remove mocked to reject for the missing path, and assert the item is still in trashStore.
verification.fix_hint: Treat 'not found' on remove/rename of a trash item as already-gone and drop the entry; fix the comment.

findings.title: restoreItem checks for an existing destination, then renames; a file appearing in between is silently replaced
findings.scenario: restoreItem runs exists(restorePath) (:116), then mkdir of the parent (:121-123), then rename(trashPath, restorePath) (:126). The plugin JS doc says rename replaces an existing non-directory destination, and the Rust side calls std::fs::rename (commands.rs:864). If a file with the same name appears in the window between exists and rename (a note created by the user or a sync tool, or a watcher-driven write), the restore overwrites it and that file's bytes are lost. The window is milliseconds, so this is unlikely, but the loss is silent. The fix would be a no-replace rename or a re-check after the rename. Tests cover only the pre-existing-file case.
findings.evidence: trash.service.ts:116-118 exists then findUniqueRestorePath; :126 rename; plugin-fs doc index.js:601-602 'If newpath already exists and is not a directory, rename() replaces it'; commands.rs:864 std::fs::rename.

verification.reasoning: There is a check-then-rename window: exists at trash.service.ts:116, mkdir at :121-123, rename at :126. The plugin rename is std::fs::rename (commands.rs:864), which replaces an existing file. Only an external process (sync tool) could create the file in a window of milliseconds, since the app's own creators do not run concurrently with a click-driven restore. The overwrite would be silent, but it is very unlikely.
verification.repro: Mock exists to return false, then have rename called after writing a file at restorePath; with a real fs the file would be replaced.
verification.fix_hint: Use a no-replace rename (renamex_np RENAME_EXCL on macOS / link+unlink) via a Rust command, or retry with a unique name on EEXIST.

findings.title: loadTrash has no vault check, so a slow load can fill the store with a previous vault's items after a switch
findings.scenario: Vault A starts loadTrash (readTextFile in flight). The user switches to vault B: teardown calls resetTrash (:643), and loadTrash(B) starts. If A's read resolves after B's load began, setItems(A's items) runs (:35) and the store shows A's entries. A later moveToTrash in B then writes A's entries into B's manifest (:79). The Trash panel in B then lists items whose files are in A, and restore or delete on them fails at rename or remove. No file is destroyed, but B's manifest is contaminated. The lifecycle version guard (app-lifecycle.service.ts:294) runs after the await in the caller, not in the store write. This needs an unlikely read-ordering race and I did not reproduce it.
findings.evidence: trash.service.ts:24-35 has no vault or version check before setItems; app-lifecycle.service.ts:288 starts the load; :643 resetTrash clears the store with no cancellation of an in-flight load.

verification.reasoning: loadTrash has no vault or version check before setItems (trash.service.ts:24-35). resetTrash (app-lifecycle.service.ts:643) does not cancel an in-flight load, and the initVersion guard (:296) runs only in the caller after Promise.all. Contamination needs vault A's tiny manifest read to resolve after vault B's, which is unlikely. No file is destroyed, but B's manifest could gain dangling entries.
verification.repro: Control readTextFile promises: start loadTrash('/A'), then resetTrash and loadTrash('/B') resolving first, then resolve A. Assert trashStore.items holds A's entries.
verification.fix_hint: Capture vaultPath and compare it with vaultStore.path (or a generation counter) before setItems.

findings.title: Restore writes the snapshot into whichever note is the active tab, not the inspected file
findings.scenario: 1) Open note A and press Cmd+Shift+H; the history dialog lists A's snapshots. 2) While the dialog is still open, press Cmd+O and open note B (or press Cmd+Shift+] / Cmd+W, which changes the active tab). B becomes the active tab and the single CodeMirror view is reloaded with B's content. 3) The dialog still holds filePath=A and its snapshots; nothing closes it on a tab change. 4) Click 'Restore This Version' on an A snapshot and confirm the prompt, which names 'this file'. restoreSnapshot fetches A's old text and dispatches it into editorStore.editorView, which now shows B. The update listener calls onContentChange, which sets B.content, and saveCurrentFile then calls saveFileByPath(B.path), overwriting note B on disk with A's old text. Only B's previously saved states survive in B's snapshot history. Unsaved B edits and content never saved through the app are lost.
findings.evidence: service.ts:86-99 uses fileHistoryStore.filePath only for a null check (line 86-87); the dispatch targets editorStore.editorView (line 90), which is the one global view (MarkdownEditor.svelte:132) and follows the active tab (MarkdownEditor.svelte:170-235). The write goes to editorStore.activeTab.path (editor.service.ts:151-154). The keybinding registry has no dialog guard (utils/keybindings.ts:30-49; the only dialog check is the '/' listener in global-keybindings.ts:44). Mod-W, Mod-Shift-[/] and Mod-O are global (global-keybindings.ts:69-100). openFileInEditor adds a tab and makes it active (editor.store.svelte.ts:52-61). closeTab and closeTabsForDeletedPath notify only registerTabCloseListener subscribers, and file-history does not subscribe (only queryjs-ports.ts:16 registers one). Nothing in file-history compares activeTabPath with filePath.

verification.reasoning: I could not refute it. restoreSnapshot uses fileHistoryStore.filePath only for a null check (file-history.service.ts:86-87). It dispatches into the single global editorStore.editorView (:90-95, set at MarkdownEditor.svelte:132), and the update listener (editor-extensions.ts:170-188) calls onContentChange -> editorStore.updateContent, which writes tabs[activeIndex] (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-87). saveCurrentFile then saves editorStore.activeTab (editor.service.ts:151-155), so the write never targets filePath. The path is reachable while the modal is open: registerKeybinding listens on document with no dialog guard (utils/keybindings.ts:30-49). bits-ui dialog.svelte.js keydown handlers only act on Space/Enter for trigger, close and cancel, with no stopPropagation. The native menu (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:184-213) has no Cmd+W item, so Cmd+W reaches closeActiveTab, and closing A (when clean) activates another tab. Cmd+Shift+[ and ] switch tabs (global-keybindings.ts:82-99). Nothing closes the dialog on a tab change, and the file-history tests never exercise a different active tab. The result is that note B's disk bytes are replaced by A's old text, and B's unsaved edits are lost.
verification.repro: Vitest: real editorStore with tabs A (active) and B, and a fake editorView whose dispatch calls onContentChange. openFileHistory('/v/A.md') with mocked call(). Then switchTab(1) and restoreSnapshot(id). Assert writeTextFile was called with '/v/B.md' and the snapshot text, and never with '/v/A.md'.
verification.fix_hint: In restoreSnapshot, after the awaits, require editorStore.activeTabPath === fileHistoryStore.filePath. Otherwise write the snapshot to filePath directly (update that tab's content if open, or writeTextFile + notifyAfterSave), or abort with a toast. Also close the dialog when the active tab changes.

findings.title: Restore discards unsaved buffer text without snapshotting it
findings.scenario: Type a paragraph into note A and press Cmd+Shift+H before 2 s have passed since the last keystroke. Open the dialog and pick a snapshot. The dialog's 'current' side is the on-disk file, so the typed paragraph is not in the diff. Click Restore and confirm. restoreSnapshot replaces the whole CodeMirror doc with the snapshot text and saves it. The typed paragraph was never written to disk and no snapshot was taken of it, so it is unrecoverable. During a continuous typing burst the buffer can stay dirty for longer than 2 s, because the debounce restarts on every keystroke. The confirmation text ('Current content will be replaced') only partly covers this, since the diff the user reviewed did not show the unsaved text.
findings.evidence: openFileHistory reads the disk content (service.ts:28-29) and never flushes the editor first. restoreSnapshot (service.ts:85-99) dispatches a replacement of the whole doc and then saveCurrentFile writes only the restored text. Nothing calls saveFileByPath or notifyAfterSave on the pre-restore buffer. The body auto-save is a debounce that resets on each call (debounce.ts:9-17, scheduled from editor.service.ts:224-227 with 2000 ms at line 197).

verification.reasoning: The data-loss claim does not hold for the realistic flow. The 2000 ms body debounce is a plain setTimeout (debounce.ts:9-17, editor.service.ts:197) that keeps running while the modal and the native ask() are open. Focus is in the dialog, so no further keystrokes reset it. By the time the user has opened history, picked a snapshot, clicked Restore and confirmed, the unsaved text has normally been saved, and the after-save hook (file-history.service.ts:190+) has snapshotted it. Even inside 2 s, restore's view.dispatch (:92-94) is an ordinary transaction that CodeMirror's history can undo. What remains: openFileHistory diffs against disk content (:28-29), not the buffer, so the 'current' side can be up to 2 s stale. That is cosmetic.
verification.repro: In the app: type, press Cmd+Shift+H, wait 2 s, restore, then reopen history. The pre-restore text appears as the newest snapshot.
verification.fix_hint: Optionally flush (saveFileByPath) before reading currentContent in openFileHistory so the diff is exact.

findings.title: Restore on a non-markdown active tab silently does nothing and closes the dialog
findings.scenario: Open a kanban board note (.md with fileType kanban) in board view, or a canvas, collection or other non-markdown tab. MarkdownEditor is not mounted for these tabs (EditorView.svelte:79-85), so its onDestroy has set editorView to null (MarkdownEditor.svelte:147-149). restoreSnapshot skips the dispatch (service.ts:90-95), saveCurrentFile sees a clean tab and returns without writing (editor.service.ts:162-163), and reset() closes the dialog. The user sees no error or toast, and the file is unchanged.

EditorView.svelte:79-83 renders Kanban, Canvas or Collection views instead of MarkdownEditor, whose destroy sets editorView null (MarkdownEditor.svelte:148). restoreSnapshot skips the dispatch when view is null (file-history.service.ts:91), saveCurrentFile returns early on a clean tab (editor.service.ts:162), and reset() closes the dialog (:100) with no toast.
