findings.title: Restore reports success when the write to disk failed
findings.scenario: The disk write fails during Restore (for example a permission error). saveFileByPath shows the toast 'Failed to save file.' and returns false. saveCurrentFile discards that boolean, so restoreSnapshot continues to reset(), which closes the dialog as if the restore worked. The restored text stays dirty in the buffer and the body auto-save retries it, so content is not lost, but the dialog has already closed.
findings.evidence: saveCurrentFile does 'await saveFileByPath(tab.path);' without returning the result (editor.service.ts:154). saveFileByPath returns false in its catch (editor.service.ts:176). restoreSnapshot calls fileHistoryStore.reset() unconditionally after the await (service.ts:100).

verification.reasoning: saveCurrentFile ignores saveFileByPath's boolean (editor.service.ts:154). saveFileByPath returns false after toasting (:174-176). restoreSnapshot then calls reset() unconditionally (file-history.service.ts:100). The restored text stays dirty in the buffer, but note that restore's dispatch path does not arm a debounce: onContentChange via the update listener does call scheduleAutoSave, so retry happens. No content loss; only the dialog closes on failure.
verification.repro: Mock writeTextFile to reject and call restoreSnapshot. Assert that the toast 'Failed to save file.' was shown and that fileHistoryStore.isOpen is false.
verification.fix_hint: Return the boolean from saveCurrentFile (or call saveFileByPath directly) and keep the dialog open with an error on false.

findings.title: Restore errors go unhandled and show no message to the user
findings.scenario: get_snapshot_content or the save throws (for example the snapshot row was removed by cleanup while the dialog was open). restoreSnapshot logs with error() and rethrows. handleRestore has no try/catch, so the rejection goes unhandled in the click handler and the user sees nothing. The dialog stays open with no explanation.
findings.evidence: service.ts:101-104 ends with 'throw err;'. FileHistoryDialog.svelte:40-51 awaits restoreSnapshot with no catch and no toast, unlike the project rule that user-facing errors should show a toast.

verification.reasoning: restoreSnapshot rethrows (file-history.service.ts:101-104). handleRestore awaits it with no catch (FileHistoryDialog.svelte:40-51). grep found no unhandledrejection handler in src/lib or src/routes. error() logs and reports to Sentry but does not toast. The user sees nothing and nothing is written.
verification.repro: Mock call('get_snapshot_content') to reject, click Restore in a component test, and assert no toast was shown and the dialog is still open.
verification.fix_hint: Wrap the restoreSnapshot call in handleRestore with try/catch -> toast.error.

findings.title: History is keyed by path, so a renamed or deleted note's snapshots show up for a new file at the same path
findings.scenario: Note A.md has history. Rename it to B.md. Path-change does not touch snapshot rows, so B.md shows 'No history' and A.md's rows remain. Create a new A.md, type some text, and save. Open history for the new A.md: the list shows the OLD note's snapshots, because the key is only the relative path. Restoring one of them replaces the new A.md's content with the old note's text. The dialog does not show that the note's identity changed. The new note's own saved states are also in the same list, so they are recoverable from history, but the restore is silent about the mismatch.
findings.evidence: get_file_history and save_snapshot use only file_path (history.rs:57-84), and list_snapshots filters on file_path alone (history_repo.rs:46-50). A grep of path-change.service.ts shows no reference to history or snapshot tables, so renames and moves never re-key rows. The key is the vault-relative path derived in service.ts:115 and 31.

verification.reasoning: Confirmed: snapshots are keyed only by file_path (history.rs:57-84, history_repo.rs:18-26, 46-50), and path-change.service.ts never re-keys them. The real consequence is that a renamed or moved note loses visible access to its history, which weakens recovery. Bringing an old snapshot into a new same-path note is not silent corruption: the user picks it after seeing a diff and confirming. No note bytes are lost by this alone.
verification.repro: Save A.md twice, renameItem to B.md, and call get_file_history('B.md'), which is empty. Create a new A.md and get_file_history('A.md') returns the old rows.
verification.fix_hint: Register a path-change consumer that re-keys snapshots (UPDATE snapshots SET file_path for from and prefix) on rename/move; keep rows on delete.

findings.title: Out-of-order snapshot selection shows one snapshot's diff while restoring another
findings.scenario: Click snapshot A (large, so its IPC is slow) and then snapshot B quickly. selectSnapshot(A) sets selectedSnapshot=A, then awaits get_snapshot_content and compute_diff. selectSnapshot(B) sets selectedSnapshot=B and its results arrive first, so diffLines=B's diff and loadingDiff=false. When A's IPC resolves it calls setDiffLines(A) with no sequence check. The right pane now shows A's diff under B's header, and 'Restore This Version' restores B (handleRestore reads selectedSnapshot). The user reviews one version and restores another.
findings.evidence: selectSnapshot has no request token or check that the snapshot is still selected before setDiffLines (service.ts:56-77, calls at 58, 62-68, 71). The header and restore use fileHistoryStore.selectedSnapshot (FileHistoryDialog.svelte:85-89, 40-50). The out-of-order arrival depends on IPC timing, so this is not reproduced.

verification.reasoning: The code has no request token: selectSnapshot sets selectedSnapshot first (file-history.service.ts:58) and setDiffLines later (:71). handleRestore uses selectedSnapshot (FileHistoryDialog.svelte:41). Out-of-order IPC completion depends on timing: both are sync Rust commands, and I could not settle whether they are serialized. The restore is of the snapshot whose header is shown, so what is restored is the labelled version, though the diff can be stale.
verification.repro: Mock call so that get_snapshot_content for id 1 resolves after id 2. Call selectSnapshot(s1) and then selectSnapshot(s2) without awaiting. Assert diffLines equals s1's diff while selectedSnapshot is s2.
verification.fix_hint: Capture snapshot.id and skip setDiffLines/setLoadingDiff if fileHistoryStore.selectedSnapshot?.id changed.

findings.title: Backup 'show in Finder' can open another snapshot's backup file
findings.scenario: Save note A at t=1000 (Rust created_at=1000), which writes backup 1003.md (JS Date.now() after the IPC returns). Save again at t=6000, which writes backup 6004.md. For snapshot t=6000, findBackupTimestamp checks the set in Set iteration order and returns the first entry within 10 s, which can be 1003 rather than 6004. The backup icon for the second snapshot then reveals the first snapshot's backup file in Finder.
findings.evidence: findBackupTimestamp returns the first Set member within tolerance (file-history.logic.ts:168-172) instead of the nearest. The backup name comes from Date.now() after the IPC (service.ts:121-122). The snapshot timestamp is the Rust created_at (history.rs:63-64). Two saves within 10 s are plausible.

verification.reasoning: findBackupTimestamp returns the first Set member within 10 s (file-history.logic.ts:168-172), not the nearest. Backup names use JS Date.now() after the IPC (file-history.service.ts:121), while snapshots use Rust now_ms (history.rs:64), so exact matches are rare. Autosave can create snapshots 2 s apart (dedupe is only on identical hashes, history.rs:67-71), so it can return a neighbouring snapshot's backup. This only affects the Reveal in Finder target.
verification.repro: findBackupTimestamp(6000, new Set([1003, 6004])) returns 1003.
verification.fix_hint: Return the backup timestamp with minimal |delta| within tolerance.

findings.title: Diff view renders every unchanged line, which can freeze the dialog on large notes
findings.scenario: Open history on a note with tens of thousands of lines and select any snapshot. compute_diff returns an Equal entry for every unchanged line, not just hunks with context, and DiffViewer renders each one as a table row with four cells and no virtualization or folding. The DOM can reach hundreds of thousands of nodes, which can make selecting a snapshot slow. Not measured.
findings.evidence: history.rs:103-112 pushes a DiffLine with DiffLineType::Equal for every unchanged line. DiffViewer.svelte:41-52 renders each entry as a <tr> with four <td> cells and no windowing.

verification.reasoning: compute_diff emits an Equal row for every unchanged line (history.rs:103-112), and DiffViewer renders every row with 4 cells and no windowing (DiffViewer.svelte:39-54). That is slow on very large notes, but I measured nothing and the cost is bounded by note size. There is no content risk.
verification.repro: Open history for a 50k-line note and time the render of the snapshot selection.
verification.fix_hint: Collapse long Equal runs to context hunks or virtualize the table.

findings.title: Toggling a task discards unsaved typing in the note's open tab
findings.scenario: 1) User types in note A. Keystrokes go only to tab.content (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88, via onContentChange at editor.service.ts:224-227). The autosave is a trailing 2000 ms debounce (editor.service.ts:197), so the text is unsaved until 2 s pass without typing. 2) Within that window the user opens the Tasks tab (toggleTasksTab, or clicks the tab). EditorView swaps in TasksView and unmounts MarkdownEditor; onDestroy only saves scroll/cursor and destroys the view (MarkdownEditor.svelte:147-165). setActiveIndex does not flush (editor.store.svelte.ts:64-68). 3) User clicks a checkbox that belongs to note A. toggle_task_status reads the DISK copy (vault.rs:669), which lacks the unsaved text, toggles one line, and writes it. 4) toggleTask then calls syncExternalContentToEditor(path, updatedContent, markSaved=true) (tasks.service.ts:113), which sets content and savedContent to the disk-derived text (editor.service.ts:80, editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136) and marks the tab clean. The pending debounced save then sees a clean tab and writes nothing. Result: every character typed since the last autosave is gone from the buffer and from disk. The external CodeMirror replace is added with addToHistory false (MarkdownEditor.svelte:332), so undo cannot recover it. The codebase already guards this case elsewhere: link-updater.service.ts:33-35 uses the in-memory buffer for dirty tabs ('to avoid losing them'), and reloadExternallyChangedTabs skips dirty tabs (editor.service.ts:378-380). toggleTask has neither check and does not flush first.
findings.evidence: tasks.service.ts:102-115 calls toggle_task_status and then syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, updatedContent, true, 'none') with no isTabDirty check and no saveFileByPath first. vault.rs:669-670 reads from disk: std::fs::read_to_string(path). editor.service.ts:70-92: markSaved true calls updateTabContentByPath, which sets tab.content = content and tab.savedContent = content (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136). scheduleAutoSave('none') is a no-op (editor.service.ts:213-221). MarkdownEditor.svelte:328-333 replaces the whole doc with addToHistory false. EditorView.svelte:68-71 renders TasksView instead of MarkdownEditor when the Tasks tab is active. Contrast: link-updater.service.ts:33-35 and editor.service.ts:378-380.

verification.reasoning: Same mechanism as F2. Its added detail (addToHistory false at MarkdownEditor.svelte:332, and onDestroy not saving content at :147-165) is verified and folded into F2.
verification.repro: See F2.
verification.fix_hint: See F2.

findings.title: write_atomic has no fsync before rename, so a crash can leave an empty or stale note
findings.scenario: toggle_task_status, propagate_type_rename or create_note runs write_atomic. The bytes sit in the page cache, then rename() replaces the note. If power is lost or the kernel panics after the rename metadata commits but before the temp file's data blocks reach disk, the note can come back zero-length, or as the old content if the rename itself did not persist. The fs.rs:11-15 doc promises 'never a truncated/empty note', which the code does not guarantee. The project's own index_cache writer does fsync before rename (index_cache.rs:66-72: 'write to .tmp, fsync, rename'), so the omission is inconsistent with the team's own pattern.
findings.evidence: fs.rs:27 uses std::fs::write(&tmp, content), which opens, writes and closes with no sync_all. fs.rs:28 then calls rename. There is no sync_all or sync_data anywhere in the write path (grep of src-tauri/src for sync_all/fsync finds only index_cache.rs:70 and db/mod.rs:77). Whether APFS can persist the rename before the data is a filesystem-behaviour question I did not verify against a primary source; it is stated from memory. The POSIX point (rename does not order data writes) is general knowledge, not checked against a source here.

verification.reasoning: Confirmed that write_atomic has no sync_all before the rename (utils/fs.rs:27-28). The only sync_all in src-tauri is in index_cache.rs:70. Whether APFS can persist the rename before the data blocks, leaving a zero-length note after power loss, is unverified (from memory). On macOS even fsync needs F_FULLFSYNC for durability. This affects only the task toggle, create_note and type rename writes, and its crash window is far smaller than the editor save's (F182).
verification.repro: Not testable in unit tests; needs a power-cut harness.
verification.fix_hint: Open the temp, write_all, sync_all (or F_FULLFSYNC on macOS) before rename; optionally fsync the parent dir.

findings.title: Frontmatter type rename writes the new name unquoted, so names with YAML syntax change the member's type
findings.scenario: User renames type 'Book' to 'Book #2' (or '[Projects]', or '#ideas'). validateTypeName only checks file-name legality (fs.logic.ts:117-124 forbids only control chars and <>:"/\\|?*), so '#', '[', '#' at the start, and similar are accepted. For an unquoted original value, rewrite_type_line writes the new name raw: '_type: Book #2'. In YAML, ' #' starts a comment, so the value is 'Book'. The members are then indexed under type 'Book', which has no definition note, and they drop out of 'Book #2'. For '[Projects]' the value is a flow sequence, extract_is_a returns None (entry.rs:362-369), and the members lose their type entirely. The bytes written differ from what the user chose, and membership changes silently. The TS mirror used for open tabs has the same raw write (type-definitions.logic.ts:205).
findings.evidence: parsing.rs:148-152: new_value = match quote { Some(q) => format!("{q}{new_type}{q}"), None => new_type.to_string() }, then format!("{key}: {new_value}{ending}"). No escaping or quoting for unquoted values. type-definitions.logic.ts:205 has the same raw interpolation. validateTypeName (type-definitions.logic.ts:157-166) calls isValidFileName, which (fs.logic.ts:117-124) does not reject '#', '[', '{', '&', '*', '!', '|', '>', '%', '@', backtick or leading quotes. TypesNavigator.svelte:368-369 wires this validator to the rename dialog. The YAML comment rule (whitespace before '#') is from the YAML 1.2 spec and was not checked against yaml-rust2's source here.

verification.reasoning: rewrite_type_line writes new_type raw for unquoted values (parsing.rs:148-152), and the TS mirror does the same (type-definitions.logic.ts:205). validateTypeName relies on getFileNameError, which forbids only control characters, a leading '.', and <>:"/\|?* (fs.logic.ts:117-124), so '#', '[', '{', '&', '*', '!', '|' and '@' are accepted. Per the YAML spec (from memory; yaml-rust2 source not checked), 'Book #2' parses as 'Book', and '[Projects]' or '{x}' parses as a collection. The members then change or lose their type silently, which corrupts the meaning of frontmatter without losing bytes. Creation has the same raw interpolation (type-definitions.service.ts:73).
verification.repro:
cargo unit test: rewrite_type_in_frontmatter("---
_type: Book
---
","Book","Book #2") yields '_type: Book #2'. Parse it with yaml-rust2 and the value is 'Book'. TS test: parseFrontmatterProperties of the output gives _type 'Book'.
verification.fix_hint: Quote the type value when it is not a safe plain scalar (always double-quote with escaping is simplest), in both Rust and TS and in resolveTypedNoteTarget. Or reject YAML indicator characters in validateTypeName.

findings.title: toggle_task_status has no staleness guard, so a stale line number can flip a different task's checkbox
findings.scenario: The Tasks list holds lineNumber values from the last get_all_tasks_v2 fetch. That fetch refreshes on the throttled vault-index-updated bump (REFRESH_DELAY_MS 2000, REFRESH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS 10000; tauri-listeners.service.ts:84-87). User inserts a line above task T in note A and autosave runs. Within the refresh window the list still shows T at its old line N. Clicking T's checkbox sends lineNumber=N, and Rust flips whatever task marker is on line N now, which is task U. toggle_task_in_content only checks that the line has a marker (parsing.rs:1889-1892). The toggle is recoverable by clicking again, and the mis-toggle is visible in the list, but the note's bytes change on the wrong line silently. If line N has no marker, the call is a no-op.
findings.evidence: vault.rs:671 calls toggle_task_in_content(&original, line_number) with no expected-text or hash argument. parsing.rs:1878-1892 uses line_number - 1 and flips the marker found on that line, with no content check. tasks.service.ts:102-104 sends only path and lineNumber. TasksView.svelte:207 passes task.lineNumber from the stale list.

verification.reasoning: toggle_task_in_content (src-tauri/src/vault/parsing.rs:1873-1906) addresses the task only by line_number. It checks only that a TASK_RE / ORDERED_TASK_RE marker is on that line and then flips it blindly (' ' becomes 'x', any other state becomes ' ', :1896-1900). There is no expected-text check. tasks.service.ts:102-105 sends {path, lineNumber}. TasksView refetches only on vaultIndexVersion (TasksView.svelte:78-83) or after its own toggle, and the bump is throttled (REFRESH_DELAY_MS 2000, MIN_INTERVAL 10000; tauri-listeners.service.ts:84-88). I found two reachable desyncs. (B) Insert a line above tasks and switch to Tasks within 1 s. The layout content effect is cleared because the active tab becomes virtual (+layout.svelte:137-155), so TasksView fetches the old line numbers. The 2 s autosave then writes the shifted file, and the list stays stale until the throttled bump. A click flips the neighbouring task on disk. (A, from F162) After at least 1 s idle, the 'edit' source pushes the unsaved buffer into VaultIndex. note-change.service.ts:88 has rust:'deduped', and :227-232 call update_note_in_index when the content is not deduped, so CLAUDE.md's 'edit skips both' is inaccurate. The Tasks list then shows buffer line numbers while Rust toggles the disk copy (vault.rs:669). A wrong-line hit also erases '[-]' / '[/]' states. The edit is visible in the file and can be undone by hand, but it changes the wrong line silently.
verification.repro:
Rust unit test: content '- [ ] A
- [ ] B'. Simulate a line inserted above, giving '- [ ] new
- [ ] A
- [ ] B'. Call toggle_task_in_content(content, 2) with the stale line for B. It flips A. Manual (B): add a line above a task, switch to the Tasks tab within 1 s, wait 2 s, then click the task. A different task gets checked on disk.
verification.fix_hint: Pass the expected line text (or the task text plus status) to toggle_task_status and refuse when the line at line_number does not match. Optionally search nearby lines for the match.

findings.title: toggle_task_status writes any path the frontend sends, skipping the ensure_safe_write_path check
findings.scenario: create_note and create_folder call ensure_safe_write_path (vault.rs:895, 924). toggle_task_status does not. Its path arrives over IPC and is read and rewritten with std::fs, with no absolute-path, '..' or vault-containment check and no .md requirement. A file outside the vault is rewritten if any line that the frontend numbers as a task marker matches. Reaching this needs a compromised webview or a bad caller. The vault.rs:853-861 doc says these std::fs commands must validate their targets because plugin-fs ACLs do not cover them, and toggle breaks that rule.
findings.evidence: vault.rs:664-669 reads std::fs::read_to_string(path) with no validation. vault.rs:707-713 is the command wrapper with no check. ensure_safe_write_path is called only at vault.rs:895 and vault.rs:924. The index-side guard (update_note_in_index_inner, vault.rs:275) does not stop the disk write, which happens first.

verification.reasoning: toggle_task_status_inner reads and write_atomic's the IPC-supplied path (vault.rs:664-683), and the command wrapper (:707+) never calls ensure_safe_write_path, unlike create_note (:895). This is defense in depth: a write needs a compromised webview or a bad caller, plus a checkbox at that line. Note that ensure_safe_write_path itself checks only absolute paths and '..', not vault containment.
verification.repro: cargo test: toggle_task_status_inner on a relative path or a '../x.md' path succeeds today, where it should return Err.
verification.fix_hint: Call ensure_safe_write_path(&path) (and ideally check that the path is a known index entry) before reading.

findings.title: write_atomic replaces the inode, dropping the note's file mode and extended attributes
findings.scenario: A note with mode 0600, or with extended attributes such as Finder tags, is saved through toggle_task_status or propagate_type_rename. rename() installs a new inode, created by std::fs::write with the default mode (0666 minus umask), so the file becomes 0644 and loses xattrs. Note bytes are unchanged, but permissions and metadata change silently. The doc at fs.rs:17-19 covers only the read-only check, not this side effect.
findings.evidence: fs.rs:27 creates the temp file with std::fs::write (default mode). fs.rs:28 renames it over the target. Nothing copies the original permissions or xattrs before the rename.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F188: the inode swap in write_atomic (utils/fs.rs:26-28) drops mode and xattrs.
verification.repro: See F188.
verification.fix_hint: See F188.

findings.title: A failed write leaves a partial .tmp file that the file tree shows
findings.scenario: Disk full in the middle of std::fs::write(&tmp, content). The `?` at fs.rs:27 returns before the cleanup in the rename closure (fs.rs:29), so Note.md.tmp-<pid>-<seq> stays on disk with partial bytes. The original note is intact. The leftover is a non-hidden file, so scan_dir lists it in the explorer (vault.rs:103-105 skips only dot-prefixed names), and nothing removes it later.
findings.evidence: fs.rs:27 uses `?` with no remove_file. The remove_file cleanup exists only in the rename map_err closure at fs.rs:29.

verification.reasoning: The `?` at utils/fs.rs:27 returns before any cleanup, because remove_file exists only in the rename error closure (:29-30). The temp name `<note>.tmp-<pid>-<n>` does not start with '.', so scan_dir lists it (vault.rs:102-104 skips only dot-prefixed names). The original note is intact, so this is only clutter.
verification.repro: Rust test: call write_atomic into a directory where creating the temp fails mid-write (hard to force), or inject the error via a full tmpfs. Check that the .tmp file remains.
verification.fix_hint: On write error, remove the temp file; name temps with a leading dot so scans skip them.

findings.title: propagate_type_rename does disk I/O under the VaultIndex write lock on a synchronous command
findings.scenario: A type with many member notes is renamed. propagate_type_rename is a sync Tauri command that takes state.write() and holds it while reading, rewriting and reparsing every member file (propagate_type_rename_inner). That blocks every index reader (backlinks, tags, tasks) for the whole pass. The project's own comment at vault.rs:1087-1092 says sync commands run on the IPC thread and block other invokes, so this could stall the UI for the length of the pass. Not measured.
findings.evidence: vault.rs:396-401 declares pub fn (not async). vault.rs:403-408 holds the write guard across propagate_type_rename_inner, which loops over every member (vault.rs:356-384) with read, write_atomic and reparse per file.

verification.reasoning: propagate_type_rename is a sync command (vault.rs:396) that holds state.write() across the per-member read, write_atomic and reindex loop (:403-408, 356-384). The repo's own comment says sync commands block the IPC thread (vault.rs:1087-1092). How long the stall lasts depends on member count and disk speed, which was not measured.
verification.repro: Bench: a vault with 2,000 members of type T. Rename T and time other invokes issued during the rename.
verification.fix_hint: Make it async with spawn_blocking, do the disk I/O outside the write lock, then take the lock only for the batch reindex.

findings.title: Undo after a note switch or external sync re-inserts deleted text into the wrong note and autosaves it
locations: node_modules/@codemirror/commands/dist/index.js:240-241 (addMapping for addToHistory=false), :404 (stored change is tr.changes.invert), :484-486 (mapEvent maps stored changes)
findings.scenario: One MarkdownEditor view is reused for markdown-to-markdown tab switches (EditorView.svelte:85 keeps one {:else} branch), so history() is shared by all notes. Steps: (1) in note A, delete 'has' from 'Note A has text' (recorded in undo history); (2) click note B (the full-doc replace with addToHistory=false maps A's undo entry through the replacement); (3) press Cmd+Z in B. Undo replays the mapped inverse into B, producing 'Note B bodyhas'. The updateListener sees a docChanged with neither suppression flag set, so onContentChange (editor.service.ts:224-227) updates tabs[activeIndex] and the 2 s autosave writes B.md. The same path runs on an external sync: 'abc foo def' -> delete 'foo ' -> external replace to 'abc def\n- [x] task' (frontmatter-write.service.ts:128, editor.service.ts:401, link-updater.service.ts:47) -> Undo gives 'abc def\n- [x] taskfoo '. A round trip A->B->A followed by Undo in A appends 'has' to the end of A ('Note A  texthas'). Any ordinary deletion followed by a note switch or external write, then Undo, silently inserts text at a document boundary of the wrong content, and autosave persists it.
findings.evidence: Reproduced in memory with the repo's installed @codemirror/state 6.7.6 and @codemirror/commands 6.11.1: history() plus a full-doc replace with Transaction.addToHistory.of(false), then the commands' undo(). (a) 'Note A has text' -> delete [7,10) -> replace whole doc with 'Note B body' -> undo gives 'Note B bodyhas'; (b) 'abc foo def' -> delete [4,8) -> replace with 'abc def\n- [x] task' -> undo gives 'abc def\n- [x] taskfoo '; (c) round trip A->B->A -> undo gives 'Note A  texthas'. An insertion undo (user typed text, then external replace) was dropped, not corrupted. No test in src/tests covers undo across a tab switch or external sync (grep for undo in src/tests/lib/core/markdown-editor and src/tests/lib/core/editor finds no such case). The app's Cmd+Z has no global interception outside the calendar, so historyKeymap handles it.

verification.reasoning: I tried to refute it and could not. EditorView.svelte:84-85 mounts one MarkdownEditor in the {:else} branch for every markdown and code tab, so the EditorView and its single history() (editor-extensions.ts:130, historyKeymap at :153) outlive tab switches. EditorState.create runs only at mount (MarkdownEditor.svelte:107). A grep of src/lib for isolateHistory, historyField, clearHistory or setState( finds nothing outside canvas, so nothing resets history. The tab switch (MarkdownEditor.svelte:230-235) and the external sync (:329-333) both replace the whole doc with Transaction.addToHistory.of(false). In @codemirror/commands 6.11.1 that path only calls state.addMapping(tr.changes.desc) (dist/index.js:240-241). addMappingToBranch/mapEvent (:460-486) keeps every stored event that still has changes after mapping, and an inverted deletion is an insertion that survives a full-doc replace. Neither guard flag is set during the later undo transaction: isTabSwitching and isExternalEdit go back to false right after each dispatch (:236, :334). So the updateListener (editor-extensions.ts:171-188) calls onDocChanged, then onContentChange (MarkdownEditor.svelte:124), then editor.service.ts:224-227 (updateContent + scheduleAutoSave), and the wrong bytes are written about 2 s later. I reproduced it in memory with the repo's own @codemirror/state 6.7.6 and commands 6.11.1: 'Note A has text', delete 'has ', full replace with 'Note B body', undo gives 'Note B bodyhas '. Same-note external sync: 'abc foo def', delete 'foo ', replace, undo gives 'abc def\n- [x] taskfoo '. Redo variant: type ' secret' in A, undo, switch, redo gives 'Note B body secret'. An undo of a typed insertion was dropped (undo returned false), which matches the claim that deletion-type edits are the trigger. No test in src/tests/lib/core/markdown-editor or core/editor covers undo across a tab switch or an external sync. I rate it high, not critical: no existing bytes are removed, but foreign text (possibly private text from another note) is silently appended to the wrong note and autosaved. In the same-note case, Cmd+Z puts recovered text at the end of the note instead of where it was deleted, often off-screen.
verification.repro: Vitest sketch with the real packages: let st = EditorState.create({doc:'Note A has text', extensions:[history()]}); st = st.update({changes:{from:7,to:11}, userEvent:'delete.backward'}).state; st = st.update({changes:{from:0,to:st.doc.length,insert:'Note B body'}, annotations:Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)}).state; undo({state:st, dispatch:tr=>{st=tr.state}}); expect(st.doc.toString()).toBe('Note B body') // fails today: 'Note B bodyhas '. In the app: delete a word in note A, click the tab of markdown note B, press Cmd+Z, wait 2 s, and B.md on disk ends with A's deleted word.
verification.fix_hint: Keep one history per tab. On a tab switch, either swap in a per-tab EditorState with view.setState (cached per path, so A's undo stack comes back when A is reopened), or at least clear the history by reconfiguring a Compartment that wraps history() (historyCompartment.reconfigure([]) and then history() again) in the same dispatch as the doc replace. For the external sync, replace the full-doc insert with a minimal diff (common prefix/suffix) so the stored undo entries map to the right positions, or clear history there too. Add a MarkdownEditor test: delete in A, switch to B, undo must not change B, and the store's B content must stay unchanged.

findings.title: Unclosed or stray $$ line makes the lezer parser swallow the rest of the block structure and hide prose in live preview
locations: src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/lezer/math-extension.ts:76-91 (loop advances with cx.nextLine(); returns false at :91 after consuming lines)
node_modules/@lezer/markdown/dist/index.js:783-790 (advance continues block parsers on the same shared Line object after a false return)
src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/plugins/block-math-field.ts:16-30 (opener replaced by MathWidget, content lines hidden with hideLines)
findings.scenario:
(a) The user types a lone '$$' line before the formula, with a heading or list below it: 'Intro

$$
x^2

# Heading

- item' parses to Document[0,32] Paragraph[0,5] only. Without MathExtension the same input gives Paragraph, ATXHeading1 and BulletList nodes, so the heading and list lose their live-preview styling until the closing $$ is typed. (b) A stray '$$' followed later by a real formula pairs with it: '$$
Some text
# Heading
$$
x^2
$$' parses to BlockMath[0,25] covering 'Some text' and '# Heading'. block-math-field then replaces the opener with a KaTeX widget and hides the prose lines, so the user's text is not visible in live preview unless the cursor enters the block. Parsing does not change bytes, but visible prose can be hidden behind a formula widget.
findings.evidence:
Ran the parser's blockMathParser (copied verbatim, style props dropped) through @lezer/markdown 1.8.1 in memory. Closed '$$
x^2
$$

# Heading

- item' parses fine (BlockMath, ATXHeading1, BulletList). The unclosed and stray cases are shown above. The baseline without MathExtension parses the unclosed input with Paragraph, ATXHeading1 and BulletList nodes. Existing tests (parsers/math.test.ts, combined-block-structures.test.ts, block-math-field.test.ts) cover only closed blocks and the regex-based findAllBlockMath, which returns empty for no closing $$ (math.test.ts:28-32); no test pins the lezer tree after an unclosed opener.

verification.reasoning:
blockMathParser (math-extension.ts:76-91) walks the shared context forward with cx.nextLine(). When it finds no closing $$, it returns false after consuming every remaining line. In @lezer/markdown 1.8.1, BlockContext.advance (dist index.js:778-790) then tries the other block parsers on the line, which is now at the end of the input, so nothing after the opener gets a node. I ran the verbatim parser through node in memory. 'Intro

$$

findings.title: Composition freeze keeps bracket decorations at pre-edit offsets because the stored set is never mapped
locations: src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/composition-aware-bracket-matching.ts:150-158 (update() returns early during composition and does not map this.decorations)
node_modules/@codemirror/view/dist/index.js:1472-1476 (ViewPlugin decorations facet returns the plugin's stored set as-is)
node_modules/@codemirror/view/dist/index.js:3455-3462 (DocView.updateDeco takes facet values without changes mapping)

The commit transaction (composing already -1) rebuilds the set, so the mismatch is transient. Stored decorations are not mapped, so a composition that deletes text before a stored position could leave a mark past the end of the document. I did not confirm that case; it would need a deletion during composition.
findings.evidence: ViewPlugin.define wraps the spec's decorations as decorations.of(view => deco(view.plugin(plugin))) (view dist 1472-1476), and DocView.updateDeco uses those values directly (3455-3462), so no mapping happens between the stored set and rendering. compositionend sets composing to -1 before the commit (view dist ~5327-5331), so the commit is not frozen. Not reproduced in WebKit.

The ViewPlugin decorations facet is read as-is (view dist 1472-1476). After a composition insert before a highlighted bracket, the mark covers the wrong character. One example: typing '(' with closeBrackets, which gives '()' with the cursor between, then a dead key. The stale ')' mark at [1,2] then covers the composing character. That is the DOM restructuring around the composing node that this file was written to avoid (header 26-43), so it may cause the WebKit glitch the file was built to prevent. I did not verify in WKWebView. The mark goes away on the commit transaction. I did not settle the claim about marks past the end of the doc, but RangeSet.spans and compare iterate only inside the document range, so a crash looks unlikely. Display only. The header comment says text is not lost.
verification.repro: jsdom test: plugin plus a doc '()' with the cursor at 1. Stub view.composing to true, then dispatch an insert 'x' at 1. Assert that the decoration ranges map to ')' at [2,3]. Today they stay at [1,2].

findings.title: Mousedown sets the drag flag for any button, so a missed mouseup leaves reveal and selection updates frozen
findings.scenario: The mousedown handler dispatches setMouseSelecting(true) without checking e.button. The flag clears only on the next document-level mouseup (or a content mouseup or dragstart). If a platform never delivers mouseup after a right-button press (for example, a native context menu swallows it), the flag stays true. Then revealPredicate returns () => false, so every document edit rebuilds with all syntax and all block-hidden lines collapsed, and selection-only updates return 'skip' and do not rebuild. A user who types into a fenced code block or table after that right-click sees the cursor line hidden while the typing lands in it. No bytes are lost or changed by the flag itself. The stuck state ends at the next mouseup in the document.
findings.evidence: mouse-selecting.ts:41-45 has no button check and arms a once-listener on ownerDocument. The sibling handlers do check it: wikilink-click-target.ts:54 (e.button !== 0) and click-handler.ts:17. reveal.ts:67 returns () => false while the flag is set. check-update-action.ts:29 returns 'skip' while dragging, and block-decorator.ts:82 rebuilds only on 'rebuild' or a forced effect. Not verified: whether WKWebView in Tauri delivers mouseup after a native context menu. I could not check this offline.

verification.reasoning: It is true that mousedown (mouse-selecting.ts:41-45) sets the flag for any button, but the trigger the reporter gives cannot happen. The editor container sits inside a bits-ui ContextMenu.Trigger (MarkdownEditor.svelte:408-414), whose oncontextmenu calls e.preventDefault() (bits-ui menu.svelte.js:1544-1549). The menu is HTML, not a native macOS menu, so no native tracking loop eats the mouseup. The mouseup then reaches the once-listener on ownerDocument (43-45). Even if a mouseup were lost, the next primary click sets and clears the flag again. A residual window, mouseup suppressed some other way, stays theoretical.
verification.repro: None reachable from the described UI. A direct test would need a mouseup that is dispatched to no node of the document.
verification.fix_hint: Optional hardening: return early when e.button !== 0, to match wikilink-click-target.ts:54.

findings.title: Decorations built before the background parse finishes are not rebuilt when it finishes, so notes over about 3000 chars can keep raw syntax
findings.scenario: The editor is built with EditorState.create (MarkdownEditor.svelte:107) and no ensureSyntaxTree call. LanguageState.init parses only the first min(3000, doc.length) characters (@codemirror/language index.js:543-545). The inline plugin builds in its constructor from that truncated tree. The background ParseWorker then dispatches Language.setState (index.js:624). That transaction has no doc change, no selection change and no effect, so checkUpdateAction returns 'none' (check-update-action.ts:19-42). The remaining rebuild triggers are the 150 ms scroll debounce, an edit, or a cursor move that changes the touched-line set. If the background parse finishes after the debounce rebuild, which can happen on a loaded machine because requestIdle waits at least 100 ms, then headings, emphasis, links and checkboxes below about 3000 chars stay as raw markdown until the user scrolls or moves the cursor onto another line. The same gating applies to the block plugins. The team documents this hazard in the test helper (test-helpers.ts:83-91 and pipeline-dom.test.ts:24-40), but the production mount path does not use that workaround.
findings.evidence: index.js:543 `let vpTo = Math.min(3000, state.doc.length)` and index.js:545 `parseState.work(20, vpTo)` in LanguageState.init. index.js:624 `this.view.dispatch({ effects: Language.setState.of(...) })` in ParseWorker.work. checkUpdateAction returns 'none' when there is no docChanged, reconfigure, drag, forceDecorationRebuild or selectionSet. Not reproduced; timing depends on the machine.

verification.reasoning: The path exists. LanguageState.init parses only min(3000, len) (@codemirror/language 6.13.1 dist 543-546). ParseWorker later dispatches only Language.setState (dist 624). checkUpdateAction returns 'none' for that transaction (check-update-action.ts:19-42), and the repo's own test helpers document this (test-helpers.ts:83-91, pipeline-dom.test.ts:32-38). The mount path (MarkdownEditor.svelte:107-133) dispatches no forceDecorationRebuild. The tab-switch path is mostly safe: LanguageState.apply parses to the viewport, and the double rAF forces a rebuild (258-268). Two things decide whether it shows on mount: whether a viewportChanged happens so the 150 ms debounce fires (scroll-debounce-plugin.ts:32-40), and whether the background parse lands before or after it. requestIdle waits at least 100 ms, or 500 ms without requestIdleCallback (dist 561-571). I could not check offline whether WKWebView provides requestIdleCallback. Only visible content past about 3000 chars on first mount is affected, and HighlightStyle marks still update from the new tree. Display only.
verification.repro: Mount MarkdownEditor with a 10k-char note that has '# H' at offset 6000 and a tall container. Wait for fake timers to pass 600 ms without scrolling. Assert that the H line has cm-lp-h1.
verification.fix_hint: Treat a change in the syntax tree as a rebuild in checkUpdateAction (syntaxTree(update.startState) !== syntaxTree(update.state)), or call ensureSyntaxTree on the viewport before new EditorView on mount.

findings.scenario: A note has frontmatter `title: Trip`, then `dates:` with a nested `start: 2026-01-01`, then `favorite: false`, then `# keep this`. Its body contains `INPUT[toggle():favorite]`. The only lossy check is detectLossyFrontmatter, called from frontmatter-write.service.ts:121, auto-move and event-calendar, never from widgets.ts or properties.service.ts (grep). findings.title: A typed but uncommitted meta-bind number or date value is discarded when a click reveals its line
findings.scenario: The user clicks an `INPUT[number():count]` field (mousedown is stopped, so the cursor stays put) and types 42. The commit happens only on blur or Enter (widgets.ts:942-944). Without leaving the field, the user clicks other text on the same line. CodeMirror's mousedown moves the selection, the touched-line set changes (check-update-action.ts:34-35), revealPredicate reveals the line (meta-bind-input-plugin.ts:74), and the decoration is removed, which removes the focused input. MetaBindTextInputWidget has no destroy() hook, so nothing commits. If the engine fires blur during removal instead, commit runs inside CodeMirror's update, and dispatchMetaBindUpdate calls view.dispatch, which throws 'Calls to EditorView.update are not allowed while an update is in progress' (index.js:8017-8018). The value is still not written. Either way the typed value is gone and the note keeps its old value.

MetaBindTextInputWidget has no destroy hook (widgets.ts has a destroy only on WikilinkNoteEmbedWidget, line 647). meta-bind-input-plugin.ts:74 uses revealPredicate, and check-update-action.ts:34-35 rebuilds on a selection change. Browser blur-on-removal behaviour is NOT verified here: WebKit and Chromium differ, and I could not check either engine's source.

verification.reasoning: The stated path (click other text on the same line) commits the value before the line is revealed. While the input is focused, view.hasFocus is false, because it requires activeElement == contentDOM (@codemirror/view index.js:8690-8697). So handlers.mousedown sets mustFocus and calls focusPreventScroll(view.contentDOM) and then active.blur() (index.js:5033-5041). Both run synchronously, before mouseSel.start(event) applies the selection (index.js:5042-5045 and 4810-4814). The synchronous blur runs commit() (widgets.ts:931-944), and its view.dispatch runs outside any view.update, so it neither throws nor loses the value. Then the selection moves and the line is revealed. A residual case I could not settle: a keyboard shortcut that switches tabs while the input has focus removes the widget during a doc replace. Whether WebKit fires blur on removal there is unverified.
verification.repro: vitest + jsdom: render INPUT[number():count], focus the input, set its value to '42', then dispatch a mousedown on another position in the same line through CM's handlers. The doc now contains 'count: ' with 42.
verification.fix_hint: None needed for the stated path. Optionally add a destroy() to MetaBindTextInputWidget that ignores late blurs once the view's doc has changed tabs.

tweet_id: 1234567890123456789

'; dispatchMetaBindUpdate(view,'fav','true'); expect(doc).toContain('1234567890123456789') // fails

findings.title: Meta-bind button actions after a navigation or create write into whichever note the shared editor shows
findings.scenario: A button configured with `actions: [{type: open, link: [[Other]]}, {type: updateMetadata, bindTarget: status, value: done}]` (or createNote followed by updateMetadata) runs its actions in sequence (widget loop, lines 33-36). The open or create action awaits host.openLink or host.createNote, which switch the active tab through openFileInEditor or openOrCreateNote. The editor is one EditorView reused across tabs (MarkdownEditor.svelte:131), and its tab-switch effect swaps the doc. dispatchMetaBindUpdate then reads view.state.doc at call time (widgets.ts:754-767), so `status: done` is written into the newly opened note's frontmatter, not the note that holds the button.
findings.evidence: Sequence: meta-bind-button-widget.ts:33-36 (for/await), then :95 openLink or :110 createNote, then app/editor-host.ts:76-79, then openFileInEditor (editor.service.ts:98+, setActiveIndex). The write target is view.state at widgets.ts:754-767. Not verified: whether Svelte flushes the tab-swap effect before the await continuation runs, and the intended target for this config. The owner should confirm what the config is meant to update.

verification.reasoning: The button click loop awaits each action with the `view` it captured (meta-bind-button-widget.ts:30-36). `open` awaits host.openLink -> openFileInEditor, which calls setActiveIndex or addTab before its promise resolves (editor.service.ts:116-140). Svelte 5.57.2 queues the batch flush as a microtask when the state is written (batch.js:915-925), so the tab-swap $effect (MarkdownEditor.svelte:170-230) replaces the shared view's document before the loop resumes. updateMetadata also adds `await import('../widgets')`. dispatchMetaBindUpdate then reads view.state.doc, which is now B (widgets.ts:755-767), so B's frontmatter is rewritten and gets the property. If B is a markdown note, the same MarkdownEditor instance persists (EditorView.svelte:85). No path check exists anywhere in the chain. A's body is not lost. B's frontmatter goes through the same lossy rebuild (F97).
verification.repro: Integration test with the real editor host and a mounted MarkdownEditor: note A holds a meta-bind-button with actions [open [[B]], updateMetadata status=done]. Click it, flush, and assert that B's tab content does not contain 'status: done' and A's does. The first assertion fails.
verification.fix_hint: Capture the button's note path at click time, and have updateMetadata target that path through updateNoteFrontmatter. Or abort the remaining actions once the active tab path differs from the captured one.

findings.title: ImageWidget throws URIError from decodeURIComponent on a raw % in a file:// URL, with no guard in toDOM
findings.scenario: A note contains `![shot](file:///Users/me/100%.png)`, a hand-typed file URL or one copied from a tool that did not encode `%`. The image plugin passes the raw URL text into ImageWidget (image-plugin.ts:131-141). In toDOM, applyFileSrc calls fileUrlToFsPath. That calls `new URL(...)`, which keeps `%.p`, and then decodeURIComponent on the pathname, which throws URIError. toDOM has no try/catch, so the exception escapes the CodeMirror DOM update that builds the widget. The editor cannot render that image line. What happens to the rest of the view after the throw was not verified.

The URIError on a lone '%' is standard JS behaviour. CodeMirror's update has try/finally only for updateState (node_modules/@codemirror/view/dist/index.js:8040-8095), so the partial DOM state after a widget throw was not checked.

verification.reasoning: In node, new URL('file:///Users/me/100%.png').pathname gives '/Users/me/100%.png', and decodeURIComponent throws URIError. fileUrlToFsPath has no try around decodeURIComponent (widgets.ts:113), and toDOM -> applyFileSrc (widgets.ts:143-161) does not catch. image-plugin.ts:131-141 passes the raw URL. In @codemirror/view 6.43.15, WidgetTile.of calls widget.toDOM with no catch (index.js:2206). EditorView.update wraps docView.update in try/finally only (index.js:8063-8096), so the throw escapes dispatch. The state has already advanced (viewState.update sets state, index.js:6343), but the update-listener loop (index.js:8100-8108), which includes the autosave onDocChanged listener, is skipped for that update. At mount, the EditorView constructor builds new DocView after the plugins (index.js:7986-7991), so a note opening with that image in view would throw from the constructor and fail to open. Disk bytes are not touched directly. Whether repeated throws starve autosave for later edits depends on the docView's state after the throw, which I could not settle by reading.
verification.repro: vitest jsdom: new EditorView with doc 'x\n![a](file:///tmp/100%.png)', the cursor on line 1, and the live-preview image plugin plus editorHost. Expect the construction not to throw and the image line to render, with a missing-image class. Also unit-test that fileUrlToFsPath('file:///a/100%.png') does not throw.
verification.fix_hint: Wrap decodeURIComponent in try/catch and fall back to the raw pathname or return null. Widget toDOM paths should never throw.

Fixing the lossy rewrite in F98 (keep raw cells, or do not re-serialise) also fixes this.

findings.title: TableWidget.eq ignores alignments, so a rendered table can keep stale alignments and +row/+col writes them back
findings.scenario: The delimiter row changes alignment (for example ':---' becomes '---:') while the table stays rendered with the cursor outside (an external reload or undo that does not reveal the table). table-field recomputes, and the new TableWidget compares equal because eq() checks headers, rows, properties and sourceRange but not alignments. CodeMirror keeps the old DOM and the old instance's click handlers (toDOM binds this to the old instance). The table keeps showing the old alignment, and the next + click rebuilds the table with the old alignments, reverting the user's change in the bytes.
findings.evidence: widgets.ts:374-392 has no alignments comparison. CodeMirror WidgetTile reuse calls tile.widget.compare(widget) and reuses tile.dom when it returns true (index.js:2617-2619). Click handlers are created in toDOM via arrow functions over this (widgets.ts:420-443, 468-482). Narrow trigger, not run in the editor.

verification.reasoning: TableWidget.eq does compare alignments: widgets.ts:378 has `if (!this.alignments.every((a, i) => a === other.alignments[i])) return false;`. Header count equality is checked first (widgets.ts:375), and table.ts:149-150 pins alignments to the header count, so the lengths match. A changed delimiter alignment yields a non-equal widget and CM rebuilds the DOM and handlers.
verification.repro: new TableWidget(['h'],['left'],[],[],r).eq(new TableWidget(['h'],['right'],[],[],r)) returns false.
verification.fix_hint: None needed.

findings.title: Media finder hides everything up to the next closing tag, including inside fenced code, with no bound
findings.scenario: (a) A ```html fenced block shows <video src="demo.mp4" controls></video>. With the cursor outside, findMediaBlock matches the single line, computeVideoBlocks replaces that code line with a MediaWidget and hides the following lines. The code sample is shown as a player instead of source. (b) A note has <video src="a.mp4"> on line 5 with no closing tag, and a later </video> on line 40. The multi-line scan (media.ts:67-88) returns that span, so lines 6-40 are hidden with the cursor outside and idx skips past them (video-plugin.ts:38). Nothing is written, so no bytes are lost, but the visible text is hidden.
findings.evidence: media.ts:67-88 scans forward for close.test() with no fence check and no limit. video-plugin.ts:12-45 and audio-plugin.ts:12-40 iterate every line with getAllLines and never consult FencedCode nodes. Contrast block-comment-field.ts:17-25, which builds codeLineStarts to exclude code. CodeMirror rendering with the code-block hideLines overlap was not run, so the exact visual outcome in (a) is unverified.

verification.reasoning: findMediaBlock scans forward to the first closing tag with no bound and no fence check (media.ts:67-88). computeVideoBlocks iterates all lines without consulting FencedCode (video-plugin.ts:12-45), so an unclosed <video src> hides every line up to a later </video> while the cursor is outside. A <video> line inside an ```html fence is turned into a player. This is display only: nothing is dispatched and no bytes change.
verification.repro:
vitest: doc '<video src="a.mp4">
line A
line B
</video>' plus a variant inside ```html. Run computeVideoBlocks with the cursor elsewhere and observe the replace or hide decorations over the code or the intermediate lines.
verification.fix_hint: Skip lines inside FencedCode/CodeBlock nodes (as block-comment-field does), and cap the multi-line scan or stop at a blank line.

findings.title: Frontmatter fence rule diverges: properties see a closing ----, but the hider needs an exact ---
findings.scenario: A note starts with ---, has YAML, and closes with ---- (four dashes), or with '--- ' plus text. frontmatterSlice returns the properties up to the ---- line (startsWith('---')), so the sidebar shows the properties. findFrontmatterBlock needs /^---\s*$/ and does not match ----, so it finds no closing line, or finds a later exact --- (for example an HR in the body). In the second case computeFrontmatter hides every line from line 1 to that HR, with no reveal check (frontmatter-field.ts:12-25), so body text is invisible in live preview. If there is no later ---, the raw YAML is shown instead.
findings.evidence: frontmatter.ts:10 uses /^---\s*$/ for the closing line. frontmatter-slice.ts:7-10 claims parity with a regex that accepts a newline followed by --- as the close, and line 16 uses startsWith('---'). frontmatter-field.ts:22 hides lines with no reveal predicate. Trace only; not run.

verification.reasoning: FRONTMATTER_FENCE_RE /^---\s*$/ (frontmatter.ts:10) does not match '----', but frontmatterSlice accepts any line that startsWith('---') (frontmatter-slice.ts:16). findFrontmatterBlock then picks the next exact '---' anywhere in the body, and computeFrontmatter hides lines 1..that index with no reveal predicate (frontmatter-field.ts:12-25). Body text becomes invisible in live preview. This is display only, with no write path in these files.
verification.repro:
vitest: doc '---
a: 1
----
body text
---
more'. computeFrontmatter hides lines 1-5, including 'body text'.
verification.fix_hint: Use one fence rule for both (the parser's FRONTMATTER_REGEX semantics), or require the close fence to match the same rule frontmatterSlice uses.

findings.title: Embed block-id lookup matches by substring, so ^abc returns the line that has ^abcdef
findings.scenario: A target note has the line 'first point ^abcdef' before 'second point ^abc'. The widget for ![[note#^abc]] calls extractBlockContent, which tests line.includes('^abc') in file order. The first line matches, so the embed shows 'first point' instead of 'second point'. The same happens if an earlier line has ^abc-x or any text containing ^abc.
findings.evidence: embed-resolver.logic.ts:45 is `if (line.includes(marker))` with marker `^${blockId}` (line 41). No word-boundary check. Node check: the first line containing '^abc' in 'first ^abcdef\nsecond ^abc' is 'first ^abcdef'. Read-only embed; nothing is written.

verification.reasoning: extractBlockContent uses line.includes('^' + blockId) (embed-resolver.logic.ts:41-45) with no boundary check, so '^abc' matches the earlier line ending '^abcdef'. The embed is read only and nothing is written.
verification.repro: extractBlockContent('first ^abcdef\nsecond ^abc', 'abc') returns 'first' instead of 'second'.
verification.fix_hint: Match with new RegExp(`\\s\\^${escape(blockId)}\\s*$`) or a check that the next character is not a word char.

findings.title: Embed heading and frontmatter extraction fail on CRLF notes and inside fenced code
findings.scenario: (a) The target file uses CRLF line endings (content is read raw from disk by host.readNote, widgets.ts:570). Each heading line ends in a carriage return. HEADING_RE /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/ cannot match because '.' excludes carriage return and '$' needs end of string, so extractHeadingSection returns null for every heading embed. (b) stripFrontmatter checks content[endIdx+4] === '\n' (line 60), which fails for a carriage return, so YAML shows in note previews. (c) A heading-like comment inside a ```bash block ('# install deps') at level 1 ends a '## Install' embed early.
findings.evidence: Node check: /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/ applied to a heading line with a trailing carriage return returns null; without it the same regex matches. Lines 14 and 26 apply HEADING_RE to raw split('\n') lines. Display-only; how common CRLF notes are is unknown.

verification.reasoning: host.readNote is readTextFile with no normalisation (app/editor-host.ts:68-70). The content is split on '\n' (embed-resolver.logic.ts:9, 43), so lines keep a trailing '\r'. HEADING_RE /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/ (line 2) has no m flag, '.' excludes '\r' and '$' needs end of string, so CRLF headings never match. stripFrontmatter checks content[endIdx+4] !== '\n' (line 60), which fails on '\r'. Heading lines inside code fences are treated as headings. Display only.
verification.repro:
extractHeadingSection('## A
text
', 'A') returns null. stripFrontmatter('---
a: 1
---
body') returns the input unchanged.
verification.fix_hint: Normalise content.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n') in loadEmbedContent before extracting.

findings.title: Indented or blockquoted mermaid/queryjs/collection/meta-bind-button fences get no renderer
findings.scenario: A list item contains an indented fence ('  ```mermaid') or a fence in a blockquote ('> ```queryjs'). Lezer gives FencedCode with language 'mermaid' or 'queryjs'. code-block-field.ts:27 skips SPECIAL_LANGUAGES, so the generic code widget does not draw it. The specialized finder regex is anchored at column 0, so it finds nothing. The user sees raw fence text with no diagram or query result, and nothing is written.
findings.evidence: mermaid.ts:19 and queryjs-block.ts:19 anchor ^ on the full opening line text (findSpecialFenceBlocks tests openLine.text, fenced-code-block.ts:131-132). code-block-field.ts:27 returns before any other handling.

verification.reasoning: MERMAID_OPEN_RE and QUERYJS_OPEN_RE are anchored at column 0 (mermaid.ts:19, queryjs-block.ts:19), and the anchoring is documented as intended. findSpecialFenceBlocks tests the whole opening line (fenced-code-block.ts:131-132). code-block-field.ts:27 skips SPECIAL_LANGUAGES by the Lezer language, so an indented or quoted special fence gets neither renderer and shows as raw text. The column-0 rule is a deliberate design choice, but the gap where neither renderer runs is real. Nothing is written.
verification.repro:
vitest: doc '- item

  ```mermaid
  graph TD
  ```'. Neither computeCodeBlocks nor the mermaid field produce a decoration.
verification.fix_hint: Have code-block-field skip SPECIAL_LANGUAGES only when the special finder will actually claim the block (or fall back to the generic code widget).

findings.title: Meta-bind writers silently drop nested mappings, comments, anchors and duplicate or colliding keys from the frontmatter they rewrite
findings.scenario: A note has `author:` with a nested `name: Ana` under it, a `# keep` comment, and `status: draft` in its frontmatter. Its body contains INPUT[inlineSelect(option(draft, Draft), option(done, Done)):status]. The user selects Done in the widget. dispatchMetaBindUpdate runs isFrontmatterUnparseable (false, the YAML parses cleanly), then parseFrontmatterProperties (drops `author` at properties.logic.ts:292-300), then rebuildContent, which emits only title and status. The comment is gone too. The frontmatter timer saves the note to disk about 500 ms later (editor-extensions.ts:184-190, editor.service.ts:200). The Properties panel on the same note refuses the write with the 'nested values' toast (frontmatter-write.service.ts:121-122, WRITE_ERROR_MESSAGES). Meta-bind toggle, number/date and button updateMetadata writes behave the same way.
findings.evidence:
widgets.ts:756 guards only isFrontmatterUnparseable. widgets.ts:761 parses with parseFrontmatterProperties, which yields no `author` property. widgets.ts:767 dispatches the whole frontmatter range. I replayed the parse with the yaml package: parseDocument on `title: Plan
author:
  name: Ana
# keep this
status: draft` gives 0 errors, 0 warnings, and toJS includes author, so the unparseable guard does not fire. detectLossyFrontmatter (properties.logic.ts:412) returns 'nested' and 'comments' for the same block, and only the panel path calls it. The ADR-0029 amendments state that meta-bind keeps the drop behaviour, so this is a documented decision that conflicts with the owner's data-loss priority. It is not a regression, and .scratch/file-io-audit/raw/scout-frontmatter-writers.md (L3) already flags it.
findings.source: map:doc-mutating-handlers (live-preview paste handlers, click/wikilink navigation, meta-bind input/button writers)

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F97: dispatchMetaBindUpdate guards only isFrontmatterUnparseable (widgets.ts:756), and parseFrontmatterProperties drops nested maps (properties.logic.ts:292-300). The 500 ms frontmatter autosave persists the result. ADR-0029:103-107 documents the drop.
verification.repro: See F97.
verification.fix_hint: See F97.

findings.title: A button action after open or createNote writes its property into the newly opened note, not the note with the button
findings.scenario: Note A has a ```meta-bind-button with actions [ {type: open, link: '[[B]]'}, {type: updateMetadata, bindTarget: status, value: done} ]. The user clicks it. The open action makes B the active tab. The MarkdownEditor $effect replaces the single shared view's document with B's content. The updateMetadata action then runs dispatchMetaBindUpdate(view, ...), which reads view.state.doc, now B's. `status: done` is written into B.md, and A.md is not changed. The change is silent, has no toast, and autosaves for B. The same happens for [createNote, updateMetadata]. Ordering: addTab runs inside openFileInEditor before its promise resolves. Svelte 5 flushes effects in a queued microtask (batch.js:915-925), which runs before the awaiting button loop resumes, so the swap has completed by the next action. I did not run this in the app.
findings.evidence: meta-bind-button-widget.ts:33-35 runs the actions in order with the same `view` for each. :90-103 open calls host.openLink and then falls through to the next action. app/editor-host.ts:76-79 awaits openFileInEditor. editor.service.ts:116 (setActiveIndex) and :140 (addTab) switch the active tab. editor.store.svelte.ts:56/59 set activeIndex. MarkdownEditor.svelte:131 creates the only EditorView, and the $effect at :170-230 replaces its document via view.dispatch when activeTabPath changes. widgets.ts:761-767 reads view.state.doc and dispatches to it. editor-host.test.ts:186-260 mocks the host (openLink is a vi.fn that never switches the view), and the createNote test asserts only the openLink call. No test covers the real view swap.
findings.source: map:doc-mutating-handlers (live-preview paste handlers, click/wikilink navigation, meta-bind input/button writers)

verification.reasoning: Same chain as F104. I verified the Svelte microtask ordering (batch.js:915-925) and the single reused view (MarkdownEditor.svelte:131).
verification.repro: See F104.
verification.fix_hint: See F104.

findings.title: Pasting a table whose clipboard HTML contains a link merges every cell in the row into one run of text
findings.scenario: The user copies a table row from a web page or spreadsheet. One cell holds a link, and the text/plain flavour is tab-separated (`Alice\t2026-01-01\tDoc`). pasteHtmlLinkHandler runs first, sees an anchor whose URL is absent from the plain text, and returns the converted text. The TSV handler never runs, so the cell boundaries disappear. The paste inserts `Alice2026-01-01[Doc](https://ex.com/a)`. Cmd+Z is the only way back.
findings.evidence: BLOCK_TAGS (paste-html-link.logic.ts:21-26) lists TABLE, TR and LI but not TD or TH, so cells are concatenated with no separator. I replayed htmlLinksToMarkdown with jsdom on a table row containing a linked cell and got `Alice2026-01-01[Doc](https://ex.com/a)` followed by the next row's text with no separator. paste-html-link-handler.ts:27-28 returns the converted string whenever it is not null. No test in paste-html-link.logic.test.ts covers table cells.
findings.source: map:doc-mutating-handlers (live-preview paste handlers, click/wikilink navigation, meta-bind input/button writers)

verification.reasoning: BLOCK_TAGS (paste-html-link.logic.ts:21-26) has TABLE and TR but not TD or TH, so blockAwareText concatenates the cells of a row with no separator. htmlLinksToMarkdown fires whenever any href is missing from text/plain (lines 72-76). The handler is registered before pasteTsvHandler (live-preview.ts:101), so the TSV conversion never runs. The pasted content is mangled, but existing note text is not touched and the paste is a single undoable transaction.
verification.repro:
vitest jsdom: htmlLinksToMarkdown('
AliceDoc
', 'Alice\tDoc') returns 'Alice[Doc](https://ex.com/a)'. Expect a separator.
verification.fix_hint: Return null (fall through) when the HTML contains <table>, or emit '\t' between TD/TH and let the TSV path handle it.

findings.title: TSV paste turns tab-indented code and any first line with a tab into a markdown table, doubling backslashes and not checking for code fences
findings.evidence:
I ran the pure functions with node (type stripping, no file writes). Input `	if err != nil {
		return err
	}` gives `|  | if err != nil { |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | return err |
|  | } |  |`. looksLikeTSV (paste-tsv.logic.ts:19-26) only needs a tab and at least 2 cells in the first row. A leading tab gives an empty first cell, so it passes. Input `C:
ew\path	b` gives `| C:\new\path | b |`, because escape (paste-tsv.logic.ts:129-130) doubles backslashes. paste-tsv-handler.ts has no context check. paste-tsv.logic.test.ts does not cover backslashes or leading tabs.
findings.source: map:doc-mutating-handlers (live-preview paste handlers, click/wikilink navigation, meta-bind input/button writers)

verification.reasoning: looksLikeTSV needs only one tab and at least 2 cells in the first parsed row (paste-tsv.logic.ts:19-26). A leading tab produces ['', rest], so tab-indented code or this app's own tab-indented nested list items qualify. paste-tsv-handler.ts:18-40 has no syntax-context check (fence or frontmatter) before preventDefault and replacing selection.main. Pasting Go or Makefile code, even into a ``` fence, becomes a pipe table. A leading '"' turns on quote mode (lines 69-73) and can merge lines. The backslash doubling (line 129-130) is valid markdown escaping for literal TSV text, not a bug by itself. The paste is mangled but undoable, and the clipboard still holds the original.
verification.repro: vitest: clipboardToMarkdownTable('\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}') returns a table and should return null. In jsdom, paste into a view whose cursor is inside a ```go fence and expect the text inserted verbatim.
verification.fix_hint: Skip when the cursor is inside FencedCode/CodeBlock/frontmatter. Require the same column count of at least 2 on at least 2 rows, and reject input whose rows all start with a tab.

findings.title: A button whose actions list is malformed next to a valid action writes null into the bound property
findings.scenario: A config has a valid `action: {type: updateMetadata, bindTarget: status, value: done}` and also `actions: [{type: updateMetadata, bindTarget: status}]` (the value is missing). validateButtonConfig accepts it because the single action is valid. getButtonActions then returns the invalid `actions` array, which takes precedence. normalizeAction gives value undefined. dispatchMetaBindUpdate sets status to undefined, and the serializer writes `status: null`, so the note's status is erased. A variant with `actions: []` plus a valid `action` makes the button do nothing. A variant with `actions: [{type: open}]` throws a TypeError at `link.startsWith` (widget line 92) inside the async click handler.
findings.evidence: meta-bind-button.logic.ts:94-98 accepts the config when hasAction is true, whatever hasActions says. getButtonActions (:141-145) returns `config.actions` whenever it is an array. normalizeAction (:121-127) keeps value as undefined. I checked the serializer with the yaml package: Document.set('title','Plan') then set('status', undefined) prints `status: null`. The chain needs an unusual mixed config, so the impact is low.
findings.source: map:doc-mutating-handlers (live-preview paste handlers, click/wikilink navigation, meta-bind input/button writers)

verification.reasoning: validateButtonConfig accepts a config when the single `action` is valid, whatever `actions` contains (meta-bind-button.logic.ts:94-98). getButtonActions prefers `config.actions` whenever it is an array (:141-145). normalizeAction keeps value undefined (:121-127). setPropertyByBindTarget sets it, and a node check confirmed that Document.set('status', undefined) prints `status: null`, so the user's value is erased. A config of `[{type:open}]` would throw at link.startsWith (widget :91). This needs a malformed mixed config.
verification.repro: vitest: parseButtonConfig('label: x\naction: {type: updateMetadata, bindTarget: s, value: d}\nactions: [{type: updateMetadata, bindTarget: s}]') is not null, and getButtonActions(cfg)[0].value is undefined.
verification.fix_hint: In getButtonActions, use `actions` only when every item validates, or reject the config when `actions` is present but invalid.

findings.title: Clicking the second of two adjacent wikilinks can open the first one
findings.scenario: The note contains `[[A]][[B]]` with no space. The user clicks B. posAtDOM returns the offset where B starts, which equals A's end. findWikilinkInfoAtPosition uses an inclusive end (`docPos <= end`), so it returns A first, and A is opened or created.
findings.evidence: decoration.logic.ts:109 uses `docPos >= start && docPos <= end`, and returns the first match. wikilink-navigation.ts:32 takes that first match. I did not check how CodeMirror's posAtDOM maps the boundary offset, so confidence is low.
findings.source: map:doc-mutating-handlers (live-preview paste handlers, click/wikilink navigation, meta-bind input/button writers)

verification.reasoning: For a live-preview plain click on B's text, this does not hold. .cm-lp-wikilink covers targetFrom..contentEnd (wikilink-handler.ts:39), so posAtDOM returns B.start+2, which is greater than A's end. A does not match, and the click is correct. It does hold in source mode, where wikilinkDecoration is installed (editor-extensions.ts:96-103). There the '[[' of B is a .cm-wikilink-bracket mark that starts at B.start, which equals A's end (decoration.ts:25-26). posAtDOM gives the position at the start of the tile (view dist 8574-3214). findWikilinkInfoAtPosition uses an inclusive end (decoration.logic.ts:109) and returns the first match, so A opens or is created. If CodeMirror merges A's ']]' and B's '[[' into one span, the position falls inside A, with the same result. A Cmd-click at the exact boundary in revealed live preview is ambiguous the same way. Scope: source mode, click on B's opening brackets.
verification.repro: Unit test: findWikilinkInfoAtPosition('[[A]][[B]]', 0, 5) should return target 'B'. Today it returns 'A'.
verification.fix_hint: Use an exclusive end (docPos < end), or prefer a match whose start equals docPos.

findings.title: A path-qualified wikilink opens any note with the same basename instead of the named path
findings.scenario: The vault has Archive/Note.md but not Projects/Note.md. A link [[Projects/Note]] is clicked. resolveWikilink compares against the basename, so it returns Archive/Note.md, and the link opens the archived note. No file is created at Projects/Note.md. No data is lost, but the user lands on a different note than the one the link names.
findings.evidence: resolveWikilink (wikilink-resolution.logic.ts:23-31) falls back to getNoteName(target) when the full target matches no name, and returns the first path with that name. followWikilink only calls createNote when resolveLink returns null (wikilink-navigation.ts:19-21). Whether the basename fallback is intended is a design question; I did not find a doc that settles it.
findings.source: map:doc-mutating-handlers (live-preview paste handlers, click/wikilink navigation, meta-bind input/button writers)

verification.reasoning: The first loop of resolveWikilink (wikilink-resolution.logic.ts:16-21) compares the basename of each file with the whole target. A target with a slash ('projects/note') can therefore never match there. The fallback (23-31) returns the first path in the file tree with the same basename. The case is worse than reported: the path part is ignored even when Projects/Note.md exists. With Archive/Note.md and Projects/Note.md both present, [[Projects/Note]] opens whichever comes first in flattenFileTree, here Archive. resolveLink (editor-host.ts:59-61) and followWikilink (wikilink-navigation.ts:19-21) pass the result through unchanged. The docstring calls the basename fallback intended, and the tests (test.ts:56-62) use fixtures with only one note of that name, so the collision case has no test. The user can edit the wrong note, but no bytes are lost.
verification.repro: expect(resolveWikilink('Projects/Note', ['/vault/Archive/Note.md','/vault/Projects/Note.md'])).toBe('/vault/Projects/Note.md'). Today it returns the Archive path.
verification.fix_hint: When the target contains '/', first match paths that end with '/<target>.md' (case-insensitive), and only then fall back to the basename. Make resolveWikilinkCached match.

findings.title: deep-link new with silent=true overwrites an existing note
findings.scenario: A URL such as kokobrain://new?vault=V&name=Inbox&content=hi&silent=true (from a browser link, Shortcuts, or a script) is sent while Inbox.md already holds notes. executeNewAction (deep-link.service.ts:309-315) has no append, prepend or overwrite flag set, so it takes the silent create branch: mkdir plus writeTextFile(fullPath, content) with no exists check. Inbox.md is replaced by 'hi'. The same URL without silent goes to openOrCreateNote, which opens the existing file untouched. clipboard=true&silent=true with an empty clipboard writes an empty file over the note. Mitigation: file-history takes a snapshot on each save (file-history.service.ts:190-196), but the snapshot is taken after the overwrite, so only the last in-app-saved version is recoverable and unsaved edits are not.
findings.evidence: deep-link.service.ts:309-315 is the only branch that writes without checking existence. deep-link.types.ts:31-36 documents append/prepend as 'instead of overwriting' and overwrite as an explicit flag. The raw-write ratchet lists this site only as 'silent create; notifyAfterSave follows' (raw-write-ratchet.test.ts:36-37). The silent-create test (deep-link.service.test.ts:287-304) runs with exists() mocked to false (beforeEach at :111), so the existing-file case is untested.

findings.title: Pending deep-link action is a single slot and can be overwritten during vault init
findings.scenario: URL 1 targets vault B: pendingAction is set to action 1 and switchVault(B) runs. URL 2 targets vault C while B's initializeVault has not yet reached step 8 (the consumer that runs executePendingAction). URL 2 sets pendingAction to action 2, overwriting action 1, which never runs. If action 1 was an append of automation content, that content is never written.

This happens before step 8 executePendingAction (:503). So every cross-vault deep link sent while a vault is open loses its action, not only the second URL in a burst. That includes `new` with append, where the automation's content is never written. No test runs resolveAndDispatch through initializeVault and checks executePendingAction. The race-audit tests call executePendingAction directly, and switch-save.test.ts checks only the save. The URL-2 overwrite scenario also happens, but this broader loss covers it. Rated medium because the lost data is external automation content, not existing note bytes.

Then resolveAndDispatch({type:'new', vault:'B', name:'n.md', content:'x', append:true}), then await initializeVault(VAULT_B). Assert that writeTextFile was never called for B/n.md and that deepLinkStore.pendingAction is null.
verification.fix_hint: Do not clear the pending action in teardownVault, or capture it at the start of initializeVault, before teardown, and run it at step 8. Turn the slot into a queue, or reject a second cross-vault link while one is pending.

findings.title: Capture title/tags injection drops the whole template frontmatter when that YAML does not parse
findings.scenario: A capture template whose frontmatter has valid keys plus a broken line, for example 'created: <% created %>' and 'tags: [inbox' (unclosed flow sequence). A capture carrying a tags param (or kind=link with a title) takes the injection path. parseFrontmatterProperties returns [] for that block (computeAndCache catches the YAML error and returns []). extractBody still removes the whole block (FRONTMATTER_REGEX matches any ---...--- block), and rebuildContent writes only the injected key. The saved note's frontmatter becomes just the injected key, and 'created' is gone. Comment and nested-value loss on valid YAML is the drop that ADR-0029 (amendment 2026-10-28) accepts for deep-link writers. The unparseable case is a different and worse drop, and the ADR does not call it out. The one-on-one path (ensureFrontmatterLink) refuses lossy frontmatter instead (properties.logic.ts:535-536).
