findings.title: .view icon and query writers bypass the open tab, so a dirty tab can revert the change
findings.scenario: With a .view file open in a dirty tab (for example after editing its YAML in source mode), a TypeNoteList filter or sort change (updateViewQuery) or an icon change (updateViewIcon) reads the disk copy and writes the patched YAML, with no syncExternalContentToEditor and no dirty check. The tab's next 2 s autosave writes its stale content back, which reverts the change. The clean-tab case self-heals through the watcher. Not a .md note, so reported as low. I did not trace the UI call sites to confirm the tab is open in that flow.
findings.evidence: updateViewIcon (type-definitions.service.ts:284-291) and updateViewQuery (:305-310) call readTextFile and writeTextFile on the path directly. Contrast renameType (:200-220), which rewrites tab.content and calls sync, and the watcher reload that skips dirty tabs (editor.service.ts:380).
findings.source: map:other-writers-creators: note-creator, periodic-notes, quick-capture, kanban, one-on-one, plus the deep-link writers that dispatch into open tabs (app/deep-link-actions.ts, features/deep-link/deep-link.service.ts) and the tasks toggle that syncs into tabs

verification.reasoning: updateViewIcon and updateViewQuery read and write disk without touching the open tab (type-definitions.service.ts:284-291, 305-310). .view files open as 'collection' tabs (editor.service.ts:136), so a dirty .view tab's autosave could revert the change. Whether a .view tab can be dirty while the TypeNoteList toolbar is used was not traced. Not a .md note.

findings.title: Cmd+Q (menu Quit, Dock Quit, logout/shutdown) exits without saving dirty tabs: onCloseRequested never runs
findings.scenario: 1) Type a sentence in a note. 2) Press Cmd+Q less than 2 s after the last keystroke (500 ms for a frontmatter edit). The app quits right away and the sentence is gone from disk. The debounce is trailing-only with no maxWait (debounce.ts:9-17), so if you type without a 2 s pause, everything since the last pause is lost. A tab whose earlier save failed (dirty, on the 5 s retry) is also dropped with no 'Failed to save' prompt. Pending event-calendar writes and the 500 ms settings write are lost too. The Update panel's Restart button (relaunch(), UpdateSection.svelte:209) has the same effect.
findings.evidence: The app menu adds the predefined Quit item (lib.rs:195 `.quit()`). In muda 0.20.0 it carries the Cmd+Q accelerator (items/predefined.rs:669) and sends `terminate:` (platform_impl/macos/mod.rs:944). tao 0.37.2 registers only `applicationWillTerminate:` (app_delegate.rs:62), with no `applicationShouldTerminate:` (grep found none in tao, tauri-runtime-wry, tauri or muda). It calls AppState::exit() (app_delegate.rs:130-133), which fires Event::LoopDestroyed (app_state.rs:271-281). tauri-runtime-wry maps that to RunEvent::Exit (lib.rs:4131-4133), and tauri runs cleanup_before_exit (app.rs:1449-1455). No WindowEvent::CloseRequested is emitted, so the only save-on-exit path, `getCurrentWindow().onCloseRequested` (tauri-listeners.service.ts:53-55), never runs. The app calls `.run(tauri::generate_context!())` (lib.rs:353) with no RunEvent callback, so nothing intercepts ExitRequested/Exit either. Mitigation that exists: closing the window with the red button does go through onCloseRequested, which saves, prompts on failure, drains and flushes settings. I could not run the app; the conclusion comes from reading the framework source.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause and same framework chain as F189: the predefined Quit sends terminate:, tao implements only applicationWillTerminate, and no CloseRequested is emitted, so onCloseRequested at tauri-listeners.service.ts:53 never runs. I verified the same muda, tao and wry source lines.
verification.repro: See F189.
verification.fix_hint: See F189.

findings.title: Canvas onDestroy flush writes canvas JSON into whichever tab becomes active, then autosave overwrites that note on disk
findings.scenario: Have a .canvas tab C and a markdown note B open. 1) Switch to C (or open it), or click or select a node in C, or type in a text node. 2) Less than 300 ms later, move away so a markdown tab becomes active: Cmd+Shift+] or Cmd+Shift+[, a click on B's tab, opening a file from the tree or quick switcher, or Cmd+W on C when B is the neighbour. C's onDestroy sees pendingPersist=true and calls onContentChange(canvasJson). That writes to tabs[activeIndex], which is now B. B's content becomes the canvas JSON and the 2000 ms body timer is armed. Two seconds later saveDirtyTabs writes the JSON into B.md, and B then reads as clean. MarkdownEditor mounts after the destroy, so it probably shows the JSON (if it instead showed B's old text, the overwrite would be silent). Cycling quickly through tabs past a canvas is enough, because xyflow writes measured dimensions into the bound nodes about one frame after mount, which arms the 300 ms timer with no user edit. C's own last edit is also never applied to C.
findings.evidence: CanvasInner.svelte:211-226: every `nodes` change that is not a sync sets pendingPersist=true and starts a 300 ms timer. :230-234: onDestroy calls persistChanges(nodes, edges) when pendingPersist is set. :102-108: persistWithoutHistory calls onJsonChange(json). EditorView.svelte:81 binds onJsonChange to the global onContentChange, which calls editorStore.updateContent(content) (editor.service.ts:225). That writes `tabs[activeIndex].content` (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88) with no path or fileType check. setActiveIndex/removeTab/addTab are synchronous, so activeIndex already points at the new tab when Svelte's flush destroys the canvas branch. Svelte 5.57.2's BranchManager.#commit creates the new branch and then destroys the old onscreen branch synchronously in the same flush (branches.js:131-158 on_destroy -> destroy_effect). The no-user-action trigger: xyflow 1.7.0 updateNodeInternals assigns `store.nodes = store.nodes.map(...)` with `measured` dims (store/index.js:57-74), which flows back through `bind:nodes` (CanvasInner.svelte:580) after the `syncing` microtask reset (:95-96), so pendingPersist becomes true right after mount. No test covers the onDestroy flush (no match for pendingPersist/CanvasInner in src/tests). The flush came from c3ab02d4 'flush pending persist on component destroy'. Not reproduced in the app.

verification.reasoning: This has the same root cause as F5. Its no-user-action trigger, xyflow measurement after mount (NodeWrapper.svelte:134-148 rAF -> store/index.js:46 store.nodes reassign -> bind:nodes), is folded into F5. That trigger depends on timing, because it needs the measurement to produce a non-empty change set after the syncing microtask reset at CanvasInner.svelte:96.
verification.repro: See F5. Variant: open a canvas tab and press Cmd+Shift+] within ~300 ms of it rendering, with no edit.
verification.fix_hint: See F5.

findings.title: Vault switch silently discards dirty tabs whose save failed (resetEditor wipes them with no prompt)
findings.scenario: 1) Edit note N. 2) N's save fails: the file is read-only (EACCES), the disk is full, a cloud-sync provider holds a lock, or the scope is denied. You get one 'Failed to save file.' toast and the tab stays dirty. 3) Open another vault from the picker or the recent list. switchVault calls saveAllDirtyTabs, which fails again and returns [N]. The result is ignored and vaultStore.open runs. initializeVault tries once more (result ignored again), then teardownVault -> resetEditor sets tabs = []. The text typed in N now exists neither in memory nor on disk, and no dialog was shown. Window close (tauri-listeners.service.ts:56-62) and closeTab (editor.service.ts:271-277) both ask first in the same situation.
findings.evidence: vault.service.ts:19 `await saveAllDirtyTabs();` discards the returned failed paths, then :21 `vaultStore.open(path)`. app-lifecycle.service.ts:180 `await saveAllDirtyTabs();` also ignores the result, and the comment at :174-179 says the switch goes ahead after a failed save. :188 teardownVault() then calls resetEditor() at :622. resetEditor cancels the timers and calls editorStore.reset() (editor.service.ts:412-417), which sets `tabs = []` (editor.store.svelte.ts:166). The retry setTimeout from saveDirtyTabs (editor.service.ts:192) is not cancelled, but by then the tab is gone, so it has nothing to retry. The scout notes say issue 34 recorded the 'switch continues' decision but not the content wipe.

verification.reasoning: I looked for a guard and found none. vault.service.ts:19 `await saveAllDirtyTabs();` discards the failed-path array that editor.service.ts:234-247 returns, and :21 opens the new vault. On a write failure, saveFileByPath (editor.service.ts:161-178) only shows a toast and returns false, so the tab stays dirty. initializeVault takes the teardown branch because unsubscribeFileChange is set (app-lifecycle.service.ts:172). It retries once at :180 and ignores the result, then calls teardownVault() at :188, which calls resetEditor (:622). resetEditor (editor.service.ts:412-417) runs editorStore.reset(), which sets `tabs = []` (editor.store.svelte.ts:165-166). There is no tab or dirty-buffer persistence anywhere (grep for tab restore found nothing). The test 'switchVault still opens B when the save of a tab of A fails' (src/tests/lib/core/vault/vault.service.switch-save.test.ts) encodes the proceed behavior. It asserts the switch but not the wipe. The close handler prompts in the same situation (tauri-listeners.service.ts:55-62). Correction on reachability: the vault picker and recent list (+page.svelte) render only when `!vaultStore.isOpen` (AppShell.svelte:160-161), and vaultStore.close() has no caller. With a vault open, the only way to switch is a deep link (deep-link.service.ts:166), as F193 notes. Severity stays high: the loss is silent, but it needs a persistent write failure plus an external URL.
verification.repro: Vitest sketch: open vault A with a dirty tab (content 'edited', savedContent 'old'). Mock writeTextFile to reject every call. Run resolveAndDispatch({type:'open', vault:'B'}), then initializeVault(VAULT_B) with unsubscribeFileChange set (or a full initializeVault(A) first). Assert that editorStore.tabs no longer contains the tab and that no dialog `ask` was called. Both hold today.
verification.fix_hint: In switchVault, check the result of saveAllDirtyTabs(). If any save failed, call ask() as the close handler does and abort the switch on cancel (resolveAndDispatch then has to clear the pending action). Do the same for the initializeVault safety-net result, or let switchVault's decision cover it.

findings.title: Toggling a task in the Tasks view replaces the open note's unsaved edits with disk content
findings.scenario: 1) Type a paragraph in note N. 2) Less than 2 s later, or at any time while N's save is failing and retrying, open the Tasks tab and tick a checkbox belonging to N. Rust reads N from disk, toggles the line and writes it atomically. The TS side then sets both content and savedContent of N's tab to that disk-based text. The paragraph disappears from the tab, the tab reads clean, and no autosave restores it. The line number comes from the index of the disk version, so if the unsaved edits moved lines, the result still matches disk and every unsaved edit is lost.
findings.evidence: vault.rs:669 `std::fs::read_to_string(path)` uses disk bytes, not the editor buffer. :683 `vault_fs::write_atomic(path, &updated)`. tasks.service.ts:114 `syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, updatedContent, true, 'none')`. With markSaved=true it calls updateTabContentByPath (editor.service.ts:78-79), which sets `tab.content = content; tab.savedContent = content;` (editor.store.svelte.ts:133-134). schedule 'none' arms no timer (editor.service.ts:213-221). Nothing checks isTabDirty or flushes N before the IPC. The same 'disk-based text + markSaved=true' pattern is used by the deep-link append/prepend paths, which I did not trace in depth.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F2.
verification.repro: See F2.
verification.fix_hint: See F2.

findings.title: Editor save truncates the note in place (O_TRUNC + write_all, no temp+rename, no fsync): a crash, power loss or ENOSPC leaves an empty or partial note
findings.scenario: A) The disk is nearly full. Autosave opens N.md with truncate (N is now 0 bytes) and write_all fails with ENOSPC. The toast says 'Failed to save file.' and the tab stays dirty, but the file on disk is now empty or partial. If the user then quits (Cmd+Q, finding 1) or switches vault (finding 3), the old disk version is gone too. B) A kernel panic or power loss shortly after a save: with no fsync, APFS can persist the truncation metadata before the data blocks, leaving a zero-length or partial note. C) A sync client (iCloud/Dropbox) or the app's own watcher reads N between the truncate and the write and sees an empty file.
findings.evidence: saveFileByPath calls `writeTextFile(path, content)` with no options (editor.service.ts:168). The JS plugin sends `plugin:fs|write_text_file` with the raw bytes (dist-js/index.js:782). In Rust, write_file_inner with options=None opens with `write: true, truncate: true, create: true` (commands.rs:1169-1180) and then `file_handle.write_all(&data)` (:1201-1202). There is no temp file, no rename and no sync_all. The repo's own write_atomic doc (utils/fs.rs:11-15) says a plain O_TRUNC + write_all 'risks' a 'truncated/empty note'. Only the task toggle uses write_atomic (vault.rs:683); the main editor save does not. Mitigation that exists: on failure the in-memory copy stays dirty and the auto-save path retries every 5 s (editor.service.ts:191-193). That protects the buffer only while the app keeps running and the tab stays open.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F182: the editor save truncates in place via plugin-fs write_file_inner (commands.rs:1169-1206), and there is no temp+rename and no fsync.
verification.repro: See F182.
verification.fix_hint: See F182.

findings.title: No per-path save serialization: overlapping writes can land out of order or mix bytes
findings.scenario: Mod+S right as the 2 s autosave fires, or the 5 s retry chain overlapping a debounce run, issues two write_text_file IPCs for the same path with different snapshots (S1, then S2). Each is a separate async command that opens its own fd with O_TRUNC and writes from offset 0. If they run in parallel (A truncates, B truncates, B writes S2, A writes S1, with S1 shorter), the file holds S1 followed by the tail of S2: a spliced note. In the non-overlapping reorder case, disk keeps S1 while markSavedByPath may record S2, so the tab reads clean and disk is stale.
findings.evidence: saveFileByPath has no in-flight guard or queue (editor.service.ts:161-178). Concurrent callers are saveDirtyTabs from the debounce and from setTimeout retries, which stack without cancellation (:191-193), plus saveCurrentFile, saveAllDirtyTabs, frontmatter-write.service.ts:129 and event-calendar.service.ts:1037. Each write_text_file call opens with truncate and calls write_all independently (commands.rs:1169-1202). I did not check whether Tauri runs these async commands on a multi-threaded runtime. True parallel execution is inferred, and the window is microseconds to milliseconds.

verification.reasoning: saveFileByPath has no per-path in-flight guard (editor.service.ts:161-178). Cmd+S (global-keybindings.ts:78) does not cancel the debounce, and the retry setTimeout chains (:191-193) are never cancelled, so two write_text_file IPCs for one path can overlap. Each opens its own truncating fd (commands.rs:1169-1206). An interleaved splice needs true parallel execution on Tauri's async runtime, which I am inferring from memory and did not verify. The reorder case leaves the tab dirty (markSavedByPath stores the older snapshot, editor.store.svelte.ts:91-96), so the next keystroke or saveAllDirtyTabs on quit rewrites it. The window is milliseconds.
verification.repro: Hard to unit test, because it needs a real fs. Manual: patch the debounce to 0 ms, hold a key, press Cmd+S in a loop, and compare the file to the buffer.
verification.fix_hint: Serialize saves per path (a Map<path, Promise> chain) and re-check dirtiness after the previous write resolves.

findings.title: External edit to an open note with unsaved edits is silently discarded, then autosave overwrites it on disk (no conflict detection)
findings.scenario: 1) Note N is open and the user is typing in it. 2) Another program writes N: iCloud/Dropbox brings in an edit made on the phone, `git pull` updates N, or `echo x >> N.md`. 3) About 500 ms (Rust) + 300 ms (TS) later the watcher batch reaches reloadExternallyChangedTabs. The tab is dirty, so N is skipped and the batch is consumed. Nothing records that disk diverged. 4) Two seconds after the last keystroke, saveDirtyTabs writes the whole buffer with truncate+write. The external content is gone from disk. 5) The echo event of that save reads disk == savedContent and is a no-op. No toast, no conflict prompt. No snapshot of the external version exists, because file history snapshots only what the app saves. The loss window is not a fixed 2 s: the autosave debounce is purely trailing (no maxWait), so the tab stays dirty for an entire typing session as long as pauses are under 2 s. Any keystroke from about 2 s before the external write until the watcher reload runs (about 0.8 s after it) also causes the loss. While a save keeps failing (5 s retry loop, editor.service.ts:191-193), the tab stays dirty and every external change in that period is dropped.
findings.evidence: editor.service.ts:380 `if (!tab || isVirtualTab(tab) || isTabDirty(tab)) continue;` drops the path. The doc comment at :371-373 states the policy: "the editor always wins — the disk version is ignored and the editor content will be saved on next auto-save". saveFileByPath :163-168 writes `tab.content` with no mtime or hash precondition. plugin-fs write_file_inner opens with truncate:true and write_all (tauri-plugin-fs-2.7.1/src/commands.rs:1157-1210). debounce.ts resets the timer on every call and has no max wait. isTabDirty is a string compare (editor.logic.ts:44-46). grep for conflict/mtime/hash detection in core/editor, core/markdown-editor and app/lifecycle returned nothing. The unit test 'skips dirty tabs — editor always wins over external changes' (editor.service.test.ts:1150) asserts this as intended behavior, so the loss is by design, not an oversight. It is still silent loss of note content that another device or tool wrote.

verification.reasoning: I tried to refute this and could not; the behavior is deliberate. reloadExternallyChangedTabs skips dirty tabs (editor.service.ts:380), and its doc (:371-373) says the editor wins. The echo watcher event finds disk === savedContent and does nothing (:398). Every file-history snapshot comes from the after-save observer (file-history.service.ts:190-195), so the external version is never snapshotted. findings.title: Task toggle (Rust toggle_task_status) and deep-link daily/append writes read the stale disk copy and then wipe the open tab's unsaved edits
findings.scenario: Task toggle: 1) The user types a paragraph in note A. 2) Within 2 s (before the autosave), they switch to the Tasks tab (a virtual tab, so A's MarkdownEditor unmounts) and click a checkbox for a task in A. 3) Rust reads A from disk without the paragraph, flips the checkbox and writes it atomically. 4) syncExternalContentToEditor(A, updated, markSaved=true) sets both content and savedContent of A's tab to the Rust result, so the tab is now 'clean'. 5) The pending debounced save finds no dirty tab and does nothing. 6) When the user returns to A, MarkdownEditor mounts from tab.content: the paragraph is gone from the buffer and was never on disk. The same happens at any age of edit while autosave is failing and retrying. Possible aggravation (inferred, not run): the 'edit' source pushes the unsaved buffer into the Rust VaultIndex after 1 s idle (note-change.service.ts:88, rust:'deduped'). Task line numbers shown in the Tasks view can therefore come from the buffer, while toggle_task_in_content flips that line number in the disk copy (parsing.rs:1873-1900). It can flip a different task on disk. Deep-link: the user is typing in today's daily note and, within 2 s, fires a global capture (Raycast/Shortcuts `kokobrain://daily?content=...`). executeDailyAction reads the disk copy, appends, writes it, then calls syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true). The daily note is the active tab, so the CodeMirror doc is replaced with addToHistory(false) and the typed text is gone with no undo. new+append/prepend on an open note behaves the same.
findings.evidence: vault.rs:669 `std::fs::read_to_string(path)`, then :683 `write_atomic(path, &updated)`: the buffer is never consulted. tasks.service.ts:114 `syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, updatedContent, true, 'none')`. editor.store.svelte.ts:133-134 sets `tab.content = content; tab.savedContent = content;`. saveDirtyTabs filters on isTabDirty (editor.service.ts:184-187), so the armed timer is a no-op. EditorView.svelte:70-84: TasksView replaces MarkdownEditor, and onMount builds EditorState from tab.content (MarkdownEditor.svelte:107-108). deep-link-actions.ts:53-63: `readTextFile(filePath)` -> `writeTextFile` -> `syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, newContent, true, 'none')`. deep-link.service.ts:255-262 and :272-281 follow the same pattern. MarkdownEditor.svelte:328-333 replaces the doc with Transaction.addToHistory.of(false). Contrast with the writers that do handle this: frontmatter-write.service.ts:111-113 uses `tab.content` as the base, and link-updater.service.ts:32-35 uses the dirty buffer. toggle_task_status and the deep-link writers have no equivalent.

The tab is now dirty. 4) The apply loop checks only that the tab exists and that diskContent !== savedContent, then calls syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true). The buffer, including the new keystrokes, is replaced by disk content and marked clean. findings.title: A failed tree refresh drops the whole watcher burst: no tab reload, so the next autosave overwrites the external change
findings.scenario: 1) Note N is open and clean. 2) An external tool changes N and, in the same burst, creates or removes a folder, or leaves a subfolder the app cannot list (permission-denied dir created by another tool/user), or deletes a directory between the parent read_dir and the recursion. 3) handleChangedPaths takes the full-refresh path (or the incremental scan fails and falls back to refreshTree). scan_vault fails because a child read_dir error propagates with `?`. 4) refreshTree rethrows. handleChangedPaths was `void`-ed, so the rejection goes unhandled and notifyListeners is never called for this burst. reloadExternallyChangedTabs and rebuildAllIndexes never see N. 5) The tab keeps showing the old content as clean. The next keystroke plus autosave writes old content + edit over the external change. With a persistent unlistable folder, every later burst fails the same way, so external changes to open notes are never reloaded for the rest of the session.
findings.evidence: fs.watcher.ts:137 and :149 `await refreshTree();` have no try, and notifyListeners runs only after it (:139, :151). The catch at :172-178 calls refreshTree again with no try. :199 `void handleChangedPaths(payload.paths)`. fs.service.ts:96-99 logs and `throw err`. vault.rs:96 `fs::read_dir(dir).map_err(...)?` and :139 `Some(scan_dir(&file_path, sort_by, depth + 1)?)` fail the whole scan for one unreadable or vanished child dir (per-entry stat failures are skipped at :114-117, but read_dir failures are not). The trigger frequency (a permission-denied dir, a deletion mid-scan) is inferred, not reproduced. A persistently unreadable dir present at vault open would already fail the initial load and be noticed.

verification.reasoning: The path exists. handleChangedPaths calls `await refreshTree()` with no try at fs.watcher.ts:137 and :149, and again inside the incremental catch at :172-178. notifyListeners (:73-81), the only route to onFileChange and so to reloadExternallyChangedTabs and rebuildAllIndexes, runs only after it. The listener is `void handleChangedPaths(...)` (:199), so a rejection is unhandled. refreshTree -> loadDirectoryTree rethrows (fs.service.ts:96-99). scan_dir fails the whole scan if one child read_dir fails (commands/vault.rs:96, recursed with `?` at :139). Per-entry stat failures are skipped (:114-117), but a directory that vanishes between its stat and its read_dir, or a subdir the process cannot list, aborts the scan. The clean tab then keeps stale content, and the next edit plus autosave overwrites the external change. I could not settle the trigger frequency. The watcher only fires after 500 ms of quiet, so a mid-scan deletion needs another writer to still be running. A persistently unlistable dir present at open would already have failed the initial load.
verification.repro: vitest with mocked call: make scan_vault reject. Feed handleChangedPaths a batch that takes the full-refresh branch, with an onFileChange listener registered. Assert the listener is never called. In the app: open clean N.md, then from a shell `mkdir X && chmod 000 X && echo ext >> N.md`. The tab is not reloaded.
verification.fix_hint: Wrap the refreshTree calls in try/catch and always notifyListeners(changedPaths), even when the tree refresh fails. In scan_dir, skip unreadable subdirectories (log and continue) instead of propagating with `?`.

findings.title: Self-save TTL (15 s, refreshed on every autosave) makes the watcher skip index rebuilds for genuine external writes
findings.scenario: The user autosaves N at T. At T+10 s a sync client writes N (the burst is [N] only). areAllRecentSaves([N]) is true, so rebuildAllIndexes returns early. If N is the active clean tab, the reload updates the buffer, and the layout content effect re-indexes VaultIndex with source 'edit', but FTS5 and semantic rows stay stale (the 'edit' change carries no vaultPath). If N is a background tab or closed, nothing is re-indexed: backlinks, tags, tasks and properties keep the pre-sync content until the next save or full rebuild. The TTL is reset on each save, so during an editing session the skip window never closes. Stale task line numbers in the Tasks view then feed toggle_task_status the wrong line (it flips whatever task sits on that line on disk). This does not affect the editor buffer: the tab reload is not gated by the self-save check (app-lifecycle.service.ts:486).
findings.evidence: watcher-handler.service.ts:41 `if (changedPaths.length > 0 && (filePaths.length === 0 || areAllRecentSaves(filePaths))) { ... return; }`. editor.hooks.ts:24 `RECENT_SAVE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000`, and markRecentSave (:37-44) re-arms the timer on every save. The check is path-only: it cannot tell our write from a later external write to the same path. +layout.svelte:137-155 indexes only the ACTIVE tab, through updateIndexesForFile (source 'edit', no vaultPath; index-updater.service.ts:34-40).

verification.reasoning: areAllRecentSaves is path-only (editor.hooks.ts:47-49). markRecentSave re-arms a 15 s TTL on every save (:37-43). rebuildAllIndexes returns early when all paths are recent saves (watcher-handler.service.ts:41-44), so an external write within 15 s of our own save to the same path is never indexed. The tab reload still runs first (app-lifecycle.service.ts:486), so the editor buffer is safe. For the active tab, the layout effect re-indexes VaultIndex through updateIndexesForFile with source 'edit' (+layout.svelte:137-155, index-updater.service.ts:33-43). That carries no vaultPath, so FTS and semantic stay stale. Background or closed notes stay stale everywhere. Task toggles use the stale line number with no expected-text check (commands/vault.rs:664-683, toggle_task_in_content by line only). The toggle can flip whatever checkbox now sits on that line on disk, which is a small silent edit to note bytes. That raises the finding slightly above an index-only problem but leaves it low.
verification.repro: Save N.md in the app. Within 15 s, rewrite N.md externally so a task moves to a different line. The watcher logs 'all 1 file(s) are self-saves'. get_tasks_in_section_v2 / get_all_tasks_v2 still return the old line, and toggling it in the Tasks view flips the wrong line.
verification.fix_hint: Make self-save detection content-aware. Store a hash of the saved bytes in recentSaves and, in the watcher, skip only paths whose disk bytes still match (read_files_batch is cheap for at most 10 files). Separately, have toggle_task_status verify the expected task text on the line.

findings.title: Deleting a note or folder throws away its unsaved editor buffer; a failed Trash move throws it away too
findings.scenario: A) Type a paragraph in note A, then within 2 s open the action bar menu (NoteActionBar.svelte:214), choose Move to Trash and press Enter on the confirm. The 2 s body autosave has not fired. The tab is force-removed, the disk file holding the older bytes goes to .kokobrain/trash, and the paragraph exists nowhere. Restoring from Trash brings back the old text. B) Autosave keeps failing on A (for example the file was made read-only: chmod 444 blocks write_text_file, but rename only needs write permission on the folder). The 'Failed to save file.' toast repeats with a 5 s retry. The user deletes the note, and every edit since the last successful save is gone. C) moveToTrash throws (mkdir or rename failure). The tab is already gone, the note stays on disk with old content, and the user sees 'could not move to Trash' with the buffer already lost. A second variant has moveToTrash resolve and asserts the trashed bytes are 'old'.

findings.title: Link rewrite after a rename drops keystrokes typed into an affected open note while its read/write IPC is in flight
findings.scenario: Note X is open and active and contains [[Plan]]. The user renames Plan.md to Roadmap.md from the note list, then clicks back into X and starts typing while updateLinksAfterRename is still running. On a hub note with hundreds of backlinks, all reads and writes go out in parallel through Promise.allSettled, so the window grows from a few ms to hundreds of ms. Characters typed after X's snapshot (clean tab: the disk read at :35; dirty tab: the buffer snapshot at :35, then the write at :39) reach tab.content through updateContent. When the write resolves, syncExternalContentToEditor overwrites tab.content and savedContent with the older rewritten text, and the content-sync effect replaces the whole CodeMirror doc with it. The typed characters vanish. Cmd+Z cannot bring them back, because the replace is not in history and the user's own transactions are mapped away. The tab is marked clean, so nothing is saved later. renameType repeats the pattern serially for every open tab (type-definitions.service.ts:215-221: content captured, await writeTextFile, then sync).
findings.evidence: link-updater.service.ts:35 takes `content` from openTab.content (dirty) or `await readTextFile` (clean). :39 `await writeTextFile(filePath, updatedContent)`. :47 `syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, updatedContent, true, 'none')`. No re-check that tab.content is unchanged since the snapshot. editor.service.ts:78-79 calls updateTabContentByPath, which sets content AND savedContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136), and bumps the signal for the active tab (:87-88). MarkdownEditor.svelte:310-335 dispatches `changes: {from: 0, to: doc.length, insert: content}` with `Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)` (:332). Keystrokes reach the store synchronously (editor-extensions.ts:170-189 -> editor.service.ts:224-227 -> editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88), so they ARE in tab.content when the overwrite lands. Mitigation that exists: the renamed note itself is excluded (:28), so typing in the renamed note is safe; only OTHER open notes that link to it are exposed. Fix shape: after the write, merge only if `tab.content === content` (the snapshot), otherwise re-apply replaceWikilinks to the current buffer and leave it dirty.

verification.reasoning: Same snapshot-await-markSaved pattern in link-updater.service.ts:33-47. The hub-note window detail is covered in the F45 verdict.
verification.repro: See F45.
verification.fix_hint: See F45.

findings.title: Rename leaves path-qualified and extension wikilinks unrewritten; they silently break or retarget another note with the same name
findings.scenario: Note A contains [[Work/Plan]] (Obsidian writes this form when a name is ambiguous) or [[Plan.md]]. Rename Work/Plan.md to Work/Roadmap.md. A is returned as a backlink and gets processed, but nothing in it changes. After the rename the link is unresolved. Worse, if Home/Plan.md exists, [[Work/Plan]] now silently resolves to Home/Plan.md through the basename fallback, so A points at the wrong note with no warning. Deterministic, not a race.
findings.evidence: Rust resolves wikilinks against `by_path`, which is keyed only by the lowercase note name (index.rs:305-307). resolve_with_cache (index.rs:110-124) tries the full lowercase target, which never matches a key that contains '/', then falls back to note_name_from_target, which strips the folder and the extension (index.rs:85-91). So [[Work/Plan]] and [[Plan.md]] both resolve to Plan, and A is in get_backlinks_v2(Plan). replaceWikilinks only rewrites when `target.trim().toLowerCase() === oldNameLower` (link-updater.logic.ts:27), and oldName is the bare stem (extractNoteName -> stem, :14-16). 'work/plan' and 'plan.md' do not equal 'plan', so the match returns fullMatch unchanged. The service does not report that a backlink file was left unchanged (link-updater.service.ts:38).

verification.repro: See F47.
verification.fix_hint: See F47.

findings.title: An autosave that overlaps the rename/move IPC recreates a ghost copy of the note at the old path
findings.scenario: Most realistic trigger is auto-move: the user sets a lifecycle property (frontmatter save at +500 ms) and keeps typing in the body. Auto-move fires 3000 ms after the save (settings.store.svelte.ts:104) and calls moveItem on the note being edited. If the 2 s body debounce fires during the `await diskOp()` rename round trip, saveDirtyTabs still sees tab.path === old path and calls writeTextFile(old) with the default create:true. That recreates the note in its original folder with the current buffer, next to the moved copy. markSavedByPath(old) then finds no tab, because the tab was already re-pathed, so the moved tab stays dirty. notifyAfterSave(old) indexes the ghost and runs the after-save observers on it (auto-move's second moveItem is then refused by exists()). Result: a duplicate note the user did not create. No content is lost, because the moved tab still holds the buffer and saves it to the new path on the next keystroke or on quit. The same ordering applies to delete when a write is already in flight as the Trash rename lands: the deleted note reappears.
findings.evidence: The tab is re-pathed only after the disk op resolves (path-change.service.ts:127 then :132). saveFileByPath reads the path when the timer fires (editor.service.ts:162-168) and writes with plugin-fs defaults. write_file_inner opens with create:true, truncate:true when no options are passed (/tmp copy of plugins-workspace fs-v2.7.1 commands.rs:1166-1180). Ordering cannot be relied on: write_text_file is `pub async fn` (commands.rs:1238), which tauri-macros 2.7.4 runs in the Async execution context, while rename is a plain `pub fn` (commands.rs:840), which runs Blocking (~/.cargo/registry/.../tauri-macros-2.7.4/src/command/wrapper.rs:243-259). So a write sent just before a rename can still open the old path after the rename completes. markSavedByPath matches by path (editor.store.svelte.ts:91-96). Mitigations that exist: a timer that fires AFTER :132 writes to the new path. A folder move is safe, because write_file does not create parent directories, so the stale write fails ENOENT and the 5 s retry (editor.service.ts:191-193) saves at the new path. The window is about one IPC round trip, so the rate is low; it is reachable only because auto-move moves the note the user is actively editing.

verification.reasoning: saveFileByPath captures tab.path when the timer fires (editor.service.ts:161-168), and the tab is re-pathed only after diskOp resolves (path-change.service.ts:127, 132). A write that is in flight while the rename runs can recreate the old path, with the default create flag. The auto-move scenario is reachable. Ordering between the async write and the sync rename commands depends on Tauri's executor (not verified here). Content is not lost because the moved tab stays dirty and saves to the new path.
verification.repro: Hard to unit test because it needs real IPC ordering. Manual test: edit a body, set a lifecycle property that triggers auto-move, keep typing around 3 s, and look for a duplicate in the old folder.
verification.fix_hint: Have a path-change barrier wait for in-flight saves (or cancel the debounce) before diskOp, or write with create:false on autosave.

findings.title: Case-only rename (note.md -> Note.md) is always refused on case-insensitive APFS
findings.scenario: Rename 'meeting notes.md' to 'Meeting Notes.md' in the explorer or the note list. renameItem compares the strings exactly (they differ), then exists('/v/Meeting Notes.md') returns true on case-insensitive APFS, because it is the same file. The user gets '"Meeting Notes.md" already exists in this folder', and a case fix is impossible from inside the app. No data is lost: the pre-check is what prevents an overwrite here.
findings.evidence: fs.service.ts:204 `if (oldPath === newPath) return oldPath;` is a case-sensitive compare. :205 `if (await exists(newPath)) throw targetExistsError(newName)`. plugin-fs exists is `resolved_path.exists()` (commands.rs:1255-1270), a stat that succeeds case-insensitively on default APFS (from memory: APFS default is case-insensitive; not run). link-updater.service.ts:25 already treats a case-only change as 'same name', so links would be fine if the rename were allowed. The same exists() checks protect move (fs.service.ts:233) and restore (trash.service.ts:116-118), so collisions there are refused or suffixed rather than overwritten. The remaining TOCTOU between exists and std::fs::rename (which replaces an existing file, commands.rs:864) needs an outside writer in a ms window.

verification.reasoning: Same check at fs.service.ts:204-205.
verification.repro: See F46.
verification.fix_hint: See F46.

findings.title: A failure after the disk rename is reported as a failed rename, and the index re-key and old-path sweep are skipped
findings.scenario: The disk rename succeeds and the tab is re-pathed, but `get_backlinks_v2` (lock poisoned) or `refreshTree`/scan_vault rejects. applyPathChange throws. rename_note and the forgetNote sweep never run, links are not rewritten, and FilesNavigator toasts 'Could not rename' (via runOrToast) even though the file IS renamed. A retry fails because the old path is gone. The watcher eventually re-indexes the new path.

Only rename_note is caught (:158-162). The doc comment at :111-113 claims 'Never throws on the index legs'. renameItem rethrows (fs.service.ts:216-218). get_backlinks_v2 only errors on a poisoned lock (vault.rs:436-438), so this is rare.

verification.fix_hint: See F50.

findings.title: Canvas onDestroy flush writes the canvas JSON into whichever tab becomes active, overwriting a markdown note (auto-saved)
findings.scenario: (a) In a .canvas tab, click the header of a file card for note D. The mousedown selects the node and the click calls openFileInEditor(D). (b) Or type in a canvas text card and within 300 ms switch tabs to a markdown note (Cmd+Shift+], tab click, Quick Switcher). (c) Or cycle tabs quickly through a canvas tab: xyflow re-measures the nodes on every mount. In each case the markdown note D's tab content is replaced with the canvas JSON. 2 s later the body auto-save writes D.md = canvas JSON. D's real text is gone from disk. In-app recovery depends on a file-history snapshot. The canvas's own last edit also goes into D instead of the .canvas file.
findings.evidence: CanvasInner.svelte:211-226: every change to `nodes` sets `pendingPersist = true` and arms a 300 ms timer. xyflow reassigns store.nodes on node mousedown selection (store/index.js:160-169 addSelectedNodes, wired from NodeWrapper.svelte:247 onNodeMouseDown) and on measurement (store/index.js:73), and `bind:nodes` (CanvasInner.svelte:580) propagates the change. CanvasInner.svelte:230-234: `onDestroy(() => { if (pendingPersist) persistChanges(nodes, edges); })` -> persistWithoutHistory (line 108) `onJsonChange(json)`. EditorView.svelte:81 passes `onJsonChange={onContentChange}`. editor.service.ts:225 `editorStore.updateContent(content)` writes `tabs[activeIndex].content` (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88), with no path. CanvasView is destroyed *because* activeIndex changed: `isCanvasTab` is derived from activeTab (EditorView.svelte:36, 80). Svelte 5.57.2 BranchManager.#commit (branches.js:132-160) destroys the old branch synchronously right after creating the new one, so activeIndex already points at D when onDestroy runs. scheduleAutoSave('body') -> saveDirtyTabs -> saveFileByPath(D.path) writes the JSON. The new MarkdownEditor's onMount (a user effect queued after the block update) then reads tab.content, which is now the JSON, so the user sees JSON in D but cannot undo it (fresh EditorState, no history). Commit c3ab02d4 added this flush for the app-quit case with no test, and it did not consider tab switches. Close variant: closing a clean canvas tab within 300 ms of a selection or measurement skips the dirty prompt (closeTab at editor.service.ts:271), removeTab moves activeIndex to the neighbour, and the JSON lands in the neighbour tab.

verification.reasoning: This has the same root cause as F5. The file-card click variant depends on the path format: FileNode.handleClick (FileNode.svelte:54-56) passes data.file raw, but the preview read prefixes vaultStore.path (:39). If data.file is vault-relative, openFileInEditor may fail to read it and never switch tabs. The tab-switch, close and selection triggers stand.
verification.repro: See F5.
verification.fix_hint: See F5.

findings.title: One CodeMirror undo history is shared by all tabs: Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z in note B re-inserts text deleted or undone in note A, then auto-saves B
findings.scenario: In note A, edit with any backspace, delete a paragraph, or replace a selection. Switch to note B (tab click or Cmd+Shift+]) and press Cmd+Z, for example to undo something in B or by reflex. A's deleted text is inserted into B, mapped to the end of B's doc. Each further Cmd+Z injects more of A's fragments. The same happens with Cmd+Shift+Z after undoing typing in A: A's undone text is redone into B. The update listener treats it as a user edit, so B is saved 2 s later with A's content (also a privacy leak between notes). History is only reset when MarkdownEditor remounts, i.e. after visiting a canvas, kanban-board or collection tab.
findings.evidence: There is one EditorView for every tab. The tab switch never creates a new EditorState: MarkdownEditor.svelte:230-235 dispatches `changes: {from:0,to:doc.length,insert:tab.content}` with `Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)`. In @codemirror/commands:240-241 such a transaction calls `state.addMapping(tr.changes.desc)`, which maps the old events (addMappingToBranch/mapEvent at 460-488) and does not drop them. Inverted deletions are insertions, and they survive mapping through the full-doc replace. Reproduced with the repo's own CodeMirror packages (node -e, no files written): doc 'Note A secret paragraph here...', delete ' secret paragraph', replace the doc with B using addToHistory(false), undo() -> 'Note B completely different content\nsecond line of B\nthird secret paragraph'. Redo variant: type ' my private sentence' in A, undo, replace with B, redo() -> 'Note B body my private sentence'. undo/redo transactions are not isTabSwitching or isExternalEdit, so editor-extensions.ts:171-188 calls onDocChanged -> onContentChange -> B dirty -> auto-save. Nothing in src/lib uses historyField, isolateHistory or setState to reset history (grep returned nothing), and no test covers undo across tabs.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F84. The redo variant this finding adds is real: type ' secret' in A, undo, switch to B, redo gives 'Note B body secret' (reproduced in memory). The underlying mechanism is the same shared history mapped through the addToHistory(false) replace, and so is the fix.
verification.repro: See F84. Redo variant: insert text in A, Cmd+Z, switch to B, Cmd+Shift+Z.
verification.fix_hint: See F84. A per-tab history or a history reset also clears the undone branch.

findings.title: File-history Restore writes the snapshot into whatever note the editor shows, not the file the history dialog is for
findings.scenario: With note A active, press Cmd+Shift+H, pick an old snapshot, then press Cmd+W (a natural way to try to close the dialog), Cmd+Shift+] or Cmd+Shift+[ while the modal is still open. The keydown reaches the global handlers, so A's tab closes or the active tab becomes B, but the dialog stays open showing 'File History: A.md'. Click 'Restore This Version' and confirm. B's whole content is replaced with A's old snapshot and written to B's path at once by saveCurrentFile(). A is not restored. Variant: when the active tab is a kanban in board mode or a canvas, MarkdownEditor is unmounted (editorView null), so nothing is dispatched, saveCurrentFile is a no-op and the dialog resets: the restore silently does nothing.
findings.evidence: file-history.service.ts:85-86 reads `fileHistoryStore.filePath` but uses it only for a null check and a debug line. Lines 89-94 dispatch the snapshot into `editorStore.editorView`, the single shared view holding the active tab's doc. The update listener -> onContentChange -> updateContent(tabs[activeIndex]). Line 98 `await saveCurrentFile()` saves `editorStore.activeTab` (editor.service.ts:151-155). There is no `activeTabPath === filePath` check. The dialog does not stop the shortcuts: bits-ui 2.20.2 focus-scope.svelte.js:141-156 handles only the Tab key, and registerKeybinding (utils/keybindings.ts:30-47) listens on document with no dialog guard. Contrast the explicit `[role="dialog"]` guard on the '/' binding at global-keybindings.ts:44. Nothing closes the dialog on a tab change: fileHistoryStore.reset/setOpen(false) are only called at file-history.service.ts:100 and 182.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F67: restore targets the active editor view and tab instead of fileHistoryStore.filePath. Its null-view variant is F69.
verification.repro: See F67.
verification.fix_hint: See F67.

findings.title: Meta-bind button with an open/createNote action followed by updateMetadata writes the property into the other note
findings.scenario: Note A contains a button with `actions: [{type: open, link: '[[B]]'}, {type: updateMetadata, bindTarget: status, value: done}]`, or a createNote action followed by updateMetadata. Clicking it opens B, then the updateMetadata step rewrites B's frontmatter: it is re-serialized through parse/rebuild and gets `status: done`. The new value goes into B instead of the button's own note A, and B is auto-saved after 500 ms. If the effect order is the other way round (the dispatch lands before the tab-switch effect runs), A's whole document plus the new frontmatter is written into tab B's content.
findings.evidence: The click handler (meta-bind-button-widget.ts:33-36) runs the actions sequentially with `await` and the `view` captured at toDOM time. That view is the app's only EditorView and is reused for every tab. `open` awaits host.openLink -> openFileInEditor -> setActiveIndex/addTab (editor-host.ts:76-79, editor.service.ts:114-140). Svelte's flush microtask is queued before the await continuations, so the tab-switch effect has already replaced the doc with B. Then `updateMetadata` calls dispatchMetaBindUpdate(view, ...) (widgets.ts:754-768), which reads `view.state.doc`, now B, and dispatches a frontmatter change. updateListener -> onContentChange -> tabs[activeIndex] (B) -> 500 ms frontmatter auto-save. dispatchMetaBindUpdate's JSDoc (widgets.ts:743-745) describes it as the write for the button's updateMetadata, meaning the note containing the button. No path is checked anywhere in the chain.

verification.reasoning: Same chain as F104. The alternative ordering it raises (dispatch landing before the tab-swap effect, so A's document goes into tab B) is refuted. The Svelte flush microtask is queued when activeIndex is written, before openFileInEditor resolves, so the swap always comes first.
verification.repro: See F104.
verification.fix_hint: See F104.

findings.title: Watcher reload does not re-check dirty state after the async read, so keystrokes typed during the read are discarded
findings.scenario: Note A is open and clean, and an external tool (sync client, git pull, another editor) modifies A.md. About 800 ms later (Rust 500 ms + TS 300 ms debounce) the batch runs: A is eligible because it is clean. While readTextFile is in flight (larger when the batch reads up to 10 files in parallel), the user types in A, which makes it dirty. When the read resolves, A's content and savedContent are overwritten with the disk version and the CodeMirror doc is replaced. The characters typed in that window are lost, and nothing marks the tab dirty again.
findings.evidence: Eligibility is checked before the await: line 380 `if (!tab || isVirtualTab(tab) || isTabDirty(tab)) continue;`. After `await Promise.allSettled(...)` the code claims to re-check ('Re-check tab state — it may have changed during parallel reads', line 396), but line 398 only tests `diskContent === tab.savedContent`, not isTabDirty. It then calls `syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, diskContent, true, 'none')`, which sets content=savedContent=disk (store lines 130-136) and bumps the signal, so MarkdownEditor.svelte:329-333 replaces the doc. This contradicts the function's own contract ('If the user has unsaved edits, the editor always wins', lines 371-373). The window is small (one IPC read), so the loss is a few keystrokes.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause, editor.service.ts:396-401.
verification.repro: See F3.
verification.fix_hint: See F3.

findings.title: Async language load from a code-file tab can land on the next (markdown) tab
findings.scenario: Switch to a .ts/.py tab for the first time in the session, and within the dynamic-import time of its parser switch to a .md tab. The markdown tab gets the markdown language synchronously, then the late TypeScript/Python reconfigure arrives and is applied to the markdown doc. Unlike the rAF chain (MarkdownEditor.svelte:251-257), there is no abort signal.

findings.title: Undo history survives the full-doc replaces of tab switches and external syncs. Cmd+Z then inserts text deleted earlier (even text from ANOTHER note) at the end of the current note, and autosave writes it
findings.scenario: Cross-note case: in note A the user selects a paragraph and deletes or cuts it. They switch to note B with a tab click, Cmd+Shift+] or the quick switcher, type a few words, then hold Cmd+Z to go back to B's opened state. After B's own edits are undone, the next Cmd+Z appends A's deleted paragraph to the end of B. The updateListener reports it as a user edit, so B is autosaved to disk with A's text. Same-note case (more frequent): the user deletes or replaces text, then changes a property in the Properties panel, toggles a task in the Tasks panel, gets a watcher reload, or a rename rewrites a link. Cmd+Z drops the typing undo events and puts the deleted text at the end of the note instead of where it was. That silently corrupts the note, often off-screen at the bottom of a long note.
findings.evidence:
There is one EditorView for all markdown tabs and one history() (editor-extensions.ts:130). The tab switch replaces the whole doc with `changes: {from: 0, to: view.state.doc.length, insert: tab.content}` and `Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)` (MarkdownEditor.svelte:230-235). The external sync does the same (:329-333). Nothing resets or isolates history: a grep for isolateHistory, historyField and clearHistory in src/lib finds nothing. A non-history change makes CM call `state.addMapping(tr.changes.desc)` (commands dist/index.js:241), which maps every stored inverse change set through the replace (mapEvent :484, `event.changes.map(mapping)`). In state mapSet (:1104-1117), when B (the full replace) covers A's change, A's deletion is dropped and its insertion is emitted after B's inserted text, i.e. at the end of the new document. Reproduced with node against the repo's node_modules: doc 'NOTE A
keep
SECRET PARAGRAPH OF A
end', delete 'SECRET PARAGRAPH OF A', then a full replace with 'NOTE B
body of b' using addToHistory(false), then undo() gives the doc "NOTE B
body of bSECRET PARAGRAPH OF A". The undo transaction is a normal docChanged update, and isTabSwitching/isExternalEdit are false by then, so editor-extensions.ts:171-188 calls onContentChange -> editorStore.updateContent + scheduleAutoSave (editor.service.ts:224-227), and the corrupted bytes are written to disk. No per-tab EditorState exists (tab-view-state only keeps scroll and cursor).

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F84. The same-note external sync case (Properties, task toggle, watcher reload, link rewrite) goes through MarkdownEditor.svelte:329-333 with the same addToHistory(false) full replace. I reproduced it: 'abc foo def', delete 'foo ', replace, undo gives 'abc def\n- [x] taskfoo '.
verification.repro: See F84, external-sync variant.
verification.fix_hint: See F84. For the external sync, dispatch a minimal prefix/suffix diff instead of a full-doc replace.

findings.title: Table +row/+col rewrites the whole table from raw cell source: it doubles backslashes, breaks aliased wikilinks, deletes cells beyond the header count, and strips `> `/indent prefixes from tables in callouts, blockquotes and lists
findings.scenario: The user hovers a rendered table and clicks the + (add row or add column) button once. (a) A cell holding `[[Project X|PX]]` becomes `[[Project X\|PX]]`. The link target is now `Project X\`, so the link is broken in live preview, the backlink disappears from the Rust index, and rename link-rewrites no longer match it. Each further click adds more backslashes (`\\\|`, then 7). (b) Any backslash in any cell (`C:\Users`, `$\alpha$`, `` `a\b` ``) is doubled on every click. (c) A row with more cells than the header (`| a | b | c |` under a 2-column header) loses the extra cells, i.e. text is deleted. (d) A table inside a callout or blockquote (`> [!note]` / `> | a | b |` ...) loses the `> ` prefix on every line after the first. The callout breaks: the rest of the table falls out of it, and the following `> ` lines become a separate plain blockquote. Tables in list items lose their indentation the same way. Every case is written to disk by autosave.
findings.evidence:
Cells are raw source slices: `raw.push(state.doc.sliceString(child.from, child.to).trim())` (table.ts:92). Lezer GFM keeps `\|` unsplit and leaves the backslash in the cell (lezer dist/index.js:2092-2117, esc handling). A `[[a|b]]` split is merged back as raw text (table.ts:96-111). renderTableSource then escapes the RAW text again: `cell.replace(/\/g, '\\').replace(/\|/g, '\|')` (widgets.ts:491). The test at table-widget.test.ts:35-38 assumes decoded input ('has|pipe'), which the parser never produces. Simulating the exact escape: '[[Note|Alias]]' -> '[[Note\|Alias]]' -> '[[Note\\|Alias]]' -> 7 backslashes; 'C:\x' -> 'C:\x'. WIKILINK_DECORATION_RE `\[\[([^\]|#]*)...` (decoration.logic.ts:2-3), the Rust split `raw.find('|')` (parsing.rs:1088) and link-updater.logic.ts:8 all read the target as `Note\`. Truncation: normalizeRow `cells.slice(0, columnCount)` (table.ts:56, applied at :143) feeds `this.rows`, which buildAppendRowSource/buildAppendColumnSource rewrite over the whole `sourceRange.from..to` (widgets.ts:470-480). Blockquote: a node parse of '> [!note] T
> | a | b |
> | --- | --- |
> | [[Note|Alias]] | C:\x |
> after' shows the Table node spans "| a | b |
> | --- | --- |
> ... 
> after", i.e. it includes the continuation `> ` markers. renderTableSource joins bare lines (widgets.ts:494-502), so the markers are deleted. computeTables does not skip tables in containers (table-field.ts:20-46). Mitigation that does exist: sourceRange is compared in eq() (widgets.ts:383-388), and every docChanged rebuilds (block-decorator.ts:82, check-update-action.ts:20), so the offsets themselves are not stale.

verification.reasoning: This bundles three already-confirmed root causes: re-escaping raw cells (F99), truncating cells beyond the header (F98), and container prefixes in the Table range (F100). Each was verified separately above with the Lezer parse and widgets.ts:468-503.
verification.fix_hint: Replace the full re-serialisation with a minimal insertion that keeps existing bytes verbatim. That fixes F98, F99 and F100 together.

findings.title: File History restore writes the snapshot into whatever tab is active, not the file the dialog was opened for, and saves it over that file
findings.scenario: The user opens File History for note A (Cmd+Shift+H) and picks an old snapshot. While the dialog is open, the active tab changes: Cmd+Shift+[ or ] or Cmd+W (global keybindings are not gated by open dialogs), or a deep link or quick-capture opens another note. The user clicks Restore and confirms the native ask() dialog. A's snapshot replaces the editor doc of the now-active note B, and saveCurrentFile() writes it to B's path. B's real content is gone from the editor and the disk; only B's own file-history snapshots can bring it back. A related silent failure: if the active tab is not a markdown editor (editorView null), the dispatch is skipped, nothing is saved, the dialog resets, and the user believes A was restored.
findings.evidence: restoreSnapshot reads `fileHistoryStore.filePath` (file-history.service.ts:86) only for an early return. It then dispatches `{from: 0, to: view.state.doc.length, insert: restoredContent}` into `editorStore.editorView` (:90-95), the ACTIVE view, and calls `saveCurrentFile()` (:99). saveCurrentFile saves `editorStore.activeTab` (editor.service.ts:151-155). No check that activeTabPath === filePath exists across the awaits (the ask() at FileHistoryDialog.svelte:44-48 and `call('get_snapshot_content')` at :85). registerKeybinding's handler has no dialog guard (utils/keybindings.ts:31-49), unlike the slash binding, which checks `closest('[role="dialog"]')` (global-keybindings.ts:44). The tab switch/close bindings are at global-keybindings.ts:82-99. The cross-audit plan only notes the null-view no-op (.scratch/cross-audit-plan-2026-08-12/plan-2026-08-12.md:128), not the wrong-target write. I did not verify that bits-ui Dialog lets Cmd+Shift+] reach the document listener; the deep-link and quick-capture route does not depend on that.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause and code path as F67 (file-history.service.ts:86-99, editor.service.ts:151-155).
verification.repro: See F67.
verification.fix_hint: See F67.

findings.title: TSV paste handler turns any pasted text whose first line has a tab into a markdown table, including tab-indented sub-lists and code pasted inside a fenced code block
findings.scenario:
In live preview the user copies nested list items starting on an indented line (`	- child one
	- child two`, which is how this tab-indented app stores them), or copies Go or Makefile code, and pastes it, even inside a ``` fence. Instead of the text they get `|  | - child one |
| --- | --- |
|  | - child two |`. A cell that begins with `"` turns on quote mode, which removes the quotes and can merge lines. The pasted content is mangled. It is recoverable with Cmd+Z (userEvent input.paste) and the clipboard still holds the original, so no stored data is lost, but it can go unnoticed in a long paste.
findings.evidence: looksLikeTSV only requires a tab and at least 2 cells in the first row (paste-tsv.logic.ts:19-26). A leading tab yields ['', 'rest'], so 2 cells. The handler has no syntax-context check (code block, frontmatter) before `event.preventDefault()` and replacing the main selection (paste-tsv-handler.ts:19-38). It only replaces `selection.main`, so the other cursors of a multi-cursor paste get nothing. The quote handling at paste-tsv.logic.ts:69-73 starts a quoted cell on any leading `"`.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F121: looksLikeTSV accepts any first line with a leading tab, and pasteTsvHandler has no context check.

findings.title: Toggling a task in the Tasks tab throws away unsaved edits in that note's open tab
findings.scenario: 1) Open note A, which has a `- [ ] Buy milk` task. 2) Type a paragraph in A. 3) Within 2 s (before the body autosave fires), switch to the Tasks tab (a virtual tab in the same editor strip) and click any checkbox from note A. Rust reads A from DISK, which does not have the paragraph yet, flips the box and writes the file. The frontend then replaces the tab's content AND savedContent with that disk-derived text. The tab is now 'clean', so the pending autosave writes nothing, and the paragraph is gone from memory and from disk. The doc replace uses addToHistory(false), so Cmd+Z cannot bring it back. The window is wider when saves are failing (each retry waits 5 s, editor.service.ts:191-193) or when the user types and then goes to Tasks.
findings.evidence: toggle_task_status_inner reads `std::fs::read_to_string(path)` (vault.rs:669), toggles, `write_atomic` (vault.rs:683) and returns `updated_content`. toggleTask then calls `syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, updatedContent, true, 'none')` (tasks.service.ts:114). markSaved=true goes to `editorStore.updateTabContentByPath`, which sets `tab.content = content; tab.savedContent = content` (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-135). The open tab is never checked for dirtiness, and nothing flushes the debounced save on a tab switch: the only saveFileByPath/saveAllDirtyTabs callers are the explicit save command, close/vault-switch, frontmatter-write and event-calendar. MarkdownEditor's external sync dispatch is `annotations: Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)` (MarkdownEditor.svelte:329-333). Existing mitigations elsewhere show the expected pattern, and the tasks path lacks it: updateNoteFrontmatter edits `tab.content` and saves it (frontmatter-write.service.ts:112-136), and updateLinksAfterRename uses `openTab.content` when the tab is dirty (link-updater.service.ts:33-35).

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F2.
verification.repro: See F2.
verification.fix_hint: See F2.

findings.title: Main note save truncates the file in place (no temp+rename, no fsync): a failed write leaves the note empty or cut short on disk
findings.scenario: The disk is nearly full, or the vault is on an external drive or network volume that drops mid-write. Autosave fires for a 40 KB note. The open truncates the file to 0 bytes, then write_all fails partway with ENOSPC or EIO. The note on disk is now empty or truncated, and its previously saved content is gone too. The app only shows 'Failed to save file.', keeps retrying every 5 s (each retry truncates again), and on quit asks 'Close anyway and lose unsaved changes?'. A user who answers yes believes the last saved version is still on disk, but the file is empty. A crash or power loss between truncate and write gives the same result. Sync daemons (iCloud/Dropbox) can also pick up the 0-byte state. The same non-atomic write is used by link-updater.service.ts:39, type-definitions.service.ts:218/291/309, deep-link.service.ts:260-313 and deep-link-actions.ts:61/173.
findings.evidence: saveFileByPath calls `await writeTextFile(path, content)` (editor.service.ts:168) with no options. The plugin's write_file_inner, with no options, opens with `write: true, truncate: true, create: true` (commands.rs:1171-1180) and then calls `file_handle.write_all(&data)` (commands.rs:1198-1206). There is no temp file, no rename and no sync_all. The repo already has `write_atomic` (fs.rs:16-32, temp file in the same directory, then rename), whose own doc comment names this exact risk ('never a truncated/empty note, which is what a plain std::fs::write (O_TRUNC + write_all) risks'), but only the Rust writers use it (toggle_task_status, create_note, propagate_type_rename), not the main editor save. Partial write on ENOSPC follows from std write_all semantics. I did not reproduce the APFS crash-consistency behaviour.

verification.reasoning: saveFileByPath calls writeTextFile(path, content) with no options (editor.service.ts:168). In the locked tauri-plugin-fs 2.7.1 (Cargo.lock:5557-5558; JS package also 2.7.1), write_file_inner with no options opens with write:true, truncate:true, create:true (commands.rs:1169-1180) and then calls write_all (:1198-1206). There is no temp file, rename or sync. The repo's own write_atomic doc (utils/fs.rs:11-15) names this exact risk, but only the Rust writers use it (vault.rs:370, 683, 899). On failure the buffer stays dirty and is retried (:191-193), so the in-memory copy survives while the app runs. The on-disk note, however, is already truncated or partial, and quitting after the 'lose unsaved changes' prompt leaves it that way. The trigger (ENOSPC, EIO on an external or network volume, power loss or crash mid-write) is rare, but the loss is the whole note. I did not verify APFS crash ordering against a primary source.
verification.repro: Manual: put a vault on a nearly full small disk image (hdiutil create -size 2m), fill it to about 1 KB free, edit a 40 KB note to grow it, and wait for autosave. The 'Failed to save file.' toast appears and `wc -c` on the note shows a size below the old one. Code-level: read commands.rs:1169-1206.
verification.fix_hint: Route the editor save through a Rust command that uses write_atomic (temp file in the same directory, sync_all, rename, optionally fsync the directory), preserving mode. Apply the same to the trash manifest and the other plain writeTextFile note writers (link-updater, type-definitions, deep-link).

findings.title: Editing one property (Properties panel or meta-bind input) silently rewrites the others: nested maps and comments dropped, numbers reformatted (01234 -> 1234, 1.10 -> 1.1, 0x1F -> 31)
findings.scenario: Take a note imported from Obsidian with this frontmatter: `zip: 01234`, `version: 1.10`, `# reviewed by legal`, `metadata:` / `  author: Ann`, `status: draft`. The user changes `status` in the Properties panel, or clicks a meta-bind toggle in the body. The block is rebuilt from the parsed JS values and becomes `zip: 1234`, `version: 1.1`, `status: ...`. The comment and the whole `metadata` mapping are deleted, and a list of maps becomes JSON strings. 500 ms later the frontmatter autosave writes it. The Properties panel path is not undoable, because the external sync dispatch uses addToHistory(false). File History cannot restore it either: snapshots are taken only AFTER an in-app save, with the new content, so a note authored outside the app has no snapshot of its original bytes.
findings.evidence:
commitChanges refuses only `isFrontmatterUnparseable` (properties.service.ts:82) and dispatchMetaBindUpdate does the same (widgets.ts:756). Neither calls detectLossyFrontmatter. The parse drops nested mappings with `continue` (properties.logic.ts:291-300). convertToProperty keeps numbers as JS numbers (188-190), so the source spelling is lost, and serializeProperties rebuilds a fresh `new Document({})` with `doc.set(p.key, p.value)` (572-584). I checked this against node_modules/yaml@2.9.1 with a read-only `node -e`: `zip: 01234
version: 1.10
ratio: 1.0
hex: 0x1F
exp: 1e3` serializes back to `zip: 1234 / version: 1.1 / ratio: 1 / hex: 31 / exp: 1000`, and the core int resolver is `parseInt(str, 10)` for `/^[-+]?[0-9]+$/` (yaml/dist/schema/core/int.js). Even the guarded path (updateNoteFrontmatter -> detectLossyFrontmatter) flags only integers past MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (properties.logic.ts:427-433), so leading-zero ints and trailing-zero floats get through there as well. ADR-0029 (lines 82, 103, 107) says these panel and meta-bind writers 'keep the drop behaviour' for comments and nested keys, so that part is documented debt. The number reformat is not in ADR-0029's list of canonical coercions (null to "", list items to strings, alias keys, quote style).

verification.reasoning: The nested-map and comment drop on panel and meta-bind edits is F97's root cause (commitChanges at properties.service.ts:82 and widgets.ts:756 guard only unparseable). The number reformat (01234->1234, 1.10->1.1, 0x1F->31) is F53, which I reproduced with yaml 2.9.1. Two extra points hold. The panel path uses addToHistory(false) (MarkdownEditor.svelte:331), and file-history snapshots only run after a save (file-history.service.ts:190-196), so the original bytes of a note authored outside the app cannot be recovered.
verification.repro: See F97 and F53.
verification.fix_hint: See F97 and F53. The in-place Document edit fixes both.

findings.title: Non-UTF-8 notes (and binary files with unrecognized extensions) are decoded lossily and permanently corrupted on the first edit
findings.scenario: A vault holds `Old notes.md` saved as Windows-1252/Latin-1 (common in Evernote, old Windows or legacy exports), e.g. 'café', 'São Paulo'. The Rust index silently skips the file (debug log only), so nothing warns the user. The user opens it from the file tree: every non-ASCII byte shows as U+FFFD. The user fixes a typo or adds a line, and autosave writes UTF-8 with EF BF BD in place of every accented byte. The original characters cannot be recovered. The same happens to a binary file whose extension is not in BINARY_FILE_EXTENSIONS: an accidental keystroke saves it as replacement-character text.
findings.evidence: plugin-fs readTextFile is `new TextDecoder(options?.encoding ?? 'utf-8').decode(bytes)` (index.js:498). The default `fatal: false` replaces invalid sequences with U+FFFD and never throws. openFileInEditor's only guard is the extension check `isBinaryFile(filePath)` (editor.service.ts:108; fs.logic.ts:95-97 is an extension Set lookup). No code checks for U+FFFD (grep for FFFD/fatal/TextDecoder in src/lib and src-tauri/src returned nothing). Rust scans use `fs::read_to_string` and on error just `skipped += 1` with a debug_log (vault.rs:182-197, 1320-1331), so the user is never told the file is not valid UTF-8. Save re-encodes with TextEncoder (index.js:781-782). Mitigation: read_files_batch and toggle_task_status fail on non-UTF-8 instead of corrupting (files.rs:63, vault.rs:669).

verification.reasoning: readTextFile decodes with new TextDecoder(encoding ?? 'utf-8') and default fatal:false (plugin-fs dist-js/index.js:498), so invalid bytes become U+FFFD without throwing. openFileInEditor guards only on extension (editor.service.ts:108). grep finds no FFFD, fatal or ignoreBOM check in src/lib. The first edit saves TextEncoder-encoded replacement characters (index.js:781-782), and that cannot be undone. On a closed Latin-1 note it gets worse: a Favorite or icon click reads through readTextFile (frontmatter-write.service.ts:117) and writes it back with no edit needed. The Rust scan only skips the file with a debug log (vault.rs:180-197), so the user gets no warning. Reachability depends on legacy-encoded files being in the vault.
verification.repro: Manual: write bytes 'caf\xE9' to a .md file in the vault, open it, type one character and wait 2 s. The file now contains EF BF BD. Or right-click the closed file, choose Favorite, and check the bytes.
verification.fix_hint: Decode note reads with TextDecoder('utf-8',{fatal:true}) (or read bytes and validate). On failure, open read-only with a toast, and refuse frontmatter writes.

findings.title: Watcher reload overwrites keystrokes typed while the disk read is in flight (dirty state not re-checked after the await)
findings.scenario: An open, clean note is modified externally (git pull, iCloud or Obsidian Sync from a phone). About 500 ms later the watcher calls reloadExternallyChangedTabs. The tab passes the eligibility filter because it is clean, and readTextFile starts. The user, already typing in that note, enters characters before the read resolves. The re-check after the await compares disk only against savedContent, not against tab.content. syncExternalContentToEditor(..., markSaved=true) then replaces the doc and marks the tab clean, discarding those keystrokes. The doc replace uses addToHistory(false). The window is the IPC read time, or the slowest file's read when several paths change at once (Promise.allSettled).
findings.evidence: Before the await: `if (!tab || isVirtualTab(tab) || isTabDirty(tab)) continue;` (editor.service.ts:380). After the await, the comment says 'Re-check tab state — it may have changed during parallel reads', but the code checks only `if (!tab || diskContent === tab.savedContent) continue;` (398) and then `syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, diskContent, true, 'none')` (401). Keystrokes update tab.content synchronously via onContentChange -> editorStore.updateContent (editor.service.ts:224-226), so a dirty tab at line 398 is never detected. The fix is to repeat `isTabDirty(tab)` at line 398.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause, editor.service.ts:380 vs 398.
verification.repro: See F3.
verification.fix_hint: See F3.

findings.title: Task toggle is addressed by bare line number, so a stale Tasks list flips the wrong task
findings.scenario: The user types in note A, inserting a line above its tasks, then switches to the Tasks tab within 2 s. The tab mounts and fetches tasks with the old line numbers, since disk and index do not have the edit yet. The background autosave then fires: A on disk gains a line and the index updates, but the Tasks list refresh rides the throttled vault-index-updated bump (2 s, up to 10 s during a burst). Clicking 'Buy milk' during that window sends line N, which now holds a different task. Rust flips whichever checkbox is on line N and writes it, so the wrong task is silently checked. The same happens when an external sync inserts or removes lines while the Tasks tab is open.
findings.evidence: The IPC carries only `{ path, lineNumber }` (tasks.service.ts:102-105). toggle_task_status_inner re-reads disk and flips the TASK_RE checkbox on `lines[line_number - 1]` with no check of the expected task text or status (parsing.rs:1877-1906). The list refetches only on vaultIndexVersion (TasksView.svelte:76-81) or after its own toggle (tasks.service.ts:115), and the version bump is throttled (REFRESH_DELAY_MS 2000 / REFRESH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS 10000, tauri-listeners.service.ts:84-88). Passing the expected line text and refusing on mismatch would close this.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F79. Its scenario matches variant B there (switch to Tasks before the save, then the throttled refresh).
verification.repro: See F79.
verification.fix_hint: See F79.

findings.title: Line endings and BOM are normalized on the first keystroke (CRLF -> LF for the whole file, BOM dropped); Rust toggle reintroduces the BOM into the tab
findings.scenario: A CRLF note from Windows or git (core.autocrlf) is opened and one character is typed: the save rewrites every line ending to LF, so the whole file shows as changed in git or sync. A Properties panel edit on a CRLF note writes an LF frontmatter over a CRLF body (mixed endings). A UTF-8-BOM note loses its BOM on the first save. If a task in a BOM note is toggled from the Tasks tab before any in-app save, Rust returns content that starts with U+FEFF, and that string becomes the tab content. TS `^---` frontmatter detection then fails, the Properties panel shows no properties, and adding one prepends a second frontmatter block. Text content is preserved in all of these cases. Only bytes the user did not edit change.
findings.evidence:
CM splits docs with DefaultSplit `/
?|
/` and `sliceString(..., lineSep = "
")`. No EditorState.lineSeparator is configured anywhere (grep found none in src/lib). onDocChanged sends `update.state.doc.toString()` to onContentChange (editor-extensions.ts:188), which becomes the saved content. readTextFile's TextDecoder defaults to ignoreBOM=false, which strips the BOM. Rust `read_to_string` keeps it, and toggle returns `updated_content` with it (vault.rs:669-689). rebuildContent hardcodes `---
${yaml}
---
` (properties.logic.ts:621), and FRONTMATTER_REGEX is anchored at `^---` (37).

verification.reasoning: No EditorState.lineSeparator is configured (grep src/lib returns nothing), so CodeMirror's doc.toString() joins lines with \n and the first keystroke saves the whole file as LF. The CRLF part on frontmatter writes duplicates F59, and the BOM strip duplicates F60. The distinct part holds: Rust toggle_task_status_inner reads with read_to_string, which keeps the BOM, and returns updated_content (vault.rs:669-689). tasks.service.ts:114 then puts that content into the tab, so the tab starts with U+FEFF, `^---` no longer matches (properties.logic.ts:37), the panel shows no properties, and adding one prepends a second block. No text is lost.
