vitest: rebuildContent([{key:'a',value:'x',type:'text'}], extractBody('﻿---
t: 1
---
b')) yields a second frontmatter block ahead of the original.
verification.fix_hint: Strip a leading U+FEFF before frontmatter detection, or set lineSeparator and BOM handling consistently across TS and Rust.

findings.title: write_atomic swaps the inode: resets the note's creation time, drops mode/xattrs/Finder tags, does not fsync, and leaves a stray temp file when the write fails
findings.scenario: The user toggles a task from the Tasks tab, or renames a type (propagate_type_rename). Every touched note is replaced by a new file, so its birthtime becomes 'now'. Collections, QueryJS `file.ctime` and note-list 'created' sorting then show the note as just created. A 0600 private note becomes 0644 (umask default), Finder tags and other xattrs disappear, and hard links are split. If the temp write itself fails (disk full), `note.md.tmp-<pid>-<n>` is left in the vault folder. With no sync_all before the rename, a power loss can still lose the new content.
findings.evidence: fs.rs:26-27 writes to `{path}.tmp-{pid}-{seq}` with `std::fs::write`, which creates a new file with default permissions and no copied metadata. On error the `?` returns without removing the temp file; only the rename failure branch cleans up (28-31). There is no File::sync_all. read_file_metadata takes `created()` from the new inode (vault.rs:242-247) into NoteRecord.ctime (789). Mitigations that hold: symlinked notes cannot reach this path, because every walker skips symlinks (fs.rs:157-159), so the index never holds a symlink path. The read-only check (fs.rs:20-24) keeps write-protected notes protected. create_note's exists()-then-rename TOCTOU (vault.rs:896-899) can only race an external process, since sync Tauri commands run serialized on the main thread (from memory of Tauri docs, not verified here).

verification.reasoning: write_atomic creates the temp file with std::fs::write, which uses default mode and copies no xattrs (utils/fs.rs:26-27), and renames it over the note (:28), so the note gets a new inode. read_file_metadata then takes created() from the new inode (vault.rs:244-249), so ctime or birthtime resets on task toggles (vault.rs:683) and type renames (vault.rs:370). Mode, xattrs and Finder tags are dropped. Note bytes are correct. The fsync and temp-leftover parts are covered separately in F77 and F82.
verification.repro: Rust test: create a file, chmod 0600, set an xattr, call write_atomic, and assert the mode is no longer 0600 and the xattr is gone. Compare created() before and after.
verification.fix_hint: Copy permissions (and optionally xattrs via the xattr crate) from the original onto the temp before rename; or for in-vault edits keep birthtime via setattrlist on macOS.

findings.title: Cmd+Q, Dock Quit and logout skip the save-on-close handler, so pending and failed-save edits are lost
findings.scenario: 1) Type a paragraph in any note and press Cmd+Q within 2 s (500 ms for a property or frontmatter edit), before the debounced autosave fires. The app exits at once. On relaunch the paragraph is gone from disk. 2) Worse: a tab whose save keeps failing (parent folder renamed in Finder, file locked, disk full) shows 'Failed to save file.' and retries every 5 s. Cmd+Q quits with no 'Close anyway and lose unsaved changes?' prompt, and all of that tab's unsaved work is lost. The same applies to Quit from the Dock menu and to macOS logout/shutdown, which also send terminate:. The handler's doc comment says it exists 'preventing data loss on quit', but it only runs on a window close request.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:195 builds the app menu with `.quit()`. muda maps PredefinedMenuItemType::Quit to `sel!(terminate:)` (macos/mod.rs:944) with the Cmd+Q accelerator (predefined.rs:669). tao 0.37.2 registers only `applicationWillTerminate:` on its app delegate (app_delegate.rs:61-63). There is no `applicationShouldTerminate:`, so termination cannot be deferred. That callback runs AppState::exit() (app_state.rs:271-281), which sends Event::LoopDestroyed, and tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.3 turns that into RunEvent::Exit (lib.rs:4131-4133). Nothing dispatches WindowEvent::CloseRequested, and lib.rs:353 `.run(tauri::generate_context!())` has no RunEvent handler. So the JS `getCurrentWindow().onCloseRequested` (tauri-listeners.service.ts:53) never runs. Its saveAllDirtyTabs + prompt (:55-62) is skipped, and so are drainEventCalendarWrites and flushSettingsPersistence. Edits sit in memory only (editor.store tab.content) until the 2000/500 ms debounce (editor.service.ts:196-200). The same gap exists for UpdateSection.svelte:208-210 `relaunch()` (no save first). It also exists for a WebContent process crash, where tauri-runtime-wry lib.rs:5053-5064 reloads the webview by default and no beforeunload exists in src/. Recovery net: file history snapshots only content that was written (file-history.service.ts:190-196 runs after a successful save), so unsaved buffers have no snapshot and there is no crash journal. This settles open lead L1 in .scratch/file-io-audit/raw/scout-lifecycle.md:167-172 against the pinned crate versions (Cargo.lock: tao 0.37.2, muda 0.20.0, tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.3, tauri 2.12.5). Not run on a device.

verification.reasoning: I tried to find anything that intercepts the quit and found nothing. lib.rs:195 adds the predefined `.quit()`. muda-0.20.0 macos/mod.rs:944 maps Quit to `sel!(terminate:)`, and predefined.rs:669 binds it to Cmd+Q. tao-0.37.2 app_delegate.rs:61-63 registers only `applicationWillTerminate:`, and grep finds no `applicationShouldTerminate` in tao, tauri-runtime-wry, tauri or muda, so termination cannot be deferred. app_delegate.rs:130-133 calls AppState::exit(), app_state.rs:271-275 sends LoopDestroyed, and tauri-runtime-wry lib.rs:4131-4133 turns that into RunEvent::Exit. No WindowEvent::CloseRequested is dispatched on this path. lib.rs:353 `.run(tauri::generate_context!())` has no RunEvent callback, and the only on_window_event (lib.rs:94-95) belongs to the quick-capture composer. On the JS side the only save-on-exit path is `getCurrentWindow().onCloseRequested` (tauri-listeners.service.ts:53-71). The other save triggers are the debounced timers (editor.service.ts:196-200, trailing-only per debounce.ts:9-17) and the close handler. No blur, visibilitychange or beforeunload handler saves tabs (grep). UpdateSection.svelte:208-210 calls relaunch() without saving first. Result: every Cmd+Q, Dock Quit or logout within 2 s of the last keystroke (500 ms after a frontmatter edit) loses the text typed since the last pause. Tabs stuck in a failed-save retry are lost with no prompt. Not run on a device.
verification.repro: Manual check on the dev build: type a sentence in a note, press Cmd+Q within 1 s, relaunch, and confirm the sentence is missing from disk. A unit test cannot cover this, because the gap is the Rust/AppKit termination path. A possible Rust test is to assert that the app registers a RunEvent::ExitRequested handler.
verification.fix_hint: Intercept the quit in Rust. Use `.build(ctx)` plus `.run(|app, event| ...)` and, on RunEvent::ExitRequested, call `api.prevent_exit()` and emit an event to the webview. The webview runs the same save, prompt, drain and flush sequence as the close handler, then calls exit. Alternatively, replace the predefined Quit item with a custom Cmd+Q menu item that triggers the close-handler flow. Also call saveAllDirtyTabs and flushSettingsPersistence before relaunch() in UpdateSection.

findings.title: Deep-link daily/append/prepend wipes unsaved keystrokes of an open note (dirty buffer replaced by disk + appended text)
findings.scenario: Today's daily note is open (auto-opened and pinned) and the user is typing in it. Within the 2 s autosave window (or at any time if a save of that note failed earlier), a Shortcut, Raycast or Alfred action fires `kokobrain://daily?vault=Work&append=true&clipboard=true`, or `kokobrain://new?vault=Work&name=<open note>&append=true&content=...`. The handler reads the OLD bytes from disk, appends, writes them, and replaces the tab's content and savedContent with that string. The typed text disappears from the editor and is never written. The pending autosave then finds a clean tab and does nothing.
findings.evidence: executeDailyAction: `await openOrCreateDailyNote()` (:37) makes the existing tab active. It then runs `const existing = await readTextFile(filePath)` (:54), `newContent = existing + '\n' + content` (:56-58), `writeTextFile` (:61) and `syncExternalContentToEditor(filePath, newContent, true, 'none')` (:63). With markSaved=true, syncExternalContentToEditor (editor.service.ts:78-79) calls updateTabContentByPath, which sets both `tab.content` and `tab.savedContent` (editor.store.svelte.ts:130-136). That discards the dirty buffer and marks the tab clean. Because the tab is active it also bumps externalContentSignal, and MarkdownEditor replaces the CM doc. schedule 'none' arms nothing (editor.service.ts:213-221), and saveDirtyTabs filters on isTabDirty (:183-186), so nothing recovers the text. The same code runs in the new+append branch (deep-link.service.ts:266-278) and the new+prepend branch (:250-262). The race-audit test sets up a tab with content 'dirty editor content' / savedContent 'saved content on disk' and asserts the sync with markSaved=true (race-audit.test.ts:133-160), so the test suite requires the loss. Recovery net: none, because the lost text was never saved, so no snapshot exists.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F7.
verification.repro: See F7.
verification.fix_hint: See F7.

findings.title: Silent `new` deep link overwrites an existing note (to zero bytes when content is empty) with no exists() check
findings.scenario: The user has `Journal.md`. A Shortcut or a clicked link runs `kokobrain://new?vault=Work&name=Journal&silent=true` (no append/prepend/overwrite). The intent is 'create a note if missing'. With no content param (or clipboard=true and an empty or non-text clipboard), `resolveContent` returns ''. writeTextFile truncates Journal.md to 0 bytes. With content, the whole note is replaced by that text. No toast, no prompt. If Journal.md is open and dirty, its buffer is not synced, and the next autosave writes the old buffer back over the URL write (silent create never calls syncExternalContentToEditor).
findings.evidence: deep-link.service.ts:308-315: `if (action.silent) { mkdir(parent); markRecentSave; await writeTextFile(fullPath, content); notifyAfterSave(...) }`. There is no `exists()` call, unlike the visible branch at :316-322, which goes through openOrCreateNote, and `create_note` there refuses an existing path (note-creator.service.ts:86-103). The type doc says `overwrite` means 'overwrite the file entirely even if it already exists' (deep-link.types.ts:35-36), which implies the default should not overwrite. resolveFilePath only appends .md and checks traversal (path.ts:33-53). Recovery net: notifyAfterSave snapshots the NEW content. The overwritten version exists in history only if the app saved it within retention (7 days by default, settings.store.svelte.ts:94-97). cleanup_history drops every snapshot older than retention+30 days, including the latest per file (history.rs:146-151), so an older, untouched note has no recoverable copy. (Also reported by scout-deep-link L1; this audit re-read and confirmed the code path.)

verification.reasoning: Same root cause and code path (deep-link.service.ts:308-315). The history-retention detail adds nothing to the fix.
verification.repro: See F126.
verification.fix_hint: See F126.

findings.title: File-history Restore writes the snapshot into whatever tab is active, not the file the dialog was opened for
findings.scenario: Open File History for note P (Cmd+Shift+H). While the dialog is open, the active tab changes to Q. Triggers: the user presses Cmd+Shift+] (next-tab binding, a document-level keydown listener with no dialog guard); a `kokobrain://open?file=Q` deep link arrives; or the window regains focus after midnight and refreshDailyNoteIfDateChanged opens today's daily note. The user picks a snapshot of P and confirms Restore. P's old content is dispatched into the CodeMirror view now showing Q, and saveCurrentFile writes it to Q.md. Q's real content on disk is replaced by P's snapshot, and P is not restored. The dialog closes as if it worked.
findings.evidence: restoreSnapshot reads `fileHistoryStore.filePath` (:86) only for the early return. It dispatches into `editorStore.editorView` (:90-95), the view of the ACTIVE tab, and calls `saveCurrentFile()` (:99), which saves `editorStore.activeTab` (editor.service.ts:151-155). Nothing checks that activeTabPath === fileHistoryStore.filePath. registerKeybinding attaches to `document` and does not skip dialogs (keybindings.ts:30-47; only the '/' binding checks `[role="dialog"]`, global-keybindings.ts:44). executeAction 'open' calls openFileInEditor, which sets the active index (deep-link.service.ts:178-184, editor.service.ts:114-117). The dispatch goes through onDocChanged into updateContent(active tab). A related silent failure: if the active tab is canvas, kanban or collection, editorView is null, nothing is dispatched or saved, and the dialog still resets as if restore succeeded. Not verified at runtime that bits-ui Dialog lets the Cmd+Shift+] keydown bubble; its dialog.svelte.js content handlers seen do not stopPropagation. The deep-link and focus triggers do not depend on that.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F67. It adds deep-link and daily-note triggers that switch the active tab without a keystroke, which strengthens reachability.
verification.repro: See F67.
verification.fix_hint: See F67.

findings.title: Deep-link vault switch silently discards tabs whose save failed (known Issue 34 decision, but externally triggered)
findings.scenario: A tab cannot be saved (its folder was renamed in Finder, the file is locked, or the disk is full), and the 'Failed to save file.' toast repeats every 5 s. An external tool opens `kokobrain://open?vault=OtherVault`. switchVault saves, the save fails, the switch goes ahead anyway, initializeVault retries, fails again, and teardownVault -> resetEditor drops the tab. The unsaved content is gone with no prompt, while the window-close path asks before discarding. With a vault open, a deep link is the only way to switch (the recent-vaults page renders only when no vault is open), so this loss is always triggered from outside the app.
findings.evidence: vault.service.ts:19 `await saveAllDirtyTabs();` ignores the returned failed-path array (editor.service.ts:246). The initializeVault safety net (:180) also ignores it, then calls teardownVault (:188), which calls resetEditor() (:622) -> editorStore.reset() `tabs = []` (editor.store.svelte.ts:165-167). The comment at app-lifecycle.service.ts:172-178 confirms 'switchVault opens the new vault anyway'. The close handler prompts in the same situation (tauri-listeners.service.ts:55-62). Known: Issue 34 left block-vs-proceed to the owner (scout-lifecycle L3). The new point here is that only an external URL can trigger it.

verification.reasoning: Same root cause as F151. Its reachability point is correct: AppShell.svelte:160-161 renders the picker and recent page only when no vault is open, and vaultStore.close() (vault.store.svelte.ts:89) has no callers. So with a vault open, an external deep link is the only trigger.
verification.repro: See F151.
verification.fix_hint: See F151.

findings.title: open_vault_db failure leaves the session with no file-history snapshots and no external-change reload, and skips teardown on the next switch
findings.scenario: The vault's SQLite DB fails to open (locked by a second instance, corrupt file). The toast says 'Some features may not work', but the editor is fully usable. For the whole session: (a) no snapshots are taken, because the history observer is registered after the early return, so the recovery net is silently off; (b) the watcher listener is never started, so a note changed by sync or git while open in a clean tab is never reloaded, and the next keystroke saves the stale buffer plus the edit over the newer disk content. On a later deep-link switch, `if (unsubscribeFileChange)` is false, so the previous vault's tabs are never reset and stay open in the new vault.
findings.evidence: Step 2 `catch { ...toast...; return; }` (:225-229) runs before registerFileHistoryHook (:264-266), before onFileChange/startWatching (:489-497), and before unsubscribeFileChange is assigned (:489). The teardown at :170-189 is gated on unsubscribeFileChange. reloadExternallyChangedTabs is only reached from runWatcherBatch (:480-487). A failed startWatching (:495-497) is only logged and has the same effect on point (b).

verification.reasoning: Partly confirmed. The open_vault_db catch returns at app-lifecycle.service.ts:237. That is before the history hook (:266-268), loadDirectoryTree (:315), the watcher (:494-499) and the unsubscribeFileChange assignment (:494). On the next switch, the gate at :172 is false, so teardownVault and resetEditor do not run, and nothing at the top of initializeVault (:133-168) resets the editor. The claim that 'the editor is fully usable' is wrong. Step 4 never runs, so the file tree is empty. There is no tab session restore (grep), and autoOpenDailyNote (step 9) is never reached. A note can only be opened by a same-vault deep link or a create path. That makes the stale-overwrite-without-watcher case, and tabs carrying into the next vault, hard to reach. Failure triggers are an uncreatable .kokobrain (db/mod.rs:36-42) or a bad DB. When tabs carry over, nothing is lost; they just stay open.
verification.repro: Mock call('open_vault_db') to reject. initializeVault(A), open a tab via openOrCreateNote, then initializeVault(B). Assert that editorStore.tabs still holds A's tab and that registerFileHistoryHook was not called.
verification.fix_hint: On DB failure, keep going without the DB-backed features instead of returning. At minimum, run steps 4 and 7 and set the teardown gate, or make the teardown gate independent of unsubscribeFileChange.

gaps: QueryJS auto-run executes JavaScript taken from note content in the main webview, with full Tauri IPC and plugin-fs write/remove rights over the vault scope. Default policy is 'first-open' (src/lib/core/settings/settings.store.svelte.ts:136), the widget runs it on the first toDOM (src/lib/plugins/queryjs/queryjs-block-widget.ts:106-117), and the code is passed straight to new Function (src/lib/plugins/queryjs/kb-api.ts:360, :469). Note text from outside the app reaches it: a kokobrain://new URL's content becomes the note body and the note is opened (src/lib/features/deep-link/deep-link.service.ts:317-321), as does a synced or shared vault. Any web page can therefore run code that rewrites or deletes notes. A `while(true)` block also freezes the main thread, so the autosave timers never fire and dirty buffers are stuck. No mapper or hunter traced queryjs as a writer or a freeze source.

Deep-link `new` with overwrite=true replaces an existing note with no confirmation and no exists or dirty check (src/lib/features/deep-link/deep-link.service.ts:291-305). It then calls syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true), which also throws away an open tab's unsaved buffer. Any URL can wipe any note in the vault. F126 (silent new) and F7 (append/prepend) cover only the neighbouring branches.

The Properties panel commit (src/lib/features/properties/properties.service.ts:78-98) guards only with isFrontmatterUnparseable and then calls rebuildContent from Property[]. So every ordinary panel edit drops nested maps, comments and duplicate keys, and only the meta-bind writer (F97) was reported for this. Second path: skipNextParseFor is armed at :89 and consumed only when the PropertiesView 300 ms timer fires (PropertiesView.svelte:100-114, properties.service.ts:33-37). A no-op commit (newContent === content) leaves the store unchanged, so the effect never reruns and the flag stays armed. The panel then skips the parse of the user's next YAML edit in the editor, and the next panel change rebuilds the frontmatter from stale properties, erasing that edit.

Tabs are identified by exact path string (findTabIndex, src/lib/core/editor/editor.logic.ts:39-41). APFS lookups ignore case and Unicode normalization, and nothing in src/lib or src-tauri/src calls normalize('NFC'/'NFD') (grep found none). Openers that build a path from user text can open a second tab on a file that is already open under its tree spelling: the wikilink createNote fallback (src/lib/app/editor-host.ts:85-105 -> note-creator.service.ts:86 exists() is true -> :128 openFileInEditor(filePath)) and deep-link open/new/daily. Two buffers on one file mean each autosave overwrites the other. Watcher reloads and recentSaves keys also miss the second spelling.

When a note open in a tab is deleted or renamed outside the app, nothing touches the tab. The watcher's delete branch only removes the note from the indexes (src/lib/app/lifecycle/watcher-handler.service.ts:105-109). reloadExternallyChangedTabs swallows the read failure (src/lib/core/editor/editor.service.ts:390-393). The next autosave or frontmatter write (writeTextFile, create defaults to true) recreates the file at the old path, so a git checkout, Finder rename or sync leaves a ghost copy. This appears in the earlier raw review (.scratch/file-io-audit/raw/review-external-change.md F5) but not in the surviving list. Only the calendar variant was carried.

There is no single-instance guard and no vault lock. src-tauri/Cargo.toml has no tauri-plugin-single-instance, and src-tauri/src has no lock file. Dev and release builds share the identifier com.diegorv.kokobrain (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:5). Two processes on one vault overwrite each other's dirty buffers (the watcher reload skips dirty tabs), and their whole-file rewrites of the trash manifest, folder-order.json and settings clobber each other.

Quick-capture screenshots are written to std::env::temp_dir() (src-tauri/src/quick_capture/commands.rs:123-141), and the note only links to them with a file:// URL (src/lib/features/deep-link/deep-link.logic.ts:272-275; the doc at src/lib/app/deep-link-actions.ts:96-101 admits there is no copy into the vault). macOS purges $TMPDIR on its own schedule, so the captured image is lost while the note still looks intact.

The recovery net records only bytes written after a change. File-history snapshots come from the after-save observer (file-history.service.ts:111-124, 190-196), so the version before the first lossy in-app rewrite is never kept: meta-bind (F97), kanban (F143), the properties panel, deep-link overwrite, table +row (F98-F100). Notes edited only outside the app have no history at all. toggle_task_status (src/lib/features/tasks/tasks.service.ts:100-115) and propagate_type_rename (src/lib/features/type-definitions/type-definitions.service.ts:226) never call notifyAfterSave, so those rewrites get no snapshot either.

parseCanvas returns an empty canvas on any JSON parse error and keeps only nodes and edges, dropping other top-level keys (src/lib/features/canvas/canvas.logic.ts:36-49). The next persist (CanvasInner.svelte persistChanges/persistWithoutHistory :101-112, the debounce at :208-226) serializes that state over the file. Example: leave invalid JSON in source mode, switch to the canvas view, add a node, and the whole canvas is replaced by `{nodes:[],edges:[]}` plus the new node.

The .collection and .view YAML writers round-trip through yaml parse() and stringify() of a plain object: updateCollectionYaml/addView and siblings (src/lib/features/collection/yaml-parser.ts:145-231, 243-324), updateViewIconYaml (src/lib/features/type-definitions/type-sidebar.logic.ts:357-379), and updateViewQuery/updateViewIcon (type-definitions.service.ts:284-310). Every toolbar sort, filter, column or icon change drops comments, expands anchors, changes quoting and rewrites number text in a user-authored vault file. The kanban finding F143 covers only .kanban files.

The bookmark migration runs at every vault open, before the scan, and rewrites the frontmatter of every bookmarked note through the closed-note branch of updateNoteFrontmatter (src/lib/features/properties/bookmark-migration.service.ts:64-91; app-lifecycle.service.ts:284-290). This applies F53, F54, F58, F59 and F60 to many notes with no user action. ensureFolderNote also writes the placeholder '---\n---\n' (src/lib/features/file-icons/file-icons.service.ts:93-104), so every folder-icon set triggers F123 (a second frontmatter block, with the original delimiters left in the body).

gap_findings.title: QueryJS blocks auto-run on first open with full Tauri IPC (fs remove/write on the whole vault). A deep link or capture can plant one, and nothing gates, sandboxes or times it out
gap_findings.scenario: A web page (or a Shortcut, Raycast snippet or shared note) fires kokobrain://new?vault=<name>&name=Inbox/x&content=hi%0A%60%60%60queryjs%0A<js>%0A%60%60%60. With clipboard=true the page can instead use clipboard text it set earlier. The user accepts the browser's 'Open KokoBrain?' prompt. The note is created and opened, live preview renders the block, the default 'first-open' policy runs it at once, and the script calls window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke('plugin:fs|remove', {path: <vault>, options:{recursive:true}}) or rewrites notes with plugin:fs|write_text_file. The vault content is deleted outside the Trash. The same block written by a Quick Capture of hijacked clipboard text runs the next time the capture note is opened. A block with a synchronous loop (while(true){}) freezes the webview instead. Pending autosaves in other tabs then never fire, and the user must force-quit and lose them. The first-open markers are in memory only (queryjs-session.store.svelte.ts:38, 111), so after a restart, opening the note freezes the app again.
gap_findings.evidence: settings.store.svelte.ts:136-137 makes autoRunQueries default to 'first-open'. queryjs-block-widget.ts:107-120: on a cache miss under 'first-open' with the file not yet marked, it calls markAutoRun and this.execute(container) with no user action. execute (191-197) calls runQueryjsBlock(api, this.jsContent), and kb-api.ts:469 runs new Function('kb','dv', `return (async () => { ${jsContent} })()`) in the main webview. kb.view() does the same with vault scripts (kb-api.ts:360). Grepping src/lib/plugins/queryjs for trust, timeout or Worker( finds no gate. The main webview carries window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke, the call @tauri-apps/api/core.js:341 itself uses. capabilities/default.json grants fs:allow-write-text-file (83-100), fs:allow-remove (138-153) and fs:allow-rename (155-170) on $HOME/kokobrain-vaults/** and $DOCUMENT/kokobrain-vaults/**. build.rs:22 calls tauri_build::build() with no AppManifest, so the custom commands in lib.rs:293-352 (toggle_task_status, rename_note, create_note...) are callable too. The CSP allows 'unsafe-eval' (tauri.conf.json:29). The injection path: deep-link.logic.ts:62-99 requires only `vault`, and `content`/`clipboard` are passed through. executeNewAction's non-silent default (deep-link.service.ts:315-320) calls openOrCreateNote({inlineTemplate: content}), which writes it (note-creator.service.ts:99-103) and then openFileInEditor (124). The attacker must know a vault name (matched case-insensitively against recent vaults, deep-link.service.ts:139-145), and the browser asks before it hands a custom scheme to an app. Those two limits keep severity at high, not critical. The only mitigation is the user setting autoRunQueries='manual'.

gap_findings.title: A Properties panel edit rewrites the whole frontmatter with no lossy-frontmatter guard: nested maps, comments, anchors and duplicate keys are deleted on the first keystroke, and Cmd+Z cannot bring them back
gap_findings.scenario: A note imported from Obsidian has frontmatter with `title: Trip`, a nested `location:` map (lat/lng), a comment line `# booking ref ABC123`, an anchor `base: &b {x: 1}` and `tags: [a]`. The user opens it and types one character into the 'title' field of the Properties panel. The block is rewritten to `title: Trip2` plus `tags: [a]`. `location` (a nested map the panel never shows), the comment and the anchor are gone, and with duplicate keys only the last one survives. The 500 ms frontmatter autosave writes this to disk. Cmd+Z in the editor does not restore it, and File History holds no earlier version unless the note had been saved in the app before.
gap_findings.evidence: PropertyField.svelte:122-126 binds oninput={handleValueChange}, which calls onUpdate on every keystroke (53-71). That reaches updateProperty, then commitChanges (properties.service.ts:76-97), whose only refusal is isFrontmatterUnparseable (81). It then runs rebuildContent(updated, extractBody(content)) and syncExternalContentToEditor(activePath, newContent, false, 'frontmatter'). In the parse step, computeAndCache uses parseDocument(raw, {uniqueKeys:false}), so duplicate keys are last-wins (262). Nested mappings are skipped with `continue` (291-300). serializeProperties (572-588) builds a new Document, so comments and anchors are lost. Two other writers guard against this: frontmatter-write.service.ts:121-122 calls detectLossyFrontmatter(base) and throws, and so do auto-move (auto-move.service.ts:201) and event-calendar (event-calendar.service.ts:937, 997). The panel does not, and grepping PropertiesView.svelte and PropertyField.svelte finds no lossy, readonly or disabled state. The external sync is dispatched with Transaction.addToHistory.of(false) (MarkdownEditor.svelte:332), so undo does not cover it. This is a different writer from the known meta-bind and closed-note findings.

gap_findings.title: A case (or NFC/NFD) variant of a note's path opens a second editable tab on the same file. That tab never receives watcher reloads, and its next autosave overwrites the other tab's saved edits
gap_findings.scenario: The vault has the folder 'Journal/' (made in Finder, or by Obsidian). The Periodic Notes base folder is set to 'journal'. The user clicks the Daily button: openOrCreateNote checks exists('<vault>/journal/2026-11-02.md'), which is true on the default case-insensitive APFS volume, and opens tab A under that lowercase path. Later the user opens the same note from the file tree, a backlink or [[2026-11-02]], which give the on-disk path '<vault>/Journal/2026-11-02.md', and gets tab B. They type in B, and B autosaves. They switch back to A with the Daily button (it always activates A). A still holds the old text. They type one character, and A's autosave writes its whole stale buffer, erasing what was typed in B. If B is clean, the watcher then reloads it with A's bytes, so the text is gone from both tabs. A user-typed deep link (kokobrain://open?vault=v&file=inbox/todo for Inbox/Todo.md) opens the same kind of duplicate tab. So may an NFC-typed [[Cafe-acute]] pointing at an NFD-named file: the resolver finds nothing, and the create path's exists() returns true, if APFS is normalization-insensitive.
gap_findings.evidence: findTabIndex compares with === (editor.logic.ts:39-41), and openFileInEditor relies on it alone before readTextFile (editor.service.ts:114-124), with no canonicalization. buildPeriodicNotePath joins settings.folder verbatim (periodic-notes.logic.ts:10-22). The folder Input stores raw input (PeriodicNotesSection.svelte:26-30 -> updatePeriodicNotes spread, settings.store.svelte.ts:189-197). resolveFilePath keeps the caller's case (path.ts:33-53). openOrCreateNote opens the existing file once exists() is true (note-creator.service.ts:86-88, 124). reloadExternallyChangedTabs matches tabs with t.path === filePath (editor.service.ts:378-381) against watcher paths (app-lifecycle.service.ts:481-488), so the variant tab never matches an event for the other spelling, and recentSaves are exact-string keys too (editor.hooks.ts:37-49). No String.prototype.normalize call exists in src/lib or src-tauri/src (grep), and resolveWikilink only lowercases (wikilink-resolution.logic.ts:14-19). The Rust index keys entries by the given path string (index.rs:198, 305), so the variant's saves also add a duplicate index entry. That APFS is case-insensitive by default and normalization-insensitive is from memory; I did not test it.

gap_findings.title: Quick Capture clipboard screenshots are stored only in the OS temp dir. The note never displays them (outside the asset scope), and macOS deletes them later, so the capture is lost
gap_findings.scenario: The user copies an image and presses the capture-clipboard shortcut. A Quick Capture note is written whose whole content is ![qc-shot-...png](file:///var/folders/.../T/qc-shot-<stamp>.png). Opening the note shows a broken image at once, because the temp dir is outside the asset-protocol scope. Days later macOS's temp cleanup removes the file. By then the clipboard has moved on, so the screenshot exists nowhere and the note is an empty link.
gap_findings.evidence: materialize_input turns Shot::Bytes into a temp file (commands.rs:104-113). write_shot_bytes_to_temp writes to std::env::temp_dir().join("qc-shot-...") (139-140). renderCaptureBody for 'shot' emits `![label](file://...)` with no copy into the vault (deep-link.logic.ts, shot case). The executeCaptureAction doc says shot/file get 'no copy into the vault ... durable attachments are a future change' (deep-link-actions.ts:96-100) and writes only the link (173). ImageWidget passes a file: URL to host.assetUrl, i.e. convertFileSrc (widgets.ts:143-162). The asset scope (tauri.conf.json:32-42) lists $DOCUMENT, $HOME/MyFiles, $HOME/kokobrain-vault, $DESKTOP, $PICTURE, $DOWNLOAD and the app cache, with no temp dir. The code shows the image living only in temp. That macOS removes old $TMPDIR files on its own is from memory; I did not check it.

gap_findings.title: File History never records a note's version before a write, and several writers take no snapshot at all, so the first lossy or destructive write of an externally authored note cannot be undone (deep-link overwrite is the sharpest case)
gap_findings.scenario: A note was last written outside the app (an imported Obsidian vault, a sync, vim). (1) The user edits a property in the panel (finding above), or a kanban/meta-bind write runs. Data is dropped, and File History lists only the post-write version. (2) kokobrain://new?vault=v&name=Projects/Plan&overwrite=true&content=x replaces the whole note with no prompt and no Trash copy. If Plan is open with unsaved edits, those edits are discarded too: markSaved=true sets both content and savedContent. File History has only 'x'. (3) A task toggle from the Tasks tab, a link rewrite on rename, or a type rename changes a note and leaves no snapshot of either version.
gap_findings.evidence: The only save_snapshot caller is saveSnapshotForFile (file-history.service.ts:117), reached only through the after-save observer registerFileHistoryHook (190-196), which snapshots the NEW content after a save. No writer snapshots before it writes. The deep-link overwrite branch (deep-link.service.ts:291-305) runs writeTextFile(fullPath, content), then syncExternalContentToEditor(fullPath, content, true, 'none'), which calls updateTabContentByPath for a dirty tab (editor.service.ts:78-79), then notifyAfterSave, which records only the new bytes. The parser takes overwrite as a plain boolean with no guard (deep-link.logic.ts:98). These writers never call notifyAfterSave: toggleTask (tasks.service.ts:100-115, which uses sync 'none' only), updateLinksAfterRename (link-updater.service.ts:38-52, which uses applyNoteChange, not the after-save observers), the renameType tab loop (type-definitions.service.ts:214-224), updateViewIcon/updateViewQuery (284-310), and Rust propagate_type_rename. The append, prepend and silent dirty-tab variants are already known; what this adds is the missing recovery coverage and the overwrite branch.

gap_findings.title: A canvas file with invalid JSON opens as an empty canvas with no error, and the first edit overwrites the file with only the new nodes
gap_findings.scenario: A .canvas file holds a JSON syntax error: git merge-conflict markers in a synced vault, a trailing comma from a hand edit, or a truncated write. The user opens it and sees an empty canvas with no warning. They double-click to add a text node, or paste. 300 ms later persistChanges serializes {"nodes":[<new>],"edges":[]}, the tab becomes dirty, and autosave replaces the file, so every original node and edge is lost. Top-level keys other than nodes and edges are dropped on any persist, even from a valid file.
gap_findings.evidence: parseCanvas returns createEmptyCanvas() on any JSON.parse failure, non-object root or missing arrays, and returns only {nodes, edges}, so other top-level keys are discarded (canvas.logic.ts:36-49). CanvasInner derives canvasData from it (71) and syncs the empty state into nodes/edges (84-97). Nothing in the canvas components reports invalid JSON (grep of the .svelte files for invalid or JSON.parse finds nothing). The next node change arms the 300 ms persist (206-224). That calls persistWithoutHistory -> flowToCanvas(..., canvasData) -> serializeCanvas -> onJsonChange (100-106), which writes over the original text. xyflow writes measured nodes back through bind:nodes (node_modules/@xyflow/svelte/dist/lib/store/index.js:39-75; CanvasInner.svelte:579-581). That may also trigger a persist on mount for a valid canvas, which would drop its extra top-level keys just by opening it. I did not verify that part by running.

gap_findings.title: A no-op Properties commit leaves skipNextParseFor armed, so the next editor burst is not parsed, and a later panel edit erases YAML typed in the editor
gap_findings.scenario: A note has `rating: 5`. The user types '5.0' in the panel's number field and stops. Number('5.0') is 5, so commitChanges builds content identical to the current content and arms the flag. They then type `status: draft` into the frontmatter in the editor (one typing burst). The panel's 300 ms re-parse consumes the stale flag and skips, so the store and panel still lack `status`. They then toggle a checkbox in the panel. commitChanges rebuilds the frontmatter from the stale store, and `status: draft` is removed and autosaved.
gap_findings.evidence: commitChanges sets skipNextParseFor = activePath (properties.service.ts:88) and calls updateTabContentOnly, which runs `tab.content = content` (editor.store.svelte.ts:142). In Svelte 5.57.2 the proxy set goes through internal_set, which does nothing when source.equals(value) (node_modules/svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/sources.js:189-190), and equals is === (equality.js:4-6). So with identical content the PropertiesView $effect (98-113) does not re-run and the flag survives. The next content change from the editor reruns the effect. syncPropertiesFromActiveTab returns false for the same path, and the timer's consumeSkipNextParse(path) returns true, skipping parseAndSetProperties. The next panel commit passes propertiesMatchActiveNote (sourcePath is unchanged) and rebuilds from the stale store. Any later editor burst re-parses and closes the window, so the loss needs this exact order.

gap_findings.title: The asset-protocol scope does not cover vaults under ~/kokobrain-vaults (plural), so local images in those vaults fail to render
gap_findings.scenario: The user keeps a vault at ~/kokobrain-vaults/brain, a root the fs capabilities explicitly support. Every ![[image.png]] or file:// embed in it resolves to an asset URL outside the asset scope and shows as broken. Vaults under ~/Documents/kokobrain-vaults work because $DOCUMENT/** is in scope.
gap_findings.evidence: The fs capabilities list $HOME/kokobrain-vaults/** (default.json:91-93 and the other fs blocks). The asset scope lists $HOME/kokobrain-vault/** and $HOME/kokobrain-vault/.kokobrain/** (singular, tauri.conf.json:37-38), with no $HOME/kokobrain-vaults entry. The image widget loads local files only through convertFileSrc / host.assetUrl (widgets.ts:143-162).
